extracted_data.name_full: Modified Behler-Parrinello-type Neural Network Potential with a System-Charge Input Node
extracted_data.brief_description: A Behler–Parrinello atom-centered neural-network potential extended by a global system-charge scalar (Q_sys) appended to each atomic network input to enable a single structural descriptor to represent multiple defect charge states; trained on DFT energies and forces and used to predict IFCs, phonon scattering rates and lattice thermal conductivity for pristine and defect-laden AlN.
extracted_data.material_systems: Single host: wurtzite AlN (pristine and defect-laden); multiple supercell sizes (32–128 atoms in training, validated on 192-atom 4x4x3 supercell).
extracted_data.defect_types: Native point vacancies and a few charged substitutional/interstitial types included in dataset generation; paper focuses on single point vacancies V_N^(1+), V_N^(3+), and V_Al^(3-). Complexes not modeled explicitly.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicit global scalar: system charge node Q_sys = c * q_sys / V (c=100); DFT data generated by manually changing electron count with a compensating jellium background charge; Q_sys is fed into atomic NN inputs (same scalar for all atoms) but does not explicitly contribute to computed forces.
extracted_data.target_properties: Lattice dynamical properties (2nd- and 3rd-order interatomic force constants), phonon bands, phonon-mode three-phonon anharmonic scattering rates, phonon-isotope scattering, phonon-defect scattering rates (via ab initio V and t-matrix computed from NNP/DFT IFCs), and lattice thermal conductivity κ (and its degradation vs defect concentration and charge state).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Atom-centered symmetry-function NNP with global charge scalar (Q_sys)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Local, atom-centered radial and angular symmetry functions (Behler–Parrinello SFs) computed inside a 7 Å cutoff per atom form the input feature vector; a single scalar Q_sys encoding the supercell net charge density is concatenated as an additional input node to each atomic feed-forward neural network, enabling the same structural coordinates to map to different atomic energies depending on charge state.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-supercell atom-centered decomposition (E_total = sum_i E_i); not a defect-centered subgraph. The representation is local per atom (within cutoff) and no explicit pristine-difference features are used (comparison to pristine done later in phonon-defect scattering via IFC differences).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Symmetry functions used: 8 radial and 24 angular functions per elemental combination (total 88 SF inputs within 7 Å). SFs include species-specific combinations (counts presented as 8×2 + 24×3 = 88 in the paper). Invariances: translational and rotationally invariant descriptors (standard Behler–Parrinello SFs). Species are handled via separate SFs per elemental combination (effectively one-hot by species in SF definitions).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Not a graph neural network; architecture is a per-atom feed-forward Behler–Parrinello network with two hidden layers. Reported NN architecture: [89-30-20-1] (89 inputs = 88 SFs + 1 Q_sys), tanh activations in hidden layers, linear output node returning atomic energy.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No use of pretrained/foundation potentials or pretrained embeddings reported. A preliminary 'rough' NNP (trained on initial DFT outputs) was used iteratively to run MD for dataset augmentation, but this is not a pretrained external model.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Training dataset: 18,558 structures (1,463,447 atoms total). Structures include pristine AlN and single-defect supercells (various defect species and charge states, sizes between 32 and 128 atoms) and MD-generated snapshots (NNP-driven MD then DFT-labelled). 10% randomly selected as test set. Dataset generation: DFT PW pseudopotential GGA calculations and iterative MD snapshot augmentation.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: NNP validated out-of-training-size by accurate relaxation, phonon bands, scattering rates and κ on a larger 4×4×3 (192-atom) supercell that was larger than training supercells. Quantitative agreement with DFT shown for energies/forces, phonon bands, scattering rates and thermal conductivities; no cross-host/chemistry transfer tests reported (only AlN).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: No explicit learning curves or few-shot experiments reported. Data-efficiency practices include PCA-based selection to maximize structural diversity and MD-driven snapshot augmentation using initially trained NNPs; no numerical sample-efficiency curves presented.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Random 10% test split (kept aside for monitoring overfitting). Training used loss weighting β=0.9 (weights energy vs forces). Optimization by I-BFGS with 50 random initial weight sets; best-performing initialization used. Stopping when training RMSE stationary and no test-overfitting observed. No charge-state or defect-type stratified split reported.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No representation ablation study (e.g., without Q_sys or with alternative descriptors) reported. Comparisons are primarily to DFT reference calculations (IFCs, phonon bands, scattering rates, κ). The paper references an earlier modified NNP development (Ref. [11]) but does not present ablation within this work.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Energy RMSE (training): 3.55 meV/atom; test: 3.48 meV/atom. Force RMSE (training): 69.16 meV/Å; test: 68.99 meV/Å. Thermal conductivity (average isotropic) pristine AlN at 293 K: NNP 256.93 W m^-1 K^-1 vs DFT 253.72 W m^-1 K^-1; with isotopes NNP 256.56 vs DFT 253.34 W m^-1 K^-1. Good agreement reported for phonon scattering rates (visual/qualitative comparison), phonon bands and IFCs; no MAE/RMSE reported for scattering rates or κ beyond the examples shown.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: NNP predicts total energies and forces → 2nd- and 3rd-order IFCs via finite-displacement (PHONOPY/thirdorder.py) → phonon frequencies, group velocities and anharmonic scattering → phonon-defect scattering via ab initio V (mass + force-constant differences) and t-matrix formalism → κ computed with AlmaBTE using relaxation time approximation and BTE integrals. Thus NNP is used as an ab initio surrogate to obtain IFCs for large supercells and multiple charge states to evaluate phonon-defect scattering rates and κ degradation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors claim that adding a global charge scalar Q_sys resolves the non-uniqueness problem where identical atomic coordinates correspond to different energies/IFCs across charge states, and therefore enables accurate multi-charge-state modeling. They also argue that the SF-based local representation captures structural distortions around defects (which strongly affect force-constant changes) and therefore captures phonon-defect scattering contributions beyond simple mass-difference models.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Q_sys does not explicitly contribute to atomic forces (stated in paper), which may be a limitation for charge-dependent forces; the highest-lying phonon branch shows a slight deviation from DFT (noted as negligible for transport). Thermal conductivity predictions are sensitive to choice of lattice constants and cutoff radii for 3rd-order IFCs. No explicit long-range electrostatics model or local charge-density descriptors beyond the global Q_sys scalar are included; no demonstration of generalization to other chemistries or defect complexes.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include an explicit global charge descriptor (Q_sys) when training ML potentials over multiple defect charge states; generate diverse training structures via MD snapshots seeded by a nascent potential and select structures by PCA on SFs to maximize coverage; use sufficiently large cutoff (here 7 Å for SFs) and test potential on supercell sizes larger than those used in training to validate transferability; include 2nd- and 3rd-order IFC convergence testing (3rd-order up to 10th NN used here) when targeting phonon transport.

extracted_data.name_full: Behler–Parrinello Radial and Angular Symmetry Functions
extracted_data.brief_description: Local invariant descriptors (radial and angular) used as per-atom inputs to the Behler–Parrinello neural networks; constructed per elemental combination and computed within a 7 Å cutoff to represent each atom's neighborhood for energy/force prediction.
extracted_data.material_systems: Used exclusively for AlN in this paper, with SFs defined per elemental pair/triplet combinations relevant to Al and N.
extracted_data.defect_types: Represent local environments around point defects (vacancies, substitutionals, interstitials) implicitly via atomic neighborhoods; used for V_N and V_Al cases in this work.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: SFs themselves are charge-blind; charge-awareness is provided separately via the Q_sys scalar concatenated to the SF inputs in the atomic NN.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used to predict per-atom energies and forces which are assembled into IFCs, phonon properties and κ (indirectly).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Behler–Parrinello symmetry functions (radial + angular)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: For each atom, a vector of radial and angular symmetry function values is computed summing contributions of neighbors within a 7 Å cutoff; species-specific SFs (separate channels per elemental combination) encode chemical identity and local geometry in an invariant manner.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Local atom-centered; by construction not explicitly defect-centered but defects appear as specific local neighborhoods with missing or displaced neighbors.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Cutoff radius: 7 Å; counts: 8 radial SFs and 24 angular SFs per elemental combination; invariance: translational/rotational/permutation invariance inherited from SF form; species handling: separate SFs per elemental pair/triplet combinations (effectively species-aware channels).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Not applicable (inputs to per-atom feed-forward NN).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Not used.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: SFs computed for 18,558 DFT-labelled structures (including MD-snapshots) spanning pristine and defect-laden supercells.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: SF space was analyzed with PCA to ensure structural features of relaxed defect-laden structures lie within training SF PCA coverage; this supports interpolation-based transfer to unseen relaxed defect structures and larger supercells.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: PCA selection used to control dataset size while preserving diversity; no explicit learning-curve reported.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: SFs used uniformly for all structures; PCA applied to SFs to guide selection of diverse structures for training.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No direct ablation (e.g., different SF sets or alternative descriptors) reported in this work.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Contributes to overall NNP errors: energy RMSE ~3.5 meV/atom; force RMSE ~69 meV/Å.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: SFs → atomic energies & forces → IFCs → phonon properties and κ; accurate local descriptors critical to capture defect-induced force-constant changes affecting phonon-defect scattering.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Local SFs capture structural distortions around defects that determine changes in force constants and therefore phonon-defect scattering, which can dominate over naive mass-difference models.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: As local descriptors with finite cutoff, SFs may miss longer-range electrostatic/charge redistribution effects; species handling is via separate SF channels but not via continuous charge density; completeness depends on SF choices and cutoff.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use sufficiently many radial/angular SFs and a cutoff large enough to capture defect-induced structural distortions relevant for IFC changes (they used 7 Å and 8 radial + 24 angular SFs per elemental combination here).

extracted_data.name_full: PCA-guided training-set selection with NNP-driven MD snapshot augmentation (iterative DFT labelling)
extracted_data.brief_description: A dataset construction workflow combining an initial DFT-labelled set, training of a rough NNP to run MD, extraction of MD snapshots, DFT labelling of snapshots, and principal-component-analysis (PCA) on SFs to select a maximally diverse final training set.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to AlN pristine and defect-laden supercells across several defect species and charge states during dataset generation.
extracted_data.defect_types: Used to collect diverse local environments around single point defects (vacancies and some substitutional/interstitial species) and pristine configurations.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: DFT snapshots generated for explicit charge states (electrons added/removed with compensating jellium); snapshots labelled per-charge-state and then included in PCA space (which is SF-based and thus charge-agnostic) while Q_sys retained in final feature vector.
extracted_data.target_properties: Dataset generation method for training the NNP to predict energies/forces and derived phonon properties.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: PCA on SF feature space combined with iterative NNP-MD data augmentation
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Compute symmetry-function vectors for structures, reduce dimensionality to PC1/PC2, and select structures to span the PCA space to maximize diversity; augment dataset with MD snapshots produced by an initial NNP to sample thermally accessible configurations, then label with DFT.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not defect-centered — selection based on global SF concatenation across atoms (local atomic features flattened to per-structure vectors) and then PCA to choose diverse structures covering different local environments (including defect neighborhoods).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: PCA applied to SFs built from per-atom SFs (number of SFs = 88 × N_atoms flattened to per-structure vector) then reduced to two principal components (PC1, PC2) for selection.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Not applicable.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: A roughly trained NNP (trained on initial DFT outputs) is used to run MD and propose new structures; this is an internal iterative augmentation, not pretraining from external datasets.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Final curated training dataset: 18,558 structures (~1.46M atoms). MD snapshot intervals: 5–30 steps sampled; PCA-based selection procedure (as in Refs. [19-21]) used to avoid redundancy.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: PCA coverage analysis showed that relaxed defect-laden structures (not used for training) lie within training PCA range, supporting interpolation ability and transfer to unseen relaxed defects. Also validated on larger supercell (192 atoms).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Workflow designed to limit the number of DFT calculations while ensuring diverse coverage; no quantitative sample-efficiency curves provided.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Structures selected to be well scattered in PC1-PC2 SF space; 10% of final dataset reserved as random test set. MD snapshots labelled with DFT used to expand training set iteratively.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No explicit comparison to uniform/random selection in this paper; the approach justified by prior literature (Refs. [19-21]).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Contributed to final NNP accuracy (energy RMSE ~3.5 meV/atom; force RMSE ~69 meV/Å); no independent metric reported for selection strategy itself.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Ensures training data include local environments relevant for defect-induced IFC changes so that NNP can produce accurate IFCs for phonon scattering and κ predictions.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: PCA selection over SF space ensures inclusion of diverse local atomic environments (including defect relaxations) so the NNP generalizes to relaxed defect structures and larger supercells.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: No quantitative ablation showing how much PCA/MD augmentation improves results vs naive sampling; selection was SF-based and therefore may miss charge-specific electronic-structure variations that are not fully encoded in SFs (mitigated here by Q_sys scalar).
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use iterative MD with an initial ML potential to propose candidate structures, then label with DFT and use PCA on invariant descriptors (SFs) to select a diverse set for training to cover defect neighborhood variability while minimizing DFT cost.

extracted_data.name_full: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network (ALIGNN) representation
extracted_data.brief_description: A crystal-graph-based representation that augments the atomic graph with a line graph to encode bond-angle (three-body) information in addition to bond-length (two-body) features, using radial basis function (RBF) embeddings for distances and angles and rich atomic feature vectors.
extracted_data.citation_title: Accelerating Defect Predictions in Semiconductors Using Graph Neural Networks
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to a large set of Group IV, III-V, and II-VI zinc-blende (ZB) semiconductors (34 unique AB binaries), also tested on CdSe_xTe_{1-x} alloys and some defect complexes in CdTe; used across many hosts (multi-host).
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies, self-interstitials, anti-site substitutions, substitutional and interstitial impurities/dopants, and some defect complexes (e.g., V_Cd+As_Te, V_Te+Cu_Cd); both single defects and complexes included in training/evaluation.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Handled by training separate ALIGNN models for each explicit integer charge state (q = +2, +1, 0, -1, -2) and for each chemical potential condition (A-rich, B-rich); target E^f predicted at E_F = 0 and CTLs obtained by constructing E^f vs E_F lines with slope = q. No explicit per-atom charge embedding or explicit long-range electrostatic field features are reported.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energy (E^f) for each charge state at E_F = 0; derived charge transition levels (CTLs) via E^f vs E_F construction; used also for structure/geometry optimization surrogate (minimizing predicted E^f). No predictions of migration barriers or phonon scattering/lattice thermal conductivity degradation are reported.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Full defective-supercell crystal graph with line-graph (bond-angle) features (ALIGNN)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Full periodic defective supercell is converted to a crystal graph with atoms as nodes and bonds (neighbors within cutoff) as edges; edge features are RBF-encoded bond distances; a line graph is constructed where nodes represent bonds and edges of the line graph represent bond pairs sharing an atom, enabling RBF-encoded angular (triplet) features; atomic features include multiple elemental properties; graph pooled to a global feature and passed to FCNN for E^f prediction.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full supercell (defective crystal) representation is used (not an explicit defect-centered subgraph nor a delta-to-pristine feature vector). The authors also compare/contrast predictions on pristine (unoptimized) defective structures vs fully optimized structures and use intermediate structures as training data.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Cutoff radius r_c reported (ALIGNN: r_c = 8 Å), neighbor count (used 12 nearest neighbors in reported best model); distance and angle features encoded via radial basis functions (RBF); triplet features t_ijk included for bond-angle RBF encoding; atomic/node features include electronegativity, group number, covalent radius, valence electrons, ionization energy, electron affinity, atomic block, atomic volume (species-specific continuous features rather than simple one-hot).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: ALIGNN (Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network) with both graph convolutional layers and line-graph convolutional layers; reported hyperparameters: 12 neighbors, r_c = 8 Å, 4 graph conv layers, 4 line graph layers, learning rate = 0.001, batch size = 16, AdamW optimizer, ~150 epochs. Uses edge (distance) and triplet (angle) features and global pooling followed by FCNN readout.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No use of pretrained GNN weights or foundation interatomic potentials is reported. MEGNET-style elemental embeddings are used in MEGNET runs (see other entity), but ALIGNN is trained from scratch on the DFT defect dataset in this work.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Training data are DFT (PBE) computed defect formation energies and geometries; datasets include: Dataset 1 (native defects in 34 ZB compounds; ~3k neutral IS, ~1.5–3k for charged states), Dataset 2 (impurities across hosts; ~14k neutral IS), Dataset 3 (CdSe_xTe_{1-x} alloys; a few hundred points), Dataset 4 (47 neutral defect-complex points in CdTe). Combined training set includes up to ~13–15k points for some q states (numbers reported per q in Table 1). Data are not 'low-shot' overall, but some subsets (complexes, alloys) are small and present few-shot conditions.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Direct transfer testing: ALIGNN trained only on native-defect dataset (Dataset 1) performs poorly on impurities (Dataset 2), alloys (Dataset 3), and complexes (Dataset 4) with RMSEs 2.17 eV, 2.68 eV, and 2.98 eV respectively; adding 50% of the new dataset to training reduces RMSEs to 0.36 eV (impurities), 0.70 eV (alloys), and 0.18 eV (complexes), showing limited out-of-distribution transfer unless representative examples are included in training.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Authors enlarge training set by including intermediate (partially optimized) structures from DFT relaxations to boost data diversity and report that including these IS improves model performance; no quantitative few-shot learning curves are given beyond the 50% inclusion experiment. Learning curves for CGCNN/ALIGNN are shown in SI (qualitative convergence), but no explicit numerical sample-efficiency curves are reported. ALIGNN yields much lower RMSE than CGCNN/MEGNET given the same dataset, indicating higher data efficiency for the chosen architecture.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: For Dataset 1: random splits 60:20:20 into training:validation:test. Transfer experiments: test datasets are Datasets 2–4 when model trained on Dataset 1; then random 50% of new dataset added to training set and model retrained. Separate ALIGNN models trained per charge state and per chemical potential (A-rich/B-rich). Some outlier removal was performed in final training to improve results.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Baselines: CGCNN and MEGNET trained on same data; ALIGNN outperforms both (test RMSE on Dataset 1 q=0: ALIGNN 0.15 eV vs CGCNN 0.35 eV vs MEGNET 0.40 eV). Ablations include testing model trained on native defects only vs combined datasets; experiments adding 50% of new data quantify importance of including impurities/alloys/complexes in training. Also examined ALIGNN predictions on unoptimized (pristine defect) structures vs DFT-optimized structures, and showed ALIGNN-based geometry optimization reduces errors.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Key RMSEs: Dataset 1 (q=0, A-rich): CGCNN test RMSE 0.35 eV, MEGNET 0.40 eV, ALIGNN 0.15 eV. Combined ALIGNN models across charges (A-rich) test RMSEs: q=+2 0.30 eV, q=+1 0.23 eV, q=0 0.32 eV, q=-1 0.25 eV, q=-2 0.26 eV. Transfer RMSEs (ALIGNN trained on Dataset1 tested on new datasets): impurities 2.17 eV, alloys 2.68 eV, complexes 2.98 eV; after adding 50% of new data to training RMSEs improved to 0.36 eV, 0.70 eV, and 0.18 eV respectively. CTL prediction: ALIGNN-optimization reduced CTL RMSE (vs DFT) from 0.37 eV (unoptimized) to 0.17 eV (ALIGNN-optimized). Average ALIGNN-unoptimized vs DFT-optimized difference for top 300 large-delta defects ≈ 1 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No direct modeling or prediction of phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity degradation is performed. The paper does not connect the ML outputs to phonon-based transport properties (no BTE/relaxation-time approximations or scattering-rate predictions reported).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue line-graph (angle) features capture three-body, long-range interactions and lattice distortions important for defect energetics beyond nearest neighbors; inclusion of partially optimized and unoptimized intermediates helps the model learn energy trends across relaxation pathways; elemental features capture periodic trends; training per-charge-state plus E^f at E_F=0 enables CTL construction with slope = q.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: ALIGNN trained on native defects does not generalize to impurities, alloys, or complexes without representative training data (large RMSEs). ALIGNN predictions on pristine (unoptimized) charged structures are less reliable (charged models trained mostly on optimized/near-optimized geometries). ALIGNN-unopt often overestimates E^f relative to DFT-optimized values (though usually an upper bound), and cannot on its own yield reliable CTLs without geometry optimization. Large structural rearrangements (especially interstitials and anti-sites) produce very large prediction errors if optimization is not considered. Models are trained on PBE-level DFT data, so band edge and CTL accuracy inherits PBE limitations.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use full defective-supercell crystal graphs with explicit angle (triplet) features (ALIGNN) for best accuracy; include intermediate (partially optimized) structures in the training set to increase robustness to unoptimized inputs; train separate models per integer charge state and per chemical potential condition and predict E^f at E_F = 0 then construct CTLs with slope = q, but perform geometry optimization (via GNN-based optimization or DFT) for accurate CTLs; include representative examples of impurities, alloys, and complexes in training to ensure transfer; treat ALIGNN predictions on pristine/unoptimized structures as an upper-bound screening metric (apply ~1 eV offset empirically or use an energy threshold) and follow up with optimization or higher-level corrections (HSE/GW) for precise electronic-level placement.

extracted_data.name_full: Materials Graph Network (MEGNET) representation with elemental embeddings
extracted_data.brief_description: A crystal graph GNN that uses learned elemental embeddings to encode periodic chemical trends and a message-passing framework over graph edges to predict materials properties; used here as a baseline structure-aware featurization for defect energetics.
extracted_data.citation_title: Accelerating Defect Predictions in Semiconductors Using Graph Neural Networks
extracted_data.material_systems: Same multihost zinc-blende semiconductor set (34 AB compounds) and associated defects/impurities/alloys/complexes as used elsewhere in the paper.
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies, interstitials, anti-sites, substitutional/interstitial impurities; complexes and alloys evaluated in transfer experiments (MEGNET used mainly as a baseline on Dataset 1).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Handled by training per-charge-state models analogous to other GNNs; paper reports MEGNET predictions per charge state similarly to CGCNN and ALIGNN (no explicit continuous charge-aware input features reported).
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energy (E^f) per charge state at E_F = 0; CTLs derived from predicted E^f values; no thermal transport properties predicted.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Crystal graph neural network with elemental embeddings (MEGNET)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Crystal supercell converted to a graph (atoms nodes, bonds edges); MEGNET uses elemental embeddings (learned continuous vectors capturing periodic trends) for node initialization plus bond/edge features and message-passing interaction blocks; readout maps aggregated node/edge features to target E^f.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full defective supercell used (no explicit defect-centered subgraph or delta-to-pristine features reported).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Edge features include bond distances (features / RBFs or bond-length encodings as per MEGNET defaults), r_c is a tunable hyperparameter (optimized in this work to some extent); number of interaction blocks and hidden sizes adopt MEGNET defaults except epochs/batch size/r_c were optimized here.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: MEGNET with message-passing interaction blocks and learned elemental embeddings; in this work only epochs, batch size, and cutoff r_c were tuned; architecture otherwise follows Chen et al. (2019) defaults as used by authors.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Elemental embeddings are part of MEGNET and encode periodic trends; authors adopt MEGNET defaults (embeddings learned during training on the defect dataset), but no external pretraining on large datasets is reported for this work.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained on the same DFT PBE defect datasets described elsewhere (Dataset 1 primarily in baseline experiments). MEGNET trained on thousands of defect IS and optimized structures; dataset sizes same as ALIGNN experiments for given splits.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: MEGNET was only directly compared on Dataset 1 and showed worse RMSE (test 0.40 eV for q=0 A-rich) than CGCNN and ALIGNN; no detailed cross-chemistry transfer experiments reported specifically for MEGNET beyond what was done generically for GNNs.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: MEGNET displays higher test RMSE than ALIGNN for same data, indicating it was less effective at capturing features needed for defect energetics in this dataset; no numerical sample-efficiency curves provided beyond baseline RMSEs.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Trained on Dataset 1 with random 60:20:20 splits (training/validation/test); hyperparameter tuning limited to epochs, batch size, and cutoff r_c in this work.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared as a baseline against CGCNN and ALIGNN on Dataset 1; MEGNET showed somewhat larger errors than CGCNN and ALIGNN (CGCNN better than MEGNET in test RMSE in the reported run, though MEGNET had more similar training/validation/test RMSEs indicating less overfitting in some cases).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: MEGNET (Dataset 1, q=0, A-rich) reported RMSEs: train 0.36 eV, validation 0.42 eV, test 0.40 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No connection to phonon scattering or lattice thermal conductivity; MEGNET predictions here are limited to formation energies and derived CTLs.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Elemental embeddings in MEGNET are suggested to encode periodic chemical trends and help generalization when data are limited, but in this dataset ALIGNN (explicit geometry/angle info) outperforms MEGNET.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: MEGNET underperforms ALIGNN for this defect dataset; it does not explicitly include 3-body angle features unless architecture is modified (and so may miss some deformation-related energetic contributions). Transfer to impurities/alloys not explicitly demonstrated for MEGNET in the paper.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: MEGNET-style elemental embeddings help capture chemical trends but for defect energetics one should also include explicit geometric/angle information (e.g., ALIGNN) and partially optimized structures to improve robustness.

extracted_data.name_full: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN) representation
extracted_data.brief_description: A crystal-graph convolutional model using atomic/node features and edge distance encodings with graph convolution and global pooling to predict formation energies; used here as a baseline GNN for defect formation energy prediction.
extracted_data.citation_title: Accelerating Defect Predictions in Semiconductors Using Graph Neural Networks
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to the same multi-host zinc-blende semiconductor defect datasets (Dataset 1 primarily) as a baseline.
extracted_data.defect_types: Same set: vacancies, interstitials, anti-sites, impurities; complexes/alloys evaluated in transfer experiments (baseline comparisons).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Per-charge-state models trained separately (as for other GNNs); no explicit charge features added to CGCNN inputs in this work.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energy (E^f) per charge state at E_F = 0; CTLs derived by constructing E^f vs E_F lines with slope = q; no phonon-related properties modeled.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Standard crystal-graph supercell representation (CGCNN)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Full defective supercell converted to a graph, atoms as nodes with elemental/atomic property-based node features, edges representing neighbors within a cutoff radius with bond-length features; multiple graph convolutional layers aggregate local neighbor information; global pooling creates a crystal-level vector used for regression.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full defective supercell representation (no explicit delta-to-pristine or defect-centered subgraph used). Authors also compare unoptimized vs optimized inputs as part of analysis.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Cutoff radius r_c is a key hyperparameter and was optimized in this work along with batch size and epochs; node features include atomic properties (number of properties used tunable), edges use bond-length encodings; explicit angular/triplet features are not part of CGCNN standard implementation.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: CGCNN (Xie & Grossman style) with several convolutional layers and global pooling; hyperparameters tuned in this work include r_c, batch size, epochs; other hyperparameters kept as in original CGCNN default.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No pretraining reported; CGCNN trained from scratch on the DFT defect datasets.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained on Dataset 1 (native defects) with 60:20:20 split; dataset sizes as reported previously (thousands of data points including intermediate structures).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: CGCNN baseline not reported as transfer experiment to datasets 2–4 in the main text; overall CGCNN gives worse performance than ALIGNN but better than prior composition-only models.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Learning curves and hyperparameter sensitivity (r_c, batch size) discussed in SI; performance (test RMSE q=0 A-rich) reported as 0.35 eV, showing decent sample efficiency but inferior to ALIGNN on same data.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Random 60:20:20 train/val/test on Dataset 1. Hyperparameter sweeps for r_c and batch size shown in SI.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared directly to MEGNET and ALIGNN on the same dataset; CGCNN performs better than prior composition-based models but worse than ALIGNN. No explicit ablation removing specific node/edge features reported beyond hyperparameter tuning.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: CGCNN (Dataset 1, q=0, A-rich) reported RMSEs: train 0.19 eV, validation 0.41 eV, test 0.35 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No phonon or thermal transport predictions or links reported.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Graph convolutions aggregate local environment information; however, lacking explicit angle/three-body encoding may limit capture of long-range lattice distortions caused by defects relative to ALIGNN.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Less accurate than ALIGNN for defect energetics likely due to missing angular/triplet features; same limitations as other GNNs regarding transfer to impurities/alloys/complexes if not represented in training; charged-state predictions for pristine/unoptimized structures can be unreliable.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Tune cutoff radius and include a diverse set of intermediate geometries in training; for best accuracy on defect energetics consider architectures that include angle/three-body information (ALIGNN) or add supplementary descriptors.

extracted_data.name_full: Training on intermediate (partially optimized) structures and iterative ALIGNN-driven geometry optimization
extracted_data.brief_description: Dataset augmentation by collecting intermediate geometries and energies from DFT relaxations (unoptimized → partially optimized → optimized) to increase structural diversity for GNN training, plus a gradient-free, iterative ALIGNN-based distortion procedure to lower predicted E^f and approximate DFT-optimized geometries.
extracted_data.citation_title: Accelerating Defect Predictions in Semiconductors Using Graph Neural Networks
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied across the same ZB semiconductor dataset (Datasets 1–4) and used in geometry-optimization demonstrations for select defects in ZnO, ZnS, AlP, Si, etc.
extracted_data.defect_types: Native defects, impurities, and selected defect complexes; geometry-optimization examples include substitutional dopants and interstitials.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Optimization is performed with ALIGNN predictions for all 5 q states; however, charged-model predictions on pristine/unoptimized charged structures are less reliable because charged calculations' training data are biased towards near-optimized geometries.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used to predict/optimize defect formation energies and to improve estimation of CTLs by yielding lower-energy geometries; not used for phonon/thermal transport predictions.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: IS-augmented training + iterative distortion (gradient-free) ALIGNN optimization
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Collect all intermediate structures (IS) during DFT relaxations and their corresponding energies to expand training set (captures unoptimized → optimized transition); use ALIGNN as an inexpensive energy predictor and perform iterative atomic displacements sampled from a normal distribution (no forces) to propose new structures, selecting those with lowered ALIGNN-predicted E^f and repeating until convergence or stagnation.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full defective supercell is used for both IS-augmented training and iterative optimization; initial structures are pristine-defect-introduced supercells (unoptimized).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Same graph featurization as ALIGNN (see ALIGNN entry): RBF distance and angular encodings, r_c = 8 Å in the reported ALIGNN-optimization runs, 12 neighbors typically used.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: ALIGNN models trained on datasets including intermediate structures (IS) and optimized structures; used as a fast surrogate energy evaluator during iterative distortion-based optimization.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No external pretraining; IS data are from DFT optimizations already run and collected (XDATCAR/OUTCAR extraction).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: IS augmentation dramatically increases the number of training samples (e.g., Dataset 1 q=0 increased to 3071 points by including IS), giving more coverage of energy/structure space between pristine and optimized configurations.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Using IS in training makes the model more aware of unoptimized/pristine geometries and improves the utility of ALIGNN-unopt predictions as screening surrogates; ALIGNN-optimization produced near-DFT energies for some defects (e.g., Re_Zn in ZnO: ALIGNN-opt 5.31 eV vs DFT-opt 5.30 eV), though other cases (e.g., La_Zn in ZnO) still showed remaining error (~1.15 eV above DFT). Overall, ALIGNN-optimization reduced CTL RMSE from 0.37 eV (unopt) to 0.17 eV.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: IS augmentation increases available training samples without expensive new DFT runs, improving model robustness to unoptimized structures; no explicit numerical learning-curve vs IS fraction is provided beyond reported dataset sizes and improved RMSEs on CTLs after optimization.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: IS were collected for all DFT relaxations by parsing XDATCAR/OUTCAR and E^f for each intermediate structure estimated via E_DFT(IS) relative to optimized E_DFT. ALIGNN-optimization applied iteratively (many hundreds to thousands of distortions) for selected defects; optimization success evaluated by comparing ALIGNN-predicted minima to DFT-optimized energies.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Comparisons made between ALIGNN-unoptimized predictions, ALIGNN-optimized predictions (via iterative distortions), and DFT-optimized results. Ablation of IS (i.e., training without IS) is implicitly shown to be worse because models trained without IS are less reliable on pristine/unoptimized inputs (charged models particularly affected).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Examples: Re_Zn (ZnO) ALIGNN-unopt → optimized reduced predicted E^f from 5.93 to 5.31 eV ~ matching DFT-opt 5.30 eV after 644 distortions; La_Zn (ZnO) reduced from 5.23 to 3.35 eV (ALIGNN-opt) vs DFT-opt 2.20 eV after 2407 distortions (less accurate). CTL RMSE improvement: 0.37 eV (ALIGNN-unopt vs DFT CTLs) → 0.17 eV (ALIGNN-optimized vs DFT CTLs).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No connection to phonon scattering or thermal conductivity is provided; optimization and IS augmentation focused on energetics only.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Including intermediate geometries helps the GNN learn how energies evolve during relaxations and improves its ability to evaluate/prioritize unrelaxed/pristine defect structures; using the model as a cheap surrogate within an iterative distortion protocol can recover near-DFT minima for many defects, enabling faster screening.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Iterative, gradient-free optimization can be trapped in local minima and there's no clear stopping criterion; number of required distortions varies widely and can be large (hundreds to thousands); for some defects ALIGNN-optimization does not reach DFT-opt energies, particularly when large rearrangements or complex relaxation pathways exist; charged-state optimization is less reliable when charged training data are scarce or biased.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Collect intermediate structures from DFT relaxations to augment training, treat unoptimized ALIGNN predictions as upper bounds (screen with conservative thresholds, e.g., ALIGNN-unopt < 1 eV to catch likely low-energy defects), use ALIGNN-based iterative optimization to reduce the number of expensive DFT relaxations required for CTL determination, and validate final candidates with full DFT and, where needed, higher-level electronic-structure corrections (HSE/GW) for CTLs.

extracted_data.name_full: Impurity-Averaged Configuration (IAC)
extracted_data.brief_description: A stochastic, ensemble-averaged defect embedding that marginalizes over unknown defect positions and correlations to produce a compact, machine-readable representation (reducing to defect concentrations for random independent defects). Used as the primary defect featurization in DefectNet.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to a large, diverse set of semiconductors (2,000 distinct parent materials) and their doped supercells; also fine-tuned/applied to SiGe alloys (amorphous/crystalline mixtures) and Al-doped MgB2 experimental GPDoS.
extracted_data.defect_types: Substitutional point dopants only (up to six coexisting substitutional defect species per sample); vacancy, interstitials, Frenkel pairs, antisites, and defect clusters are explicitly outside current implementation.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: The IAC formalism is stated to be general enough to encode charge and spin correlations via the defect embedding and the probability model P_phi, but in practice the work treats substitutional dopants without explicit defect charge-state labels or Fermi-level/electrostatic corrections (i.e., effectively neutral/undifferentiated charge states).
extracted_data.target_properties: Predicts chemical identity (which elements are present as substitutional dopants) and quantitative concentrations from vibrational spectra (PDoS/GPDoS). Theoretical derivation links IAC to changes in PDoS (Eq. 5/ S17) but the network does not directly predict phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Impurity-Averaged Configuration (IAC)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Represent defects as learnable site embeddings g_{jαθ} and treat defect positions R_{jα} as random variables sampled from a learnable distribution P_φ; compute the ensemble average of defect contributions in momentum space. For independent, random defects the IAC reduces to a concatenated vector proportional to defect densities n_α times average defect embeddings g_{αθ} (i.e., effectively a sparse vector of concentrations).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not defect-centered in the conventional local-subgraph sense: it is an ensemble/global representation that discards explicit positional detail (unless P_φ encodes correlations) and is used alongside a pristine reference (pristine composition and pristine PDoS are inputs to DefectNet).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: No explicit local cutoff or radial/angular expansion; underlying atomic feature vectors for each species are Embed_θ(1, Z, m, s, r, ...). The IAC aggregates these embeddings across sites (expectation/average) rather than encoding explicit neighbor lists or angular basis functions.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: No defect-centered graph model for IAC itself; DefectNet uses a spectral encoder (multi-channel 1D convolutions) + multi-head attention with an embedded dopant-query and MLP heads (see separate representation entries).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: IAC embeddings (g_{αθ}) are learnable within DefectNet; training data (PDoS) are generated using foundation ML interatomic potentials (MACE-MP-0 and MatterSim) but those potentials are used for data generation rather than as direct fixed embeddings inside DefectNet.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretraining on 16,000 simulated doped supercells derived from 2,000 parent semiconductors; dopants sampled from first 56 elements (no noble gases); supercells of 433–500 atoms to achieve dilute concentrations (0.2%–25%); vibrational spectra computed by MLIPs (MACE-MP-0) and Gaussian-smeared to mimic experiment; fine-tuning datasets: ~500 GPDoS for SiGe and additional experimental GPDoS for SiGe and MgB2.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Tested both in-distribution (same parent materials split) and out-of-distribution (entire pristine parent materials excluded from training). DefectNet generalizes to unseen crystals across the 56 element set with modest accuracy drop O(see Fig.4). It was fine-tuned on MLIP-based amorphous/crystalline Si datasets and successfully recovered Ge fractions in experimental Si1-xGex and Al in MgB2 (predicted concentrations track experimental trends).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Pretraining used 16k simulated PDoS; bridging to experiment required fine-tuning: for SiGe fine-tune used ~500 GPDoS samples (plus 100 amorphous Si supercells for parent-disorder coverage) to reach test RMSE=0.019 in Ge fraction. Authors state fine-tuning is essential to bridge MLIP->experiment domain gap.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Two main splits: (1) in-distribution random split by PDoS curves from the same parent materials (train/test from same parents); (2) out-of-distribution by excluding entire pristine parent materials from training (test on unseen parents). Tests include distractor dopants in the initial guess to evaluate false-positive suppression. Hard-masking ensures predictions only for candidate dopants provided.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No direct comparisons to standard defect-centered graph or local-descriptor baselines reported in main text; ablations mentioned conceptually (e.g., spectral attention importance) but quantitative ablation results vs alternate featurizations are not provided in the main paper (some additional tests referenced in Supplementary Information 3, but no explicit descriptor-vs-IAC numerical baselines shown).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Claims detection of substitutional dopant concentrations down to ≈0.2%; fine-tuned SiGe test RMSE in Ge fraction = 0.019; when applied to experimental Si1-xGex (nominal x=0.05,0.10,0.20) predicted x ≈ 0.07,0.13,0.22 respectively. General in-distribution/out-of-distribution prediction error summarized by MSE quartiles in Fig.4 (no single global MAE/RMSE across the whole simulated test set reported numerically in main text).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: IAC is explicitly connected to PDoS via many-body/neutron-scattering derivation (Eq.5/S17): D(E)-D0(E) contains terms ∝ Σ_{α,β} n_α n_β g_{α} g_{β} (plus cross terms). This provides a formal link between defect concentration/embeddings and vibrational spectra. However, the work does not use DefectNet to predict phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity directly — only defect concentrations from vibrational spectra; no BTE or kappa predictions are reported.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: IAC reduces combinatorial structural complexity by averaging over positional degrees of freedom; captures ensemble (density and correlation) information, and allows representation of positional, charge, and spin correlations if P_φ is specified; spectral attention is claimed to increase sensitivity to subtle PDoS perturbations; hard-masking with a dopant recommender reduces false positives.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Authors report decreased sensitivity at very low concentrations where PDoS perturbations approach noise; current implementation limited to substitutional dopants (no vacancies/interstitials/complexes); success depends on quality of initial candidate- dopant guess (hard-masking prevents recovery of missed dopants); MLIP-generated spectra differ from DFT/experiment so fine-tuning on target experimental datasets is necessary; INS access limits practical deployment.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use MLIPs for high-throughput generation of training PDoS, provide a credible initial candidate-dopant list (human or recommender) and apply hard-masking, fine-tune the pretrained DefectNet on a modest-size experimental/target dataset to bridge domain gap, feed consistent pristine reference (DFT/MLIP/experimental) to minimize distribution mismatch, and use GPDoS (neutron-weighted) when targeting neutron scattering measurements.

extracted_data.name_full: Ensemble Embedding Embed_θ (atomic / defect feature embedding)
extracted_data.brief_description: A learnable embedding layer that maps atomic feature vectors (e.g., one-hot, Z, mass, spin, radius, ...) to dense feature embeddings f_{jθ} for host atoms and g_{jαθ} for defect atoms; used as the input features for IAC and the network.
extracted_data.material_systems: Same 2,000 semiconductors and their doped supercells used to generate training PDoS; embeddings encode elemental attributes for all species considered (56 elements).
extracted_data.defect_types: Substitutional dopants encoded via defect-site embeddings g_{jαθ}; no explicit encoding for vacancies/interstitials in current work.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Embedding can accept charge/spin as input features (authors list charge number Z and spin s among inputs), but no explicit charged-defect labels or Fermi-level features are included in the implemented dataset/training.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used to parameterize defect/site identity information that feeds into IAC and hence into the defect-concentration prediction from PDoS; not directly predicting formation energies or charge transition levels.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Ensemble embedding / Embed_θ
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Atomic feature vector (1, Z, m, s, r, ...) is projected by a learnable Embed_θ to produce f_{jθ} (host) and g_{jαθ} (defect) dense embeddings; ensemble averaging over sites/defects is used to produce compact descriptors (IAC).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Site-level embeddings exist but are averaged across defects in IAC; the approach does not build local defect-centered subgraphs in the model's implementation.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Input atomic features explicitly include values like atomic number, mass, spin and effective radius (authors list these example channels); embeddings are learned end-to-end (no explicit radial/angular cutoff or explicit species one-hot only), and the first component of g can be interpreted as concentration when averaged.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Embeddings are used in a non-graph pipeline (convolutions on spectra + attention). The embedding mechanism itself is similar in spirit to ensemble-embedding GNNs but the overall model does not run a graph-based message-passing on atomic coordinates for the defect prediction task.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Embed_θ parameters are learned during DefectNet pretraining; authors cite prior work on ensemble-embedding GNNs (Hung et al.) but do not use an externally pretrained embedding in the reported DefectNet.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained end-to-end on simulated PDoS dataset (16k) with embeddings learned jointly with the prediction head.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Learned embeddings transfer via DefectNet's pretraining/fine-tuning procedure: pretraining on MLIP data then fine-tuning to experimental GPDoS demonstrates that the learned embeddings can adapt to domain shifts with modest fine-tuning (~500 GPDoS).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: No explicit learning-curve ablation for embeddings alone; the overall pipeline requires substantial pretraining but relatively small fine-tuning to adapt to experiment (see IAC entry).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Embeddings learned as part of standard DefectNet training with in-distribution and out-of-distribution splits (host exclusion tests).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No explicit ablation contrasting different embedding input channels (e.g., excluding mass or radius) is reported in main text.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: No separate metric reported solely for embedding quality; performance reported at system level (see IAC entry).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Embedding encodes atomic properties that influence vibrational contributions (mass, etc.), which feed into IAC and the theoretical link between defect embeddings and changes in PDoS; embeddings are thus an indirect factor in phonon-sensitive predictions.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Embedding compresses diverse atomic features into a compact continuous representation that supports averaging across defects and enables the network to learn chemical trends that map to spectral perturbations.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: No explicit experiments separating the effect of particular atomic feature channels; embeddings alone do not encode explicit long-range electrostatics or charged-state information unless such channels are included in input features and in training data.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include physically meaningful atomic attributes (Z, mass, spin, radius) in embedding inputs when defects affect vibrational spectra; learn embeddings end-to-end with sufficient pretraining and fine-tune on experimental data to handle real-measurement shifts.

extracted_data.name_full: Spectral attention mechanism with dopant-query embedding and hard-masking
extracted_data.brief_description: A modelling/featurization strategy that combines multi-channel 1D convolutional encodings of pristine and doped PDoS with a learnable dopant-query embedding (from an initial candidate list) and multi-head attention to focus on spectral features informative for particular candidate dopants; final outputs are hard-masked to candidate dopants.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied across the full DefectNet dataset (16k simulated PDoS) and in experimental fine-tuning tasks (SiGe, MgB2).
extracted_data.defect_types: Substitutional dopants encoded via the candidate list; supports up to six coexisting species in predictions (model architecture allows multiple candidates).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: No explicit charge-state tokens in the dopant-query; query encodes candidate elemental species only (binary vector over 56 elements).
extracted_data.target_properties: Predicts which candidate dopants are present and their concentrations directly from PDoS inputs; attention concentrates spectral information relevant to each candidate.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Spectral encoder + dopant-query attention with hard-masking
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Inputs: 3-channel 1D signals (pristine PDoS, doped PDoS, composition vector) of length 100 are encoded by multi-channel 1D convs into a latent sequence V; initial candidate dopant binary vector (56-dim) is projected to a 128-dim query Q; MultiHead Attention(Q,V,V) yields features that link candidate dopants to spectral tokens; a downstream MLP predicts concentrations and a hard mask restricts outputs to provided candidates.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Global spectral representation (PDoS) with a candidate-list conditioning; uses a pristine reference PDoS and composition as inputs (i.e., delta-like information implicit in inputs), rather than an explicit defect-centered local atomic neighborhood.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Spectral tokens length L=100, latent dimension d=128 after convolutional encoder; no atomic neighbor cutoff or angular basis because featurization is based on spectra not explicit local atomic geometry.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Implements transformer-style multi-head self-attention (standard scaled dot-product attention) with H heads; attention Q derived from dopant embedding, K=V from spectral encoder. No atomistic GNN is used for the prediction head.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Model is pretrained on MLIP-generated PDoS data (16k) and then fine-tuned to experimental GPDoS; the attention/query design conditions spectral interpretation on a candidate list (provided via Hautier recommender or human).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Same 16k simulated PDoS for pretraining; fine-tuning used ~500 GPDoS for SiGe plus experimental GPDoS samples for final evaluation.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Out-of-distribution host-exclusion tests show modest performance reduction but continued ability to identify true dopants and suppress distractors; fine-tuning with experimental GPDoS yields strong alignment to experimental concentrations (SiGe RMSE=0.019).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Fine-tuning to experimental data achieved with a relatively small dataset (~500 GPDoS samples), indicating good data efficiency for domain adaptation when pretrained on large MLIP-generated dataset.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Model trained with train/validation/test splits described in IAC entry; hard-masking ensures predicted nonzeros only on candidate list during both training and inference, and distractor experiments added at test time to probe false-positive suppression.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No explicit baseline attention-less model numeric comparison shown in main text; authors assert the spectral attention is necessary to extract subtle signals at low dopant concentrations, but quantitative ablation numbers (with/without attention) are not provided in main text.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: System-level metrics as in IAC entry: sensitivity down to ~0.2% concentrations (claim), fine-tuned SiGe RMSE=0.019; qualitative and quartile-based MSE visualizations for multi-dopant cases shown in Fig.4.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: The attention module is used to amplify subtle PDoS changes induced by defects (which are related to phonon behavior). The architecture does not predict scattering rates or kappa, but it is positioned to extract the spectral signatures that would be needed as inputs to transport calculations.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Attention conditioned on candidate dopants helps the network focus on spectral regions/features most informative for particular elements, improving sensitivity to weak signals and enabling suppression of distractor species via hard-masking.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Dependence on initial candidate-dopant list: if a true dopant is omitted from the candidate list, hard-masking prevents recovery; attention/hard-masking may suppress discovery of unexpected species. Sensitivity declines at very low concentrations and domain-shift between simulation and experiment requires fine-tuning.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Provide a reasonably comprehensive candidate list (e.g., use dopant recommender), fine-tune pretrained spectral-attention models on representative experimental spectra, and include pristine reference spectra to maximize delta-information captured by the encoder.

extracted_data.name_full: ML Interatomic Potentials (MACE-MP-0, MatterSim) for high-throughput PDoS generation
extracted_data.brief_description: Use of foundation/large-scale machine-learned interatomic potentials to generate high-throughput, DFT-quality vibrational spectra (PDoS/GPDoS) for many doped supercells, enabling large-scale pretraining of DefectNet.
extracted_data.citation_title: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry
extracted_data.material_systems: All simulated training data (2,000 parent semiconductors, 16k doped supercells) produced with MACE-MP-0 MLIP; MatterSim (a high-accuracy MLIP) used for SiGe amorphous/crystalline GPDoS simulations for fine-tuning.
extracted_data.defect_types: Substitutional dopants in MLIP-relaxed supercells (simulated substitutional defects only).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: MLIP calculations used for structural relaxation and frozen-phonon calculations do not encode explicit charged defect states in this workflow (standard MLIP frameworks model neutral atomic interactions unless augmented).
extracted_data.target_properties: Generation of vibrational properties: PDoS and GPDoS via frozen-phonon calculations using MLIPs; not used to predict energies or charge transition levels in the present work.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation MLIPs for data generation (MACE-MP-0, MatterSim)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Employ pre-existing, general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potentials to relax large supercells and compute frozen-phonon PDoS, thereby producing large-scale training data with reduced computational cost compared to DFT.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: MLIP-simulated datasets include full supercells (433–500 atoms) with explicit atomic positions; DefectNet, however, discards explicit coordinates and uses the resulting spectra as inputs together with composition.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: MLIP computations implicitly capture local environments; no explicit MLIP-to-DefectNet feature transfer (potentials are not used as fixed feature extractors in the classifier).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: N/A for the classifier; MLIPs themselves are foundation atomistic models (MACE-style architectures) but are only used to produce data.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: These MLIPs are foundation models used to create training labels/spectra; no evidence that their internal latent embeddings were exported into DefectNet.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Enabled generation of 16,000 doped-supercell PDoS samples covering 2,000 hosts and substitutional dopants across 56 elements; supercell sizes selected to reach dilute concentrations as low as 0.2%.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Authors note MLIP-generated spectra differ from DFT/experiment (force-field inaccuracies, measurement noise, uncontrolled defect environments), and thus fine-tuning on experimental data is necessary; successful fine-tuning to experimental GPDoS supports the approach's practical transferability when adapted.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: MLIPs dramatically lower cost vs DFT, enabling a 16k dataset that would be otherwise costly; this large simulated corpus plus modest fine-tuning (~500 experimental/simulated GPDoS) yields good experimental performance (SiGe RMSE=0.019).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: All pretraining PDoS computed with MACE-MP-0 under frozen phonon formalism; Gaussian smearing applied to mimic experimental resolution; MatterSim used for SiGe GPDoS and amorphous Si sampling.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No direct DFT-vs-MLIP quantitative comparison in main text, only qualitative discussion that domain gap exists and must be bridged by fine-tuning.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Enables the creation of the 16k training set and supercell PDoS for concentrations down to 0.2%; no direct numerical metric comparing MLIP accuracy to DFT reported in main text.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: MLIPs used to compute PDoS (and GPDoS) that encode phonon spectra; while PDoS is used to infer defects, no end-to-end prediction of phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity was performed. The MLIPs produce the vibrational inputs necessary for any downstream transport modeling, but such coupling was not demonstrated here.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Using high-quality MLIPs enables broad chemical coverage and high-throughput generation of vibrational spectra for training foundation defect identification models, alleviating the DFT bottleneck.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Simulated MLIP spectra can differ from DFT/experimental spectra due to force-field errors and missing measurement noise; these distribution shifts mandate fine-tuning on experimental data for accurate real-world performance.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use validated MLIPs to generate diverse training spectra covering disorder and concentration ranges; apply Gaussian smearing to mimic instrument resolution; always fine-tune on a modest experimental dataset to bridge MLIP↔experiment domain gaps.

extracted_data.name_full: Dopant recommender (Hautier substitution model + Shannon-radius fallback) with output hard-masking
extracted_data.brief_description: An upstream candidate-generation system (Hautier et al. probabilistic substitutional doping model, with Shannon ionic radius fallback) is used to propose plausible dopant species per host; DefectNet then hard-masks its outputs to the provided candidate set to suppress false positives.
extracted_data.citation_title: Data mined ionic substitutions for the discovery of new compounds
extracted_data.material_systems: Used to select plausible substitutional dopants for the 2,000 semiconductors in the training dataset and to provide candidate lists at inference for experimental/validation samples (applies to diverse semiconductors and Si-based alloys).
extracted_data.defect_types: Substitutional dopants only (recommender proposes element substitutions consistent with oxidation state/radius criteria).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Hautier recommender considers chemical compatibility but does not output explicit defect charge-state labels; Shannon-radius fallback addresses ionic size/oxidation mismatch but not explicit electrostatic charging corrections.
extracted_data.target_properties: Serves as a prior/candidate set for DefectNet to predict defect chemical identities and concentrations from PDoS; not itself used to predict energetics or concentrations.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Probabilistic substitutional-dopant recommender + hard-masking
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: For each host, the Hautier MD-substitution model ranks likely substitutional pairs; where that fails, a Shannon ionic-radius matching fallback is used; the resulting candidate dopant binary vector (length 56) is embedded and serves as the query for attention; outputs are hard-masked so only candidates receive non-zero predictions.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Provides a global candidate list conditioned on host composition; does not provide local structural defect coordinates.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not applicable — recommender is chemistry/ionic-radius based, not a local-structure featurizer.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Recommender implemented via Pymatgen interface; no graph architecture in recommender itself in this work.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Hautier model is an external data-mined substitutional model; DefectNet embeddings are conditioned on its candidate output but recommender itself is not a learned embedding inside DefectNet.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Used across the full generated dataset to propose plausible dopants; ensures training samples are chemically reasonable and guides both dataset generation and inference-time candidate sets.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Recommender helps constrain plausible dopants across diverse chemistries; however, authors note that missed/incomplete candidate lists can prevent recovery of true dopants (hard-masking failure mode), limiting open-ended discovery.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Using a recommender reduces the candidate space and likely improves data efficiency and prediction precision by narrowing the model's search space, but no explicit ablation quantifying this effect is provided.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Recommender outputs binary candidate vectors used during both dataset generation and model inference; hard-masking applied to network outputs during both training and test.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: No explicit comparisons between recommender-constrained vs unconstrained (open-vocabulary) inference reported in main text; authors note that unconstrained inference may be more challenging and was not the adopted workflow.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: No standalone metrics for recommender efficacy; system-level results (DefectNet predictions) reflect constrained-candidate strategy benefits (reduction of false positives shown qualitatively in distractor experiments, Fig.4).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Recommender only provides candidate species and does not interface directly with phonon/transport calculations.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Providing a chemically plausible candidate list allows attention to focus on relevant spectral features and reduces false-positive predictions; recommender thus acts as a useful prior for constrained inverse inference from PDoS.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Hard-masking prevents recovery of true dopants omitted from the candidate list; recommender may fail for hosts with unusual oxidation states (authors apply Shannon-radius fallback in such cases).
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use a robust recommender (Hautier model + radius-based fallback) to propose candidate dopants, but ensure candidate lists are comprehensive for discovery tasks; consider alternative workflows (e.g., soft-masking or open-vocabulary models) if unknown/unexpected dopants are possible.
