extracted_data.name_full: Machine Learning Hamiltonian (MLH) model for total energies and forces
extracted_data.brief_description: An MLH-based workflow that predicts real-space Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian matrix elements with an equivariant GNN (HamGNN) and then derives wavefunctions, charge density, total energy and atomic forces, enabling linear-scaling defect relaxations and accurate formation energies from a small DFT dataset.
extracted_data.material_systems: Amorphous SiO2 (a-SiO2) only in this study (multiple amorphous host cells were generated); single host chemistry tested (Si,O).
extracted_data.defect_types: Neutral oxygen vacancy (V_O) point defects only; no substitutional dopants, interstitials, antisites, Frenkel pairs or defect complexes considered.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Neutral-only; paper explicitly focuses on neutral defects and neutral defect formation energies (no explicit charged-defect labels, Fermi-level or background-charge corrections included).
extracted_data.target_properties: Predicted: Hamiltonian matrix elements, band structure, real-space wavefunctions and charge density, total energies, atomic forces, structural relaxation trajectories, and neutral defect formation energies.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Real-space Hamiltonian prediction via an equivariant graph neural network (MLH/HamGNN)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: An E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (HamGNN) maps atomic positions and species to real-space Hamiltonian matrix blocks (decomposed into on-site and off-site parts). The network uses node (atomic/orbital) and edge (pair) features, with distance expanded in Bessel basis and relative directions embedded via spherical harmonics to produce orbital-resolved Hamiltonian matrix elements for the full supercell (periodicity handled through real-space to k-space Fourier transforms).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-supercell Hamiltonian prediction (not a small defect-centered delta representation). The model is trained on defect-containing 95-atom supercells and applied to larger supercells without relying on an explicit pristine reference subtraction; formation energies benefit from cancellation of host/defect total-energy errors.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Interatomic distances expanded with Bessel basis (N_b = 64); cutoff radius r_c = 26 Bohr (~13.8 Å); relative directions embedded with spherical harmonics up to l_max = 4; equivariant feature channels specified across parity and angular orders (detailed channel counts reported); species (Si, O) are included via node features in the graph (no explicit one-hot specification given, but species are encoded in node features).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: HamGNN: a transferable E(3)-equivariant graph neural network with 3 orbital-convolution layers, equivariant message-passing, and a pair-interaction layer; node features updated via orbital convolution; edge features formed by integrating atom-pair features. Detailed irreducible-representation channel counts and parity (even/odd) are reported.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No pretraining used for the MLH in this work; HamGNN is trained from scratch on the reported small DFT dataset (no transfer from foundation potentials or pretrained interatomic potentials).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Training dataset: 120 SCF calculations (unrelaxed V_O structures) + 480 configurations sampled along 12 relaxation trajectories = 600 structures total (all from DFT on 95-atom supercells). Dataset split random 8:1:1 (train/val/test) for MLH. Relatively small/low-shot dataset compared with typical MLIPs.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Strong in-domain and out-of-training-size transfer demonstrated: MLH trained only on 95-atom defect supercells successfully predicts Hamiltonians, charge densities, energies and forces for hosts and V_O defects in larger supercells (tested 95, 215, 383 and host supercells up to 576 atoms). Quantitative results: Hamiltonian MAE on held-out test set 0.26 meV (matrix elements); for unseen 95-atom defect MAE 0.72 meV; charge-density MAE 3e-4 e/Å^3. Energy per-atom errors remain low (majority < ~1.2 meV/atom) and formation energy MAEs: 16 meV (95-atom), 26 meV (215-atom), 45 meV (383-atom), showing error cancellation and transfer to larger supercells.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Explicit claim and demonstration of small-data efficiency: model trained on only 120 SCF + 12 relaxations (600 structures) yet achieves DFT-comparable formation energies (<50 meV) and accurate forces; contrasted with other MLIP studies requiring thousands of DFT points (cited examples). No formal learning curves are provided, but the numerical outcomes show high sample efficiency.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Dataset randomly split 8:1:1 for MLH (train/val/test). In relaxation-transfer tests, configurations encountered during a given relaxation trajectory were excluded from the training set to avoid leakage. For MLIP baseline, a 9:1 train/validation split was used. Additional out-of-training-size tests used unseen larger supercells.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Main baseline: an Allegro-style MLIP trained on the same dataset; direct comparison to DFT. Ablation-style evidence: comparison emphasizes that MLIP trained only on defect supercells shows systematic host energy errors and potential-energy-surface softening, while MLH avoids these systematic errors. No explicit internal ablation (e.g., varying HamGNN cutoffs or equivariance) is reported.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Hamiltonian MAE (matrix elements): test 0.26 meV; unseen 95-atom defect: 0.72 meV. Charge-density MAE: 3×10^-4 e/Å^3. Total-energy errors: example MLH total energy 94 meV higher than DFT (≈1 meV/atom for a 95-atom cell); MLH per-atom energy errors reported ≈0.85 meV/atom (95-atom case), 0.41 meV/atom (215-atom), 1.1 meV/atom (383-atom). Atomic-force MAE: ~27 meV/Å for an example defect; typical force MAEs ≈25 meV/Å across many cases. MLIP baseline errors (for same tests): much larger — total energy error 990 meV and forces 115 meV/Å in one example; systematic host error ~1180 meV/atom in some host tests. Formation-energy MAEs (defect formation energy): 16 meV (95-atom), 26 meV (215-atom), 45 meV (383-atom). Band energies deviations ~0.01 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: None in this work: the paper does not predict phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity degradation. It only notes in related-work citations that MLIPs have been used elsewhere to compute phonon spectra, Grüneisen parameters and related vibrational properties (e.g., Shimizu et al.). No coupling of MLH outputs to phonon/BTE calculations is presented.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors attribute MLH success to directly learning the electronic Hamiltonian (thus enabling charge density and wavefunction recovery) and to the equivariant graph representation that captures orbital and spatial symmetries; these features allow accurate host and defect energies even when trained on a small defect-only dataset. They also point to error cancellation between host and defect total-energy errors as the reason formation energies are much more accurate than absolute total-energy errors.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Reported limitations: MLH total energies are slightly elevated relative to DFT due to residual Hamiltonian errors and structural differences; the study focuses only on neutral defects (no charged defects or defect complexes); the MLH still exhibits increasing per-atom energy error at the largest supercell sizes (formation-energy errors grow with supercell size though remain <50 meV up to 383 atoms). No handling of long-range electrostatics for charged systems is presented.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Train models that describe both host and defect systems (or use representations that recover electronic structure) to avoid systematic host-energy bias seen in MLIPs; use Hamiltonian-predicting equivariant models (MLH/HamGNN) to recover wavefunctions/charge density and derive energies/forces; exclude relaxation-trajectory configurations from training when evaluating transferability; small but carefully sampled DFT sets (including SCF samples and relaxation trajectories) can suffice for MLH training.

extracted_data.name_full: HamGNN (Transferable E(3) equivariant graph neural network for Hamiltonian prediction)
extracted_data.brief_description: An E(3)-equivariant graph neural network architecture used here to predict real-space Hamiltonian matrix elements by decomposing them into on-site and off-site parts and performing orbital-aware equivariant message passing.
extracted_data.citation_title: Transferable equivariant graph neural networks for the Hamiltonian of molecules and solids
extracted_data.material_systems: Used here on amorphous SiO2; HamGNN was developed for molecules and solids generally (ref. paper).
extracted_data.defect_types: Applied to neutral oxygen vacancies in a-SiO2 in this work; HamGNN itself targets general Hamiltonian prediction (molecules/solids).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: No explicit scheme for charged defects in this implementation; used for neutral systems here.
extracted_data.target_properties: Hamiltonian matrix elements, band structures, wavefunctions, charge densities, derived total energies and forces.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Equivariant graph representation with orbital-resolved node features and pairwise edge features
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Nodes represent atoms/orbitals; edges encode pair interactions within cutoff; distances expanded in Bessel basis (N_b=64) and orientations in spherical harmonics (l_max=4) producing equivariant message passing that outputs on-site and off-site Hamiltonian blocks.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-supercell graph (not defect-centered delta features); uses periodic image information when reconstructing k-space Hamiltonian.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Cutoff r_c = 26 Bohr; Bessel radial basis (N_b=64); spherical harmonics to l_max=4; equivariant irreducible representation channels with explicit parity and angular-order channel counts (detailed in Methods).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Equivariant orbital-convolution layers (3 layers reported), pair interaction layer, equivariant message passing; orbitally resolved outputs (on-site/off-site decomposition).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No pretraining; trained from scratch on DFT Hamiltonian data in this work.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained on 600 DFT configurations derived from 95-atom supercells (120 SCF + 480 relaxation-sampled).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: HamGNN (as used here) transfers to larger supercells and unseen amorphous configurations; Hamiltonian MAE on test 0.26 meV and unseen defect 0.72 meV; charge-density and energy/force predictions validate transfer.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: High efficiency shown: accurate Hamiltonian and derived properties from ~600 training structures.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Random 8:1:1 split; held-out larger-supercell tests excluded training-relaxation configurations.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared directly to a local MLIP (Allegro) baseline trained on same data; HamGNN + MLH outperforms MLIP notably for host-energy bias and force accuracy.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Hamiltonian MAE 0.26 meV (test), 0.72 meV (unseen 95-atom); charge-density MAE 3e-4 e/Å^3; energy/force errors reported in MLH entry.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: None in this implementation; HamGNN enables wavefunction/charge density outputs that in principle could be used for further vibrational/phonon coupling but not demonstrated.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Equivariance + orbital-aware features allow direct learning of electronic Hamiltonian, enabling recovery of electronic structure and better generalization to different supercell sizes.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: No charged-defect handling demonstrated; residual Hamiltonian errors can lead to slight systematic elevation of total energies; needs DFT Hamiltonian/SCF data for training.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use orbital-resolved equivariant GNNs with sufficiently large radial cutoff and angular resolution for Hamiltonian prediction; include relaxation-trajectory samples to cover configuration space.

extracted_data.name_full: Allegro-style equivariant local interatomic potential (MLIP) baseline
extracted_data.brief_description: A local equivariant interatomic potential (Allegro implementation) trained on the same small dataset as MLH and used as a baseline; it uses local atomic environment descriptors and predicts per-atom energies and forces.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied on amorphous SiO2 hosts and V_O defect supercells in this study as a baseline.
extracted_data.defect_types: Neutral oxygen vacancies (same as MLH tests); local potential learns defect configurations within cutoff.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: None (neutral systems only).
extracted_data.target_properties: Per-atom energies and atomic forces (used for structural relaxations and energy comparisons).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Local atom-centered equivariant descriptors with finite cutoff (Allegro-style)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Local environment representation with cutoff 6 Å, equivariant tensor product layers (3 layers), l_max = 2; per-atom energy decomposition and force derivation via gradients.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Atom-centered local descriptor (full supercell energy obtained by summing local contributions); relies on local environments within 6 Å (no explicit pristine-reference subtraction).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Cutoff radius = 6 Å; 3 tensor product layers; maximum angular quantum number l_max = 2; species included implicitly via node features as standard in Allegro-style models.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Allegro-style equivariant local model with 3 tensor product layers; trained to predict per-atom energies and forces (details in Methods).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Trained from scratch on the small dataset in this work; no foundation-model pretraining used for this baseline.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Same small dataset as MLH (600 structures from 95-atom defect supercells); train/validation split 9:1 for Allegro baseline.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Poor transferability observed: Allegro trained on defect-only small-supercell data exhibits large systematic host-energy bias when applied to host supercells and to larger supercells (examples: systematic overestimation ≈1180 meV/atom in host tests; large total-energy and force errors for defect relaxations).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Despite being trained on same small dataset, Allegro/MLIP shows poor performance; highlights that local MLIPs can require much larger datasets for reliable host/defect transfer.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Random 9:1 train/validation split; tested on unseen relaxations and larger supercells where training relax configs were excluded.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Used as the principal baseline versus MLH; shows systematic energy errors and potential-energy-surface softening not present in MLH predictions.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Example errors: total-energy error 990 meV and force MAE 115 meV/Å for an example defect; systematic host error ~1180 meV/atom in host relaxations; ΔQ structural deviations up to ~18 amu^{1/2}Å for MLIP-relaxed structures vs <2 amu^{1/2}Å for MLH in many cases.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: None in this work; Allegro baseline was not used to compute phonon-related properties here.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Local decomposition and training only on defect supercells caused inaccurate estimation of host-atom contributions and PES softening, leading to systematic errors; suggests MLIPs need host data or much larger datasets to avoid bias.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Large systematic host-energy bias when trained only on defect-containing small supercells; potential-energy-surface softening and poor structural-relaxation fidelity; not suitable here for accurate formation energies unless training sets expanded to include host configurations or much larger amounts of data.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include both host and defect supercells in MLIP training or greatly expand dataset diversity; validate MLIP host-energy bias before using summed-per-atom energies for formation energies.

extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Not detailed in this paper; mention relates to transfer and catastrophic forgetting upon fine-tuning.
extracted_data.target_properties: Contextual: interatomic potential tasks (energies/forces) and downstream defect/doped-system predictions in cited work.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation pretrained interatomic potential (MACE-MP) on large dataset MPtrj
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Pretrained model (MACE-MP) was trained on a large universal dataset (MPtrj) and then fine-tuned for doped systems in cited work; the paper cites limitations (struggled on doped perovskites and fine-tuning caused catastrophic forgetting).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not specified in this paper; cited as an example of pretraining then fine-tuning on dopants.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not specified in detail in this paper (the citation refers to a foundation model trained on large trajectory datasets).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: MACE-MP referenced (an equivariant message-passing architecture) in related work but not used in this study.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Mentioned as a cautionary example: pretrained on MPtrj then fine-tuned for dopants led to improved dopant predictions but catastrophic forgetting on original dataset.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: MPtrj foundation dataset referenced in related work (large pretraining corpus); not used directly in this paper.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Cited evidence (from Wang et al.) that foundation models can perform well on pretraining distributions but may struggle on out-of-distribution doped systems and suffer catastrophic forgetting upon fine-tuning; used to motivate need for methods with modest dataset requirements that still transfer.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Mentioned as background: foundation models are data-hungry to build but may still fail on specific doped systems without fine-tuning; this paper positions MLH as an alternative with smaller data needs.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: No protocol in this work (this is a literature mention).

extracted_data.performance_metrics: Not reported in this paper (citation summarizes qualitative failure modes).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Not relevant here.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Cited claim: foundation-interatomic-potential pretraining can lead to good performance on in-distribution tasks but poor cross-chemistry transfer and catastrophic forgetting upon fine-tuning.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Cited limitation: foundation model MACE-MP struggled with doped perovskites and fine-tuning caused catastrophic forgetting on original dataset; motivates caution when applying pretrained potentials to defects/dopants.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Implying that (a) fine-tuning must be done carefully to avoid catastrophic forgetting, and (b) alternative strategies (e.g., MLH) that need smaller, defect-focused datasets may be useful for defect calculations.

extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects (single-atom vacancy/dopant examples cited in the literature).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Not specifically addressed in the citation summary used here; referenced for energy transferability issues.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energies and related total-energy predictions with MLIPs.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Local MLIP trained on small-supercell defect configurations (general MLIP warning)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Local per-atom energy decomposition MLIPs trained only on defect-containing small supercells can mis-estimate host contributions leading to systematic errors in larger cells.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Training on full defect supercells only (no host-only examples) produces host-energy bias; recommendation to include host supercells.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not detailed in this paper (this is a citation summarizing the finding).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: General MLIP classes (message-passing/pairwise) in cited literature; specifics not reproduced here.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Not relevant to this citation.

extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Direct empirical observation cited: MLIP trained on Te_1^0 in small CdTe supercells exhibited systematic energy errors in larger supercells; authors of cited work suggested including host supercells in training.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Cited work implies that adding host data is essential for correct transfer, increasing data requirements for MLIPs.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Not detailed in this paper (citation used as motivation).

extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Cited limitation: poor transfer of MLIPs trained only on defect small-supercell data to larger supercells without host data included.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include both host and defect supercells in MLIP training to avoid systematic host-energy biases and improve transferability (recommendation from cited work).

extracted_data.name_full: M3GNet universal graph machine-learning force field (fine-tuned on defect configurations)
extracted_data.brief_description: A universal graph-based machine-learning interatomic potential (M3GNet) pre-trained on bulk crystal data and fine-tuned here on a curated defect dataset to serve as a surrogate PES for rapid defect geometry exploration and structure searching.
extracted_data.citation_title: A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to neutral cation vacancies in a diverse set of metal chalcogenides/ mixed chalcogen/halide hosts (50 hosts total) and to CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} pseudo-binary alloys; multiple hosts and alloys evaluated.
extracted_data.defect_types: Neutral point defects — specifically neutral cation vacancies (V_cation^0). No charged defects, interstitials, substitutional dopants, antisites, Frenkel pairs or explicit complexes were modeled in experiments (defect complexes not included).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Neutral-only in experiments (authors explicitly state universal MLFFs limited in describing charge); charge states not modeled. Paper discusses possible encodings: net charge as graph global attribute and use of 4th-generation MLFFs with explicit atomic charges, but these were not used here.
extracted_data.target_properties: Qualitative potential energy surface (PES) mapping: predicted relaxed geometries (local minima), relative energies of defect configurations (energy ordering), used to select candidates for DFT relaxation; indirectly accelerates calculations of formation energies once ground-state geometries are found. The work did not compute charge transition levels, migration barriers, or phonon thermal conductivity directly with the MLFF as final predictions (but discusses possible future applications).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-fine-tuned universal graph MLFF (M3GNet) with weighted-atom readout
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Graph constructed from the full supercell (periodic) using M3GNet graph featurisation: nodes = atoms with elemental embeddings from pretraining, edges encode radial (pair) and explicit 3-body information within cutoffs; model uses radial and 3-body cutoffs of 5 Å and 4 Å respectively and a weighted atom readout function. Model outputs energies, forces and stresses and is trained with a combined loss on energy/force/stress (weights 1/1/0.1).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full supercell graph representation (universal MLFF) fine-tuned on defect-containing supercells — not a reduced defect-only subgraph; however SOAP descriptors (see another entity) were computed only for the defect site to identify distinct minima.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Graph cutoffs: radial cutoff 5 Å; 3-body cutoff 4 Å. Species encoded implicitly in node features initialized from the pre-trained bulk model (atomic/effective embeddings from M3GNet pretraining). Readout: weighted atom readout. Training loss: MSE on energies and forces (weights 1,1) and stresses (weight 0.1).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: M3GNet (universal graph deep learning interatomic potential). The paper also benchmarks architectures (CHGNet, MACE) during model selection but selects M3GNet. Key settings used: radial cutoff = 5 Å, 3-body cutoff = 4 Å, weighted atom readout, batch size 4, exponential LR scheduler (initial 5e-4).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Yes — model initialized from pre-trained M3GNet bulk model weights (trained on Materials Project bulk/formation-energy data); transfer learning/fine-tuning strategy used (bulk -> defect). The Materials Project/bulk pretraining provided embeddings and chemistry knowledge (e.g., Se–Te bonds) that improved generalisation to mixed alloys.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: First-principles (DFT HSE06) dataset created by authors: 132 neutral cation vacancies across 50 host compositions (25 elements, 6 space groups). After cleaning and frame selection: training = 11,955 configurations (63%), validation = 2,100 (11%), test = 4,830 (26%). For the alloy application a custom training set: ~1,420 frames (trained on CdTe and CdSe end-members) and validation ~140 frames; test on mixed CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} compositions.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Quantified: on a robust test set (13 unseen compositions, 32 defects) the fine-tuned M3GNet surrogate + DFT workflow correctly identified the DFT ground state in 88% of test defects and reduced required DFT calculations by 73% (acceleration factor ≈13). For the chalcohalide family (more chemically similar systems) the model identified the correct ground state for all test cases (100%). For CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} alloys: training on end-members and testing on mixed alloys resulted in correct ground-state identification for all defects and found more favourable ground states for 70% of defects (mean energy lowering −0.4 eV).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Model trained with ~12k configurations (fine-tuned from pre-trained bulk weights) — authors show fine-tuning is effective and that including bulk structures with defects improves performance vs defect-only training. They compared sampling strategies (MS: 10 evenly spaced frames per relaxation vs DIRECT) and found MS performed better at similar dataset sizes; DIRECT only wins when its dataset is larger. Model training time: 30 epochs (~5.3 hours) for full dataset; alloy model trained for 80 epochs. The surrogate approach reduced the number of expensive DFT relaxations by 73% in structure searching.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Composition-wise split: dataset split by composition into training (68% of defects/compositions), validation (5%) and test (27%) to evaluate out-of-distribution generalisation to unseen compositions; validation augmented with 5% of configurations from training systems. For alloys they trained on end-members and tested on mixed (out-of-sample) compositions; also a family-specific split for chalcohalides was tested. Spearman correlations computed per-defect and averaged. SOAP-based clustering / t-SNE used for manifold visualisation (M3GNet embeddings).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Benchmarks: compared model architectures (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE), training on defect-only vs defect+bulk (defect+bulk improved performance), and sampling strategies (MS vs DIRECT). Ablation outcomes: defect+bulk training improved errors; MS sampling (evenly spaced frames) outperformed DIRECT for similar dataset sizes; pretraining (bulk -> defect) yielded transfer benefits (enabled detection of Te–Se bonds not present in defect training but present in bulk pretraining). Details in SI.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Energy prediction metrics: MAE_absolute_energy (test) = 31.2 meV/atom; MAE_relative_energy (test, energies relative to defect ground state) = 11.3 meV/atom; for configurations <≈5 eV above minimum: MAE = 3.6 meV/atom (≈0.29 eV for an 80-atom supercell). Spearman rank correlation (ρ) on test set averaged across defects = 0.72. Structure-search success: MLFF+DFT identified correct DFT ground state in 88% of test defects; accelerated structure searching by factor ≈13; reduced DFT relaxations by 73%. For alloy application: found better ground states in 70% of defects with mean lowering −0.4 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Paper does not compute phonon scattering or lattice thermal conductivity degradation directly. It cites related work showing MLFFs can be used for phonon properties and defect phonon studies (e.g., Shimizu et al.) and suggests the surrogate approach could enable calculation of defect formation entropies and accelerate migration/phonon studies, but provides no direct ML prediction of scattering rates or kappa degradation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue that learning plausible defect reconstruction motifs (e.g., anion–anion dimerisation) across related chemistries is sufficient to qualitatively capture low-energy regions of defect PESs; pretraining on bulk databases encodes general chemical motifs (e.g., Se–Te bonding) that aid transfer to unseen local environments; graph-based universal MLFFs capture local bonding and many-body interactions needed to predict structural reconstructions; SOAP defect-site fingerprints effectively distinguish distinct local minima.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Model limited to neutral cation vacancies in metal chalcogenides (no charged defects). Performance drops for out-of-distribution chemistries (ρ lower than bulk-only MLFFs) and for hosts with very complex PESs (e.g., V_Sn in Li4SnS4) — ~12% of test defects where MLFF ground state differed from DFT; errors for absolute energies sizeable though relative energy errors are smaller. MLFF cannot describe net charge transfer/charged states in current setup; sensitivity to sampling strategy (DIRECT biased to high-distortion frames) and to training data composition; SOAP/MLFF based identification may miss basins if training biased.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use a pretrained universal MLFF (bulk-trained) and fine-tune on defect configurations (include bulk frames to improve stability); sample ionic relaxation trajectories with evenly spaced frames (MS) for small training budgets; use SOAP fingerprints of the defect site (r=5 Å, n_max=10, l_max=10, σ=1.0 Å used here) to cluster/identify unique minima; split dataset by composition to assess cross-chemistry transfer; for alloys train on end members if possible and apply to mixed compositions; when addressing charge states either train separate MLFFs per charge state, encode net charge as a global graph attribute, or use 4th-generation MLFFs with explicit atomic charges; after MLFF-driven search refine chosen candidates with higher-accuracy DFT (tighter thresholds, SOC where needed).

extracted_data.name_full: Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) descriptor computed for the defect site
extracted_data.brief_description: A local rotationally- and translationally-invariant density-based descriptor computed on the defect neighbourhood used to fingerprint/cluster MLFF-relaxed structures and to identify distinct local minima of the defect PES.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to the same set of defect-containing supercells (metal chalcogenides and alloys) to characterise local defect motifs.
extracted_data.defect_types: Used for neutral point defect configurations (cation vacancies) to fingerprint local minima; not used for charged defects or complexes here.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: SOAP itself is geometry-based and charge-agnostic; no explicit charge features were included in SOAP fingerprints in this study.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used to identify and cluster distinct local minima of defect relaxation trajectories (helps select unique candidate structures for DFT refinement) — not used to directly predict scalar properties like energy or transition levels (although used in combination with MLFF energies to find minima).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-site SOAP fingerprint
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: SOAP computed on the local neighbourhood centred on the defect site (local cutoff r = 5 Å), expanded in radial basis and spherical harmonics (n_max = 10, l_max = 10) with Gaussian smearing σ = 1.0 Å; cosine distance between SOAP vectors used to group minima.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered: SOAP computed for the defect site/local neighbourhood only (not full-cell SOAP).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Parameters reported: local cutoff r = 5 Å; n_max = 10 radial basis functions; l_max = 10 spherical harmonics; σ = 1.0 Å Gaussian smearing. Species included implicitly via atomic densities in SOAP expansion (standard SOAP, species-aware). Descriptor is invariant to rotations/translations and permutation of expansion coefficients handled by SOAP kernel/cosine distance.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Applied to the MLFF-relaxed structures from the DFT-generated dataset (tens of thousands of configurations), used to identify unique minima for each defect trajectory.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: SOAP successfully discriminated minima across diverse hosts and was robust enough to identify different motifs (e.g., dimers vs non-dimer states) across compositions; used to select unique MLFF minima for DFT relaxation in the test set.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: SOAP-based clustering helped reduce the number of DFT relaxations by selecting unique candidates, contributing to the reported 73% reduction in DFT calculations when using MLFF+SOAP selection vs a full DFT-only search.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Cosine distance between SOAP vectors of the defect site used to identify distinct minima; thresholding/clustering details in SI (SOAP parameters as above).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Authors report SOAP of defect site was more robust than energy- or RMSD-based grouping: energy-based grouping can miss minima with similar energies; RMSD sensitive to changes far from defect. SOAP chosen as the preferred fingerprint for motif identification.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Not reported as a predictive metric; used qualitatively to identify distinct minima. Its use contributed to success rates (88% correct ground-state identification) by enabling selection of representative distinct MLFF minima for DFT refinement.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: SOAP is geometric and not by itself predictive of phonon scattering; authors do not use SOAP outputs for phonon/thermal transport tasks here.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: SOAP of defect site captures local bonding rearrangements (e.g., anion–anion dimer formation) and is therefore effective to distinguish reconstruction motifs which are the key structural feature controlling defect energetics.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: SOAP depends on chosen cutoff and expansion parameters; may not capture long-range strain/electrostatic differences; can fail if two minima have very similar local atomic densities but different long-range relaxations.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Compute SOAP centred on defect site with r ≈ 5 Å for typical point-defect supercells; use relatively high n_max and l_max (authors used 10/10) and σ ≈ 1.0 Å; use SOAP cosine-distance clustering to select a small set of distinct candidate minima for high-accuracy DFT refinement rather than energy/RMSD thresholds.

extracted_data.name_full: Pretrained M3GNet / bulk-derived graph feature vectors (Materials Project pretraining) used as embeddings
extracted_data.brief_description: Feature vectors obtained from a universal ML graph model pre-trained on bulk formation-energy data (Materials Project) that are used to represent defect configurations for dimensionality reduction (t-SNE) and to visualise/assess chemical similarity across defect structures.
extracted_data.citation_title: A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table
extracted_data.material_systems: Used to visualise and compare defect configurations across the diverse set of metal chalcogenides and mixed-anion hosts in the dataset.
extracted_data.defect_types: Applied to neutral vacancy-containing configurations (same dataset).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Embeddings are bulk-trained and not charge-aware in the defect application described; charge is not encoded in the t-SNE visualisations.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used for unsupervised analysis / visualization (t-SNE) of structural similarity and clustering by host composition; not used directly as a predictive descriptor for energies in this study.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Bulk-pretrained M3GNet embeddings (used as fixed feature vectors)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Extracted feature vectors from M3GNet (trained on bulk formation energies of Materials Project) for each defect configuration; vectors dimensionally reduced via t-SNE for visualization; similar chemical systems cluster together.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-configuration embeddings (M3GNet outputs on the defect-containing supercell) rather than defect-only centerings for the t-SNE visualization.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not applicable beyond the M3GNet graph featurisation details (radial/3-body cutoffs as above).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Used M3GNet pretrained model to generate feature vectors.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Yes — M3GNet trained on Materials Project bulk formation-energy data; embeddings transferred without further modification for t-SNE analysis.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Applied to the entire DFT relaxation dataset (visualization used 10 evenly spaced frames per trajectory for clarity).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: The pretrained bulk embeddings contained chemical motifs (e.g., Se–Te bonding) that enabled the fine-tuned MLFF to generalise to bond types absent in the defect-only training set (e.g., Te–Se bonds appearing in alloys), supporting the benefit of pretraining.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Pretraining allowed fine-tuning with fewer defect-specific frames to achieve qualitative PES mapping and transfer to alloys; exact sample-efficiency curves not shown but qualitative evidence provided (successful alloy transfer).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: t-SNE projection of M3GNet feature vectors; 10 evenly spaced steps selected from each relaxation for plotting and clustering.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Authors compared fine-tuning from pretrained bulk model vs training from scratch on defect-only data (defect+bulk fine-tuning gave improved performance).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Not predictive metrics; used qualitatively to show chemical clustering of configurations. Indirect evidence of benefit: model could predict Te–Se bond formation in alloys despite absence in defect training because bulk pretraining included such bonding motifs.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: None direct; embeddings used purely for geometry/chemical similarity visualisation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Pretrained bulk embeddings encode common bonding motifs across chemistries that can be re-used (transfer learning) to improve MLFF generalisation to unseen local defect environments.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Bulk pretraining cannot encode defect-charge-specific physics; embeddings may not capture rare local motifs absent from bulk training data.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: When building defect ML surrogates, initialize from a bulk-pretrained universal MLFF (e.g., M3GNet) to capture general chemical motifs and accelerate/facilitate transfer to unseen defect environments; complement with defect-specific frames for fine-tuning.

extracted_data.name_full: Graph global-attribute charge encoding and fourth-generation MLFFs with explicit atomic charges (mentioned strategies)
extracted_data.brief_description: Strategies discussed to handle charged defects: (1) encode the net defect charge as a graph-level/global attribute to condition the ML model; (2) use fourth-generation MLFFs that explicitly predict/contain atomic charges to account for nonlocal charge transfer and electrostatics.
extracted_data.material_systems: Discussed generally as applicable to systems where charged defects are important (e.g., semiconductors with charged vacancies); not applied experimentally in this work.
extracted_data.defect_types: Charged point defects and different defect charge states (general discussion).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Described options: encoding net charge as graph global attribute (citing Shimizu et al. 2022) and using 4th-gen MLFFs that include atomic charges (citing Ko et al. Acc. Chem. Res. 2021) — neither implemented in the experiments.
extracted_data.target_properties: Intended to enable MLFFs to model PES/structures for different charge states, and hence enable charged-defect geometry searches and properties dependent on charge (formation energies, transition levels).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Charge-conditional graph attribute or explicit-charge MLFFs (conceptual)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Encode global net charge as a scalar attribute of the graph to condition predictions, or employ MLFFs that maintain per-atom partial charges as internal degrees of freedom that can change with environment to model nonlocal charge transfer and electrostatics.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Would be full-supercell graphs with additional global/atomic charge features; could also be paired with defect-centered local descriptors.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not implemented here; discussed references indicate charge treated as extra feature channels or via self-consistent charge models inside MLFFs.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Cites Shimizu et al. (neural network potentials for charged defects) and Ko et al. (general-purpose ML potentials capturing nonlocal charge transfer) as examples — architectures not implemented in this study.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Not used; authors suggest these as avenues for future improvement.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Not present in current dataset (only neutral states included). Authors note need for dataset and models that include charged-relaxation data to implement these strategies.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: No experimental evidence in this paper; the approach is suggested as a remedy for the current limitation (neutral-only) based on cited literature.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Not provided here; authors suggest separate models per charge-state or charge-conditional encodings could be used but require charge-state-specific data.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Not applied; suggested protocols include training separate PES models per charge state or encoding charge as a graph global attribute.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Not performed in this work.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Mentioned that charge-aware MLFFs (and MLFFs in general) can enable phonon property calculations and defect formation entropies (citing Shimizu et al.), but no direct phonon transport predictions are presented here.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue that charged defects require explicit charge-aware modelling because different charge states have distinct PESs and structural configurations; global-charge attributes or explicit atomic-charge MLFFs would better capture these effects.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Current surrogate approach cannot handle charged-defect PESs; authors explicitly list this as a limitation and propose the above remedies.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: To model charged defects, either (a) train separate MLFFs per charge state, (b) encode net charge as a global graph attribute, or (c) adopt 4th-generation MLFFs that predict atomic charges (and train on charge-state-resolved data). Also recommend on-the-fly fine-tuning during relaxations to improve robustness.

extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Not discussed in this paper's use-case; referenced as related prior art without detail on charge handling.
extracted_data.target_properties: Literature-cited approach aimed at predicting defect properties (formation energies, etc.) — not applied here.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Sparse defect representation (descriptor-based)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Mentioned as a descriptor/sparse-representation approach to featurise defects (paper cited); details not used or reproduced here.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Likely defect-centered (typical of sparse defect representations) — not specified or used in current experiments.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not provided in this paper; readers referred to the cited work.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Cited as related work on 2D defects; not part of the authors' dataset.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Not applicable here; referenced as part of literature motivating different representation strategies.

extracted_data.name_full: Atom-centered local energy contributions (E = sum_i E_i)
extracted_data.brief_description: Standard MLIP featurization where total energy is modeled as a sum of learnable per-atom contributions that depend on the positions and species of neighbors; used as the base representation in the tested uMLIPs.
extracted_data.material_systems: Wide range of crystalline materials studied in the paper: 29 elements and binaries for surfaces (147 slabs), 32 chemical systems for point defects (~129–134 defects), Ca_xMg_{2-x}O_2 solid-solution (many orderings), 229 phonon materials from PhononDB, ~470 Mg-ion migration paths across 110 structures, 1000 WBM compounds for OOD sampling. Multiple hosts used (metals, oxides, halides, sulfides, Li-containing compounds, etc.).
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects benchmarked include vacancies, interstitials, and antisites (substitutional); defect complexes are not reported as included.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Not explicitly represented for charged point defects in the defect benchmarks; defect energies referenced to elemental chemical potentials; overall approach in benchmarks appears neutral/no explicit charged-defect pipeline.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation/point defect energies, relaxed defect structure energies (referenced to bulk), migration barriers (ion migration paths), surface energies, phonon frequencies (vibrational modes) — all obtained via MLIP energy/force predictions.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Atom-centered local descriptor / energy partitioning
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Each atomic contribution E_i is a learnable function of the local neighborhood (positions and chemical identities of neighbors). The MLIP sums atomic contributions to predict total energy; forces derived by analytic differentiation. Descriptor implementation is via the underlying model (graph/GNN or other) but conceptually atom-centered.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full supercell / atom-local representation: models operate on the full atomic configuration (supercell) and compute per-atom contributions; no specialized defect-centered subgraph or delta-to-pristine encoding is described for the defect benchmarks.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Paper states importance of informative local descriptors with proper translational/rotational symmetries; mentions use of graph representations, high-order interactions, preservation of SE(3)/E(3)-equivariance (tensor products based on spherical harmonics), Fourier basis, and Cartesian atomic density expansions in general MLIP literature. Specific neighbor cutoff values for defect calculations are not reported in the main text (ionic relaxations converged to 0.05 eV/Å).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Not specific to this entry (see separate GNN entry), but atom-centered partitioning is implemented by the used uMLIPs (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE) which are graph or equivariant-graph based.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: All three uMLIPs used are pretrained foundation potentials (M3GNet / CHGNet / MACE) trained on Materials Project-derived datasets; the atom-centered energy partitioning is the basis for these pretrained potentials which are then fine-tuned.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretraining datasets: MPF (Materials Project formation?) 188.3k structures for M3GNet; MPtrj 1.58M structures for CHGNet and MACE (Table I). Defect benchmarks: 129–134 point defects across 32 systems; DFT labels used for defect, surface, phonon, and migration benchmarks. High-energy OOD samples: 1000 WBM compounds with 10 high-temperature MD samples each.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Extensive OOD testing: uMLIPs pretrained on near-equilibrium Materials Project trajectories systematically underpredict energies/forces for OOD states (surfaces, defects, migration barriers, phonons); >90% of 1000 WBM compounds show PES softening (softening scale <1). Evidence indicates limited transfer to high-energy/low-symmetry defect environments without fine-tuning.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Fine-tuning pretrained uMLIP (CHGNet) with a single high-energy DFT label via a scalar linear correction greatly reduces systematic error (e.g., CHGNet force MAE improved from 0.190 eV/Å to 0.166 eV/Å with 1 configuration). Full parameter fine-tuning with 10 DFT structures reduced force MAE to 0.125 eV/Å. The paper argues that pretrained atom-centered models provide data-efficient starting points because many errors are systematic.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Benchmarks use DFT reference calculations; for high-energy sampling 20 ps, 1000 K MD with CHGNet produced samples (NVT). For fine-tuning CHGNet: train/val 9:1, test set of 100 DFT structures reserved; losses include energy/force/stress with 0.1-100-0.1 weighting. For defect and surface relaxations, ionic relaxations converged to 0.05 eV/Å. OOD evaluation explicitly uses compounds not in pretraining datasets (WBM substitutions).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Comparisons across three uMLIPs of differing architectures/sizes (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE) and model-size variants (CHGNet-matgl and M3GNet-matgl in supplement). Ablation-style experiment: freezing all weights and training only a scalar multiplicative energy layer (linear correction) vs full fine-tuning; the scalar correction with one label recovers much systematic error.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Representative numbers reported: surface energies MAE (MACE) = 0.032 eV/Å; ion migration barrier MAEs: MACE = 0.30 eV, CHGNet = 0.39 eV, M3GNet = 0.49 eV; force MAEs (high-energy MD sampling) pre-trained M3GNet/CHGNet/MACE = 0.220 / 0.190 / 0.176 eV/Å and linear-corrected cMAEs = 0.184 / 0.162 / 0.155 eV/Å. CHGNet fine-tune: 1-structure scalar correction MAE = 0.166 eV/Å (from 0.190), full fine-tune with 10 structures MAE = 0.125 eV/Å. >90% of 229 phonon materials show reduced max frequency relative to DFT (softening).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: MLIPs are used to compute harmonic phonons (finite displacement) and show systematic reduction of vibrational frequencies (phonon softening) compared to DFT across many materials; this implies softened force constants which would affect phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity, but the paper does not directly predict phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity degradation or perform BTE/relaxation-time calculations with MLIPs.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors attribute the systematic underprediction (PES softening) to biased pretraining data that sample predominantly near-equilibrium ionic relaxation trajectories, providing poor coverage of high-energy curvature/force gradients; larger model capacity reduces softening somewhat; the systematic nature of errors is why a simple global scalar correction is effective and why fine-tuning is data-efficient.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Universal softening (energy/force underprediction) for OOD states including surfaces, undercoordinated defect sites, migration transition states, and phonons; poor extrapolation to high-energy curvature regions; lack of explicit handling for charged defects/charge states in defect benchmarks; non-analytic phonon corrections unavailable because MLIPs lack electronic Born charges; dataset bias towards near-equilibrium configurations limits generalization.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include a small number of high-energy/out-of-distribution DFT samples in fine-tuning to correct systematic softening (even a single force label can help via a scalar correction); construct pretraining datasets with broader PES sampling (include high-energy states, strained configurations); consider larger model capacity or enhanced sampling strategies to reduce softening; use hybrid MLIP-DFT workflows for properties requiring electronic quantities (e.g., Born charges for NAC).

extracted_data.name_full: Graph-based representations with SE(3)/E(3)-equivariance (equivariant message-passing networks)
extracted_data.brief_description: Use of graph representations and E(3)/SE(3)-equivariant message-passing or high-order interaction blocks (spherical harmonics/tensor products, Fourier basis) to encode atomic neighborhoods and preserve rotational/translational symmetries; underlying architecture for the uMLIPs tested (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE).
extracted_data.material_systems: Same broad set as above (surfaces, defects across dozens of chemistries, phonons, migration paths).
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies, interstitials, antisites (as used in defect benchmarks); no explicit defect-complex graph-specific treatment reported.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Equivariance/graph encoding itself does not provide charged-defect handling; charge-aware variants exist (CHGNet includes charge information) but the defect benchmarks here do not explicitly model charged defect states.
extracted_data.target_properties: Energetics, forces (used to compute relaxed defect energies, migration barriers, phonons), phonon spectra (via forces), and derived material properties.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Graph / E(3)/SE(3)-equivariant message-passing networks
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Crystals represented as graphs (atoms as nodes, bonds/neighborhood as edges) with message passing that respects rotational and translational symmetries; higher-order interactions captured via equivariant tensor products (spherical harmonics) or other basis (Fourier, atomic density expansion). Edge features and multi-body interactions encode local geometry and species.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-structure graph applied to defective supercells; no dedicated defect-centered subgraph or delta-to-pristine encoding described in experiments — the entire supercell graph is fed to the uMLIP.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Paper references SE(3)/E(3)-equivariance with tensor products based on spherical harmonics, Fourier basis, Cartesian atomic density expansion; species information included (chemical identity) and in CHGNet additional charge information can be included; exact neighbor cutoffs and angular/radial basis details are model-dependent and not enumerated in the main text.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Specific uMLIPs used: M3GNet (graph deep learning interatomic potential), CHGNet (charge-informed graph NN), MACE (equivariant architecture). The paper notes MACE is larger (~4.69M params) and E(3)-equivariant approaches and tensor-product based equivariant blocks are used in modern MLIPs. Edge features and interaction blocks are part of these models but exact block counts/hyperparams not listed.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: All models are pretrained graph/equivariant GNNs on Materials Project-derived datasets (MPF, MPtrj); the pretrained graph weights act as foundation models for downstream fine-tuning on defect/surface/phonon tasks.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretraining: MPF (188.3k) for M3GNet, MPtrj (1.58M) for CHGNet and MACE. Downstream datasets: DFT-relaxed defective supercells (129–134 defects), 147 surfaces, 229 phonon materials, 470 migration pathways. OOD WBM sampling: 1000 compounds × 10 samples each.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: OOD benchmarks show systematic underprediction across graph/equivariant architectures; MACE (largest equivariant model) performs better and shows less softening, suggesting better transfer with larger equivariant models but still exhibits systematic errors in many OOD scenarios. Softening scale distributions reported for 1000 WBM compounds show <1 for >90% of cases across models.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Pretrained graph/equivariant models fine-tuned with very small datasets (1 label via scalar correction; 10 structures for full fine-tune) show substantial error reduction, demonstrating data-efficiency of foundation graph models relative to training from scratch (supplementary comparisons).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Pretrained graph models tested on DFT reference data across multiple OOD tasks; for fine-tuning CHGNet used energy/force/stress MSE loss weights 0.1/100/0.1, Adam optimizer, lr schedule and early stopping on validation force MAE; held-out test sets of DFT MD structures used.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Direct comparisons between three different graph/equivariant models (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE), and model-size variants (CHGNet-matgl, M3GNet-matgl) show performance and softening differences; ablation of only training a scalar linear layer vs full fine-tuning quantifies how much of the error is systematic and correctable with minimal change.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: See atom-centered entry for numbers. Equivariant graph model (MACE) had best overall metrics: migration barrier MAE 0.30 eV; force MAE 0.176 eV/Å pre-fine-tune. CHGNet (charge-informed graph) and M3GNet larger/smaller differences reported.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Graph/equivariant GNNs used to produce forces for phonon finite-displacement calculations; predicted phonon bands systematically softened (lower frequencies) relative to DFT. No direct thermal-conductivity (kappa) or scattering-rate calculations performed using the ML-derived force constants in this work.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Equivariance and expressive graph architectures improve ability to capture PES curvature; larger equivariant models reduce softening, indicating architecture and capacity matter; nonetheless, dataset sampling matters greatly for extrapolating to defect/high-energy regions.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Even equivariant graph models trained on near-equilibrium data underpredict forces/curvature for defect and high-energy configurations; lack of explicit treatment for long-range electrostatics and electronic-response in many graph models limits ability to model charged defects and non-analytic phonon corrections.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use pretrained equivariant graph models as foundations and include targeted high-energy/defect-like samples for fine-tuning; consider increasing model capacity and/or dataset PES diversity; for properties needing electronic response (Born charges, NAC) use hybrid MLIP-DFT corrections.

extracted_data.name_full: Charge-informed graph neural network embedding (CHGNet)
extracted_data.brief_description: CHGNet is a pretrained universal MLIP that explicitly incorporates charge information into the atomistic representation to improve prediction accuracy for charged/ionic systems; used in this paper as one of three uMLIPs benchmarked.
extracted_data.material_systems: Benchmarks include oxides, halides, sulfides, metallic compounds, Li-containing compounds and others; CHGNet was evaluated on the same defect/surface/phonon/migration datasets as the other uMLIPs.
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects benchmarked are vacancies, interstitials, antisites (neutral reference used); no explicit charged-defect examples or charge-transition level predictions reported in the benchmarks.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: CHGNet includes charge as part of its representation (paper states incorporation of chemical information such as charge can enhance MLIPs). However, in the defect benchmarks this study did not perform charged-defect formation energy calculations with explicit electron chemical potential/Fermi-level features or background charge corrections; the defect energies were referenced to elemental chemical potentials (neutral references).
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energies (neutral references), surface energies, migration barriers, phonon frequencies and forces.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Charge-aware graph embedding (CHGNet)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Graph-based representation that includes additional chemical information related to charge (charge-informed features/embeddings) alongside atomic coordinates and species; used within the CHGNet pretrained model to produce energies and forces.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Full-supercell graph encoding; no specialized defect-centered subgraph/difference features employed for defect benchmarks reported here.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Species and charge-related information are embedded in node/graph features; model preserves necessary symmetries via the underlying graph/equivariant architecture. Specific cutoffs and basis choices are model-internal and not enumerated in main text.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: CHGNet (v0.3.0) — a charge-informed graph neural network; model size ~412.5K parameters per Table I. Underlying architecture is graph-based and charge-aware.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: CHGNet is used as a pretrained foundation potential (pretrained on MPtrj dataset, 1.58M structures) and evaluated out-of-the-box on OOD tasks; fine-tuned in this work (scalar correction and small-data fine-tuning) to mitigate PES softening.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretraining on MPtrj (1.58M structures). Defect/surface/migration/phonon benchmark datasets described above. Fine-tuning experiments used Li2B3PO8 DFT ab-initio MD (small number of structures: 1 for scalar correction, 10 for small-data full fine-tune).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: CHGNet shows the same systematic PES softening as other uMLIPs on OOD tasks but performs closer to DFT than M3GNet in some energy tasks; fine-tuning with very small data (1–10 structures) substantially improves force MAE, demonstrating transferability via fine-tuning.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Scalar linear correction with one DFT configuration improved CHGNet force MAE from 0.190 to 0.166 eV/Å; full fine-tune with 10 structures reduced MAE to 0.125 eV/Å. These show high data efficiency when fine-tuning a pretrained, charge-aware model.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: CHGNet pretrained weights frozen except scalar layer for the one-label experiment; full fine-tune optimized all parameters with a small dataset (energy/force/stress loss weighting 0.1/100/0.1). Validation-based checkpointing used.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared against M3GNet and MACE (both pretrained) and model-size variants in supplement; ablation by training only scalar multiplicative layer vs full fine-tuning quantified systematic error correction.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: CHGNet migration barrier MAE = 0.39 eV; pre-trained CHGNet force MAE (OOD high-energy sampling) = 0.190 eV/Å; cMAE after linear correction = 0.162 eV/Å; scalar-finetune MAE = 0.166 eV/Å; full fine-tune (10 structures) MAE = 0.125 eV/Å.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: CHGNet predicted phonon spectra show systematic frequency reduction similar to other uMLIPs; no direct thermal conductivity or phonon scattering rate predictions presented. The paper notes non-analytic corrections (Born charges) are unavailable from MLIPs without electronic info, limiting phonon accuracy for polar materials.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Charge-informed embeddings help capture ionic/charge effects in materials, but pretraining data bias still yields PES softening in defect/high-energy regions; fine-tuning can correct systematic scaling errors even in charge-aware models.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: CHGNet, despite charge-aware features, still underpredicts energies/forces in OOD defect/high-energy scenarios; the present work does not demonstrate explicit charged-defect formation energies or charge-state dependent properties with CHGNet; MLIPs lack electronic response variables (e.g., Born charges) necessary for some phonon corrections.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: When applying charge-aware MLIPs to defect problems, include explicit high-energy/defect-state training samples and consider hybrid DFT steps for electronic-response properties; use small-data fine-tuning for rapid correction of systematic errors.

extracted_data.name_full: Pretrained universal MLIPs (foundation potentials) and downstream fine-tuning strategies
extracted_data.brief_description: Use of large, pretrained uMLIPs (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE) trained on Materials Project-derived datasets as foundation models that can be fine-tuned with small amounts of task-specific DFT data to correct systematic PES softening and improve defect-related predictions.
extracted_data.material_systems: Same broad crystalline materials used in the benchmarks; fine-tuning experiments performed on Li2B3PO8 (ab-initio MD) as an example and applied to OOD WBM compounds evaluation.
extracted_data.defect_types: Benchmarks cover point defects (vacancy/interstitial/antisite) and migration transition states; fine-tuning primarily targeted high-energy OOD atomic configurations rather than explicit defect charge-state labels.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Fine-tuning procedure described does not incorporate explicit electron chemical potential or charged-defect labels; scalar correction fine-tunes energy scale only and full fine-tuning uses standard energy/force/stress DFT labels (presumably neutral supercells).
extracted_data.target_properties: Improved energy/force predictions used to calculate defect formation energies (neutral references), migration barriers, surface energies, and phonon frequencies; the fine-tuned potentials reduce MAEs for these downstream tasks.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation-potential pretraining with small-data fine-tuning (including scalar linear correction)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Models are pretrained on large datasets of near-equilibrium ionic relaxation trajectories (Materials Project/MPtrj). Downstream, either (a) a single scalar multiplicative energy layer is trained (all other weights frozen) using one high-energy force label, or (b) full model fine-tuning with small DFT datasets (e.g., 10 structures) is performed to correct systematic errors.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Fine-tuning operates on full-structure labels (energies/forces) from defective or high-energy configurations; no specialized defect-centered delta features are described as part of the fine-tuning.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Pretraining encodes local environments via the chosen uMLIP architecture (graph/equivariant). Fine-tuning updates model parameters to better represent high-energy curvature; scalar correction multiplies predicted energies globally (equivalent to scaling all forces).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Applied to pretrained M3GNet (graph), CHGNet (charge-aware graph), and MACE (equivariant); scalar correction is model-agnostic and implemented as an extra scalar linear layer on top of the energy output.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Explicit use of pretrained foundation potentials: M3GNet (MPF, 188.3k), CHGNet (MPtrj, 1.58M), MACE (MPtrj, 1.58M). The pretrained weights serve as the starting point for fine-tuning experiments.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretraining: large datasets described above. Fine-tuning datasets: extremely small examples shown — single high-energy configuration (1 force label) and 10-structure small datasets from DFT ab-initio MD (Li2B3PO8). OOD evaluation: 1000 WBM compounds sampled at 1000 K (10 states each).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Fine-tuning foundation models with minimal data substantially improves OOD force predictions across sampled materials; the scalar correction brought the CHGNet softening scale closer to 1 (from 0.859 to 0.965) and reduced MAE. This supports transferability via small-data fine-tuning rather than zero-shot transfer.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Numeric examples: single-label scalar fine-tune reduced CHGNet MAE from 0.190 to 0.166 eV/Å; ten-structure full fine-tune reduced MAE to 0.125 eV/Å. Authors argue a large fraction of pretrained errors are systematic and thus correctable with few labels.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Scalar correction: freeze all pretrained weights, add scalar linear multipler initialized to 1, train on a single high-energy force label. Full fine-tune: optimize all parameters on small DFT datasets with energy/force/stress loss weighting and validation-based checkpointing. Test sets withheld (e.g., 100 structures reserved).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Baseline is pretrained model without fine-tuning. Ablation: scalar-only fine-tune (1 parameter) vs full fine-tune (all parameters) demonstrates that most systematic scaling error can be removed by a single scalar, but further MAE reductions come from full fine-tuning with more labels. Comparisons to training from scratch (supplement) show pretrained fine-tuning is more data-efficient.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: See entries above: CHGNet example numbers (0.190 → 0.166 eV/Å with scalar correction; →0.125 eV/Å with 10-structure full fine-tune); cMAE reductions for all three uMLIPs: M3GNet/CHGNet/MACE cMAEs 0.184 / 0.162 / 0.155 eV/Å (from 0.220 / 0.190 / 0.176).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Fine-tuning corrects force magnitudes and PES curvature, yielding phonon frequencies closer to DFT and thus could improve MLIP-derived phonon properties; however, the paper does not perform direct lattice thermal conductivity calculations or phonon-scattering-rate predictions post fine-tuning.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Because pretrained uMLIPs are biased toward near-equilibrium configurations, a large fraction of their errors are systematic (global curvature/scale); therefore small-data fine-tuning can efficiently correct these systematic components (hence foundation models are data-efficient).
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Scalar correction is a global remedy and may not fix non-linear or chemistry-specific errors; fine-tuning requires at least targeted DFT labels from the relevant OOD regions; foundation models still limited by pretraining dataset bias and absence of electronic response descriptors for charged-defect/phonon NAC corrections.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: For defect/high-energy applications start from a pretrained uMLIP and include a few targeted high-energy/defect DFT samples for fine-tuning (even a single force label can significantly reduce systematic softening); prefer small full-parameter fine-tuning when more labels are available; construct pretraining datasets with better PES coverage for next-generation foundation models.

extracted_data.name_full: Single-parameter scalar energy scaling (linear correction) for MLIP fine-tuning
extracted_data.brief_description: A minimal fine-tuning strategy adding a single scalar multiplicative layer on the MLIP energy output (E_corr = c * MLIP) to correct systematic underprediction of PES curvature and forces; can be trained with a single force label to rotate force parity distribution back toward unity slope.
extracted_data.material_systems: Demonstrated on high-energy OOD MD samples of Li2B3PO8 and statistically evaluated over 1000 WBM compounds; applied to uMLIPs (CHGNet, M3GNet, MACE) in benchmarks.
extracted_data.defect_types: Used to correct systematic force/energy errors relevant for defects, surfaces and migration barriers generally; not a defect-specific featurization but a fine-tuning trick applicable to defect calculations.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Does not introduce charge awareness; purely a scalar correction to predicted energies/forces irrespective of charge state.
extracted_data.target_properties: Improves force predictions (MAE), which in turn improves derived properties such as migration barrier height, phonon frequencies, and defect/surface energies indirectly by correcting PES curvature scale.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Scalar multiplicative energy correction (single-parameter fine-tune)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Add a scalar linear layer multiplicative factor c to the MLIP predicted energy: E_corr = c * MLIP(...). Since forces are gradients, f_corr = c * f_MLIP. Fit c by minimizing MSE on a small set (even a single force component suffices) to counteract systematic underprediction (softening).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Applies globally to full-supercell MLIP predictions; does not require defect-centered descriptors or pristine references.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: No change to local descriptors; the scalar corrects output energy scale globally across all local-environment encodings.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Model-agnostic; implemented on top of CHGNet in experiments (all other parameters frozen during scalar training).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Designed specifically as a low-cost fine-tuning step for pretrained foundation MLIPs to correct systematic scale errors with minimal data/parameter updates.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Demonstrated with 1 DFT high-energy configuration (single force component) and evaluated across 1000 WBM compounds; also compared to 10-structure full fine-tune.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Scalar correction trained on one configuration from Li2B3PO8 shifted CHGNet softening scale from 0.859 → 0.965 and reduced force MAE (0.190 → 0.166 eV/Å) on withheld test OOD states from the same material; distributionally across WBM compounds cMAE indicates meaningful lower-bound error reduction potential.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: One-parameter correction trained on a single force label yields measurable MAE reduction (example above). Authors present cMAE distributions showing ~15% typical error reduction achievable with such a linear correction.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Scalar layer initialized at 1.0; all other model parameters frozen; trained on one DFT configuration (or last-epoch for 1-structure case) and evaluated on withheld high-energy OOD samples. Larger fine-tuning (10 structures) used full-parameter optimization for comparison.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Baseline: pretrained model without correction. Ablation: single-parameter correction vs full fine-tune. Full fine-tune yields further MAE decreases beyond scalar correction (e.g., CHGNet: scalar MAE 0.166 eV/Å; full fine-tune with 10 structures MAE 0.125 eV/Å).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Example numeric results: CHGNet pre-trained force MAE 0.190 eV/Å → scalar-corrected MAE 0.166 eV/Å (softening scale from 0.859 to 0.965). cMAE reductions across 1000 WBM compounds ~15% typical improvement reported.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Because scalar correction scales forces, it directly affects phonon force-constant magnitudes and thus phonon frequencies; scalar correction moves phonon spectra closer to DFT by restoring PES curvature scale, but paper does not compute thermal conductivity consequences explicitly.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: A large fraction of pretraining error is systematic multiplicative bias in PES curvature (softening); a global scalar corrects this dominant mode of error efficiently, explaining data-efficient fine-tuning benefits of foundation models.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Scalar correction only remedies global multiplicative bias and cannot correct spatially or chemically local systematic errors or non-linear discrepancies; if errors vary strongly by chemistry, local environment, or defect type, scalar may not suffice; must still supply at least one relevant high-energy label from the OOD regime of interest.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use scalar multiplicative correction as a first, very low-cost fine-tuning step when applying pretrained MLIPs to defect/high-energy tasks; follow with small full-parameter fine-tuning if residual errors remain; choose training label(s) representative of the OOD regimes (defect, migration TS, strained states).
