extracted_data.name_full: Hand-crafted physical and chemical descriptors for oxide vacancy formation
extracted_data.brief_description: Low-dimensional descriptor sets (oxide formation enthalpy, band gap, O 2p band center, electronegativity differences, ionic radii, energy above hull, etc.) used in linear and regression models to predict oxygen-vacancy formation energies and related defect energetics in oxides.
extracted_data.material_systems: Primarily binary and ternary oxides (wide range of oxide chemistries; large-screen datasets of thousands of oxides in extended work); earlier small sets (<50) then extended to ~2000+ compounds.
extracted_data.defect_types: Neutral and charged oxygen vacancies (V_O); primarily single vacancies, typically not defect complexes in early descriptor work.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Mostly neutral vacancy models; some later works extended to charged (e.g., 2+ O vacancy) using additional descriptors; charged-state prediction performance noted to be worse and requiring additional descriptors.
extracted_data.target_properties: Oxygen vacancy formation energy E^f(V_O) (neutral and in some studies charged 2+), sometimes extended to vacancy screening for catalytic/functional metrics.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Hand-crafted global & site-specific scalar descriptors
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Features are scalar bulk or site properties (oxide formation enthalpy, band gap from various functionals, O 2p band center energy, electronegativity differences, ionic radii, binding energies, energy above hull) assembled into linear functions or regression inputs to predict vacancy formation energies.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not defect-centered in a geometric sense; uses bulk/unit-cell or site-averaged properties (host-derived features) rather than explicit supercell defect neighborhoods.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not spatially local descriptors; chemical/energetic quantities from unit cell (band gap, band-center), ionic radii and electronegativities, and formation enthalpies; no explicit neighbor cutoff or angular basis reported for these methods.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Started from small datasets (<50) in earliest work (Deml et al.), extended to thousands of oxides where descriptors were available; DFT-derived target values; dataset sizes and protocol vary between studies cited.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Out-of-sample tests showed degraded performance: e.g., Deml et al. reported in-sample MAE ~0.2 eV but out-of-sample MAE ~0.39 eV for 18 unseen oxides; other works report worse performance for charged vacancies and for chemistries outside training distribution.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Early models trained on small datasets (<50) gave useful trends; expanding dataset to thousands improved coverage but out-of-distribution errors persisted—evidence that simple descriptors are data-efficient but limited in transferability.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Mostly random/holdout splits and then external out-of-sample tests (small sets); details vary by cited study (some explicitly tested unseen oxides), but no unified cross-chemistry protocol across works.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Comparisons among different descriptor combinations (e.g., Deml compared GW vs DFT+U band gaps in formulae); descriptor importance ranking reported in later works (Kumagai et al.) showing different dominant descriptors for neutral vs charged vacancies.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported MAEs for E^f(V_O): Deml ~0.19–0.21 eV (in-sample), out-of-sample ~0.39 eV; other works reported MAE ~0.3–0.45 eV depending on dataset and defect charge (e.g., Wan ~0.4 eV, Wexler 0.45 eV, Kumagai ~0.34 eV neutral, 0.44 eV for 2+).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No direct phonon/thermal-conductivity predictions; these descriptor models focus on formation energies and screening, not on phonon scattering or kappa degradation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue bulk/unit-cell surrogate properties capture the dominant chemical/energetic trends controlling vacancy formation (e.g., binding energy, band edge positions, O 2p center), enabling cheap screening.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Models degrade on chemistries not represented in training; charged-defect predictions are harder (higher MAE); inability to capture geometry-specific reconstructions, local distortions, and localized charge/polaron formation.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use simple bulk descriptors for rapid screening and trend identification; augment with larger, diverse training sets for transferability and include additional descriptors when predicting charged vacancies.

extracted_data.name_full: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN)-based defect predictions
extracted_data.brief_description: Graph neural network operating on crystal structure graphs adapted to predict site-specific defect formation energies (not handcrafted descriptors), using structural connectivity and elemental embeddings to predict vacancy formation energies and migration barriers.
extracted_data.material_systems: Varied (oxides and broader inorganic compounds); models trained on diverse oxide datasets and other compound classes in cited studies.
extracted_data.defect_types: Primarily oxygen vacancies and a range of point defects; vacancy migration barriers in some extensions (NEB-trained models).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Mostly neutral vacancy predictions in earliest CGCNN defect work; charged defects were less frequently treated and pose challenges—charged defect handling not explicitly intrinsic to basic CGCNN.
extracted_data.target_properties: Neutral oxygen vacancy formation energy E^f(V_O^0), vacancy migration barriers (in later extension trained on NEB data).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-site-enabled crystal graph representation
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Crystal is represented as a periodic graph with nodes for atomic sites and edges for neighbor connections; vacancy predictions use the crystal graph and information about the vacancy site (site-specific features) to produce formation-energy predictions.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Graph is global (entire unit cell/crystal), but predictions are localized to specific vacancy sites (site-aware outputs); not explicitly a defect-centered supercell graph.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Graph neighbors defined by crystal connectivity/cutoffs used in CGCNN; elemental species encoded via learned embeddings; no explicit angular basis reported (CGCNN uses distance-weighted interactions within neighbor shells).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: CGCNN-like message-passing convolutional GNN (crystal graph convolutional neural network); deep GNN variant used for defect tasks.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Not in earliest studies; later comments in review mention pretraining/foundation models as complementary (but CGCNN examples described were trained end-to-end on defect datasets).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Training datasets ranged from hundreds to thousands of vacancy/site examples; scarcity and diversity of data identified as primary limiter—errors increase markedly on unseen chemistries.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Witman et al. reported MAE increases: 0.3 eV when predicting unseen vacancy sites in seen compositions, 0.5 eV for unseen compositions with seen cations, and 1.2 eV for completely unseen cations—showing limited cross-chemistry transfer without matching data.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Performance strongly depends on dataset diversity; model reliable for interpolation (seen chemistry/site) but poor for extensive extrapolation to new elements without data.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Reported splits distinguishing 'seen' vs 'unseen' at multiple levels (vacancy sites, compositions, cations) to explicitly probe transferability; holdout/out-of-composition tests used.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared to descriptor-based models where available; demonstrated that scarcity/diversity of training data, not model capacity, was main limitation; no reported ablation on defect-centering vs full-graph in this summary.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: MAE for E^f(V_O^0): ~0.3 eV (interpolation) rising to ~0.5–1.2 eV for various out-of-distribution splits; migration barrier MAE ~0.9 eV overall but ~0.5 eV for barriers between 1–4 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Not directly used for phonon scattering or lattice thermal conductivity in the CGCNN defect prediction studies summarized; later MLFF/phonon sections use different GNN architectures.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Graph-based structural encoding captures local coordination and composition information enabling site-specific predictions; limitations arise from insufficient training diversity rather than representation expressivity.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Poor generalization to unseen elements/chemistries; charged defects and complex polaronic localization not well-captured by basic CGCNN without additional descriptors or charge-aware features.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Explicit out-of-distribution evaluation (seen/unseen splits) to assess transferability; increase dataset diversity for cross-chemistry generalization; consider multi-fidelity inputs to aid extrapolation.

extracted_data.name_full: Bulk-property based models (branch-point energy and related unit-cell features) for defect transition levels
extracted_data.brief_description: Analytical/regression models that use bulk electronic metrics (branch-point energy, dielectric mid-gap energy, interstitial hydrogen transition level) to predict neutral defect formation energies and charge transition levels for vacancies and impurities.
extracted_data.material_systems: II–VI and III–V semiconductors and various alloy systems (e.g., ZnSeTe, ZnMgO) where branch-point energy correlations were studied.
extracted_data.defect_types: Cation vacancies (V_M) and impurity/impurity-level predictions; focused on charged transition levels (epsilon(q1/q2)).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicitly aimed to predict charge transition levels using bulk-derived electrostatic/band-alignment descriptors (branch-point alignment and hydrogen-like reference levels).
extracted_data.target_properties: Charge transition levels epsilon(q1/q2) and neutral formation energies for cation vacancies / impurities.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Branch-point and hydrogen-reference bulk-feature model
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Use universal references (e.g., interstitial H transition level aligned to standard hydrogen electrode) and computed bulk band alignment metrics to analytically predict expected defect charge transition levels without explicit supercell defect calculations.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not defect-centered; uses host bulk electronic properties as surrogate predictors for defect levels.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Descriptors are global electronic properties (branch-point energy, dielectric mid-gap), not local neighbor cutoffs or angular bases.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Models derived and validated on datasets of II–VI and III–V semiconductor defect calculations (hundreds of examples across materials and alloys).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Demonstrated correlation between branch-point energy and neutral vacancy formation energy; used across alloys and compounds in cited work, indicating reasonable transfer within similar semiconductor classes but not assessed for broad chemical spaces.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Leveraging universal physical references enables low-data predictions of transition levels across related semiconductors.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Comparisons to DFT-calculated transition levels across semiconductor datasets; cross-material tests in alloys noted.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared against direct DFT defect calculations; shown to provide useful predictive trends but limited by accuracy of bulk reference quantities and inability to capture local reconstructions.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Qualitative/quantitative correlation shown (plots reported in review); specific numeric errors not reported in review summary.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: No direct connection to phonon scattering or lattice thermal conductivity; focuses on electronic transition-level prediction.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Physical alignment to universal hydrogen reference and branch-point energy captures band-edge related drivers of defect charge transition energies without explicit supercell computations.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Cannot capture local geometry relaxations, polaron formation, or qualitative errors in lower-level bulk properties; applicability mainly within similar semiconductor families.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use bulk-reference models for rapid, low-cost estimates of transition levels in related semiconductors; combine with higher-fidelity or delta-learning approaches when qualitative local effects are suspected.

extracted_data.name_full: Delta-learning / multi-fidelity defect models (augmenting low-fidelity DFT with high-fidelity corrections)
extracted_data.brief_description: Models that use inexpensive low-fidelity defect outputs (e.g., PBE defect levels or formation energies) as descriptors or inputs to learn corrections (delta) to higher-fidelity targets (e.g., HSE06) to improve prediction of defect levels/energetics with limited high-fidelity data.
extracted_data.material_systems: Semiconductors and doped materials where both low- and high-fidelity DFT data exist (examples include III–V/II–VI semiconductors and perovskites in cited studies).
extracted_data.defect_types: Native and extrinsic defects, impurity levels, charged defect states where high-level theory is expensive.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Charge states included via input low-fidelity calculations (explicit PBE defect levels and formation energies used as descriptors) but delta models cannot fix qualitative failures in low-fidelity data.
extracted_data.target_properties: High-fidelity defect levels (HSE06), formation energies, and charge transition levels.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Delta / multi-fidelity features (low-fidelity outputs as descriptors)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Include low-cost DFT defect outputs (e.g., PBE energies/levels) among descriptors, and train regression to predict the difference to high-fidelity targets (delta), leveraging larger low-fidelity datasets to augment scarce high-fidelity labels.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not explicitly geometric; relies on whole-defect low-fidelity calculations as part of descriptor set (practical 'paired' defective calculations are used).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: In addition to delta features, other elemental and bulk descriptors are used (ionic properties, band edges); specifics vary across implementations.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Used with regression models and GNNs in different works; primarily a feature-engineering strategy rather than a single architecture.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No explicit foundation model use necessary; strategy leverages low-fidelity computed labels as extra inputs.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Intended for small high-fidelity datasets supplemented with larger low-fidelity datasets; demonstrated to improve performance when PBE data is informative.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Delta learning improves quantitative accuracy for cases where low-fidelity data is qualitatively correct; review stresses delta cannot correct qualitative failures (e.g., wrong localization or geometry) in low-fidelity data.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Reported to dramatically improve accuracy with limited high-fidelity data by leveraging low-fidelity inputs (specific numeric gains reported qualitatively in review; Mannodi-Kanakkithodi noted dramatic improvement when including PBE defect levels).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Typical training where high-fidelity targets are scarce; no single standard protocol across cited works—use paired low/high-fidelity splits and test on high-fidelity held-out data.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared models with and without low-fidelity descriptors; inclusion of PBE defect levels shown to substantially improve high-fidelity prediction accuracy.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Examples: Polak et al. ML-MBA (multi-input including low-level quantities) RMSE 0.27 eV vs MBA, 0.36 eV vs HSE06; Mannodi-Kanakkithodi reported improved HSE06 level predictions when including PBE defect levels as features (no single MAE quoted in review).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Not directly linked to phonon predictions; delta-learning is applicable whenever multi-fidelity labels exist, including MLFF/phonon contexts if low-/high-fidelity vibrational data are available.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Delta learning is effective because lower-level DFT often captures trend/qualitative placement which can be quantitatively corrected with small high-fidelity data; cannot fix qualitative disagreements.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Cannot correct qualitative failures in the low-fidelity data (wrong geometry, localization); risk of propagating biases if low-fidelity data are systematically wrong.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use delta learning when low-fidelity data are qualitatively reliable; assess low-fidelity failure modes before trusting delta corrections; combine with targeted high-fidelity sampling for problematic chemistries.

extracted_data.name_full: Pretrained foundation interatomic potentials (equivariant GNN MLFFs) used as transferable priors for defects
extracted_data.brief_description: Large, pre-trained equivariant message-passing interatomic potentials (e.g., MACE, NequIP, M3GNet) trained on diverse bulk datasets and deployed directly or fine-tuned to accelerate defect structure search, relaxations, and phonon/thermal calculations.
extracted_data.material_systems: Diverse bulk materials (foundation potentials trained on broad datasets) and applied across many hosts including metal chalcogenides, CdTe/CdSe, perovskites, SiC, MgTiO3 examples in review.
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies (including split vacancies), interstitials, dopants, defect complexes; used for geometry optimization, PES exploration, phonon calculations.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Usually trained on neutral/bulk data; effective when defects are in fully-ionized charge states dominated by electrostatics (Kavanagh example). Charge-state effects require either explicit charged training data or fine-tuning; not intrinsically charge-aware.
extracted_data.target_properties: Relaxed defect geometries, formation energies (semi-quantitatively), phonons and vibrational properties, PES sampling and finite-temperature free energies, sometimes migration paths.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation potential embedding / pretraining and fine-tuning
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Pretrain a high-capacity equivariant GNN MLFF on very large and diverse atomistic datasets (bulk and/or AIMD), then apply directly to defect supercells or fine-tune on a small defect-specific dataset (tens to hundreds of DFT points) to improve accuracy for that defect.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Models operate on full-structure coordinates (entire supercell) but their transferability stems from learned local atomic environments; fine-tuning often focuses on defect-centered configurations.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Equivariant message-passing networks encode local neighbor environments with radial cutoffs and learned continuous embeddings for species; specific cutoff/spherical basis details are architecture-dependent (not detailed in review).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Equivariant message-passing GNN architectures (examples: MACE, NequIP, M3GNet); use of equivariance to E(3) symmetries and directional features emphasized.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Explicit use: MACE and NequIP foundation potentials pre-trained on bulk datasets; M3GNet pretraining fine-tuned on defect relaxations by Mosquera-Lois; foundation models sometimes used without fine-tuning (Kavanagh).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Foundation models trained on very large diverse datasets of bulk crystals/AIMD; fine-tuning typically uses small defect-specific DFT sets (tens to hundreds of structures).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Kavanagh found foundation potentials could identify split-vacancy geometries across diverse material classes without fine-tuning (noting restriction to fully-ionized states); Mosquera-Lois fine-tuned M3GNet on small hybrid-DFT defect dataset and achieved 90% success in finding energy-lowering reconstructions on unseen defects/compositions.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Fine-tuning with small datasets (tens of DFT relaxations) yielded dramatic accuracy improvements for defect phonons and force constants (Turiansky) and for structural reconstructions (Mosquera-Lois); foundation-only predictions gave reasonable trends but lacked fidelity for strongly localized relaxations.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Transfer tests: apply pre-trained potential to unseen defects/hosts; fine-tune on small defect-specific sets and test on held-out defect configurations and unseen compositions; specific seen/unseen splits used in cited experiments.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared foundation-only, fine-tuned, and defect-specific-from-scratch models in phonon tasks (Turiansky, Sharma, Zhou). Fine-tuning improved force constants and PL/Huang-Rhys predictions; defect-specific training gives best fidelity.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported outcomes: Mosquera-Lois reported successful identification of energy-lowering reconstructions in ~90% cases; Turiansky reported near-hybrid-DFT accuracy for Huang–Rhys factors and spectral features after fine-tuning with tens of structures; quantitative MAEs vary by study and property.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Foundation MLFFs applied to compute force constants and defect phonons; after fine-tuning they produced accurate Huang–Rhys factors, PL lineshapes, and enabled phonon-based calculations feeding into thermal transport analyses; foundation models alone capture trends but may miss localized-mode details needed for accurate scattering predictions.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Pretraining on diverse data gives priors for common local atomic motifs enabling transfer to defects; equivariance and message-passing implement physically relevant symmetries and directional information aiding phonon/force prediction.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Foundation potentials struggle with strongly localized modes and large structural reconstructions unless fine-tuned; not inherently charge-aware so charged-defect PES can be problematic without charged training data; risk of semiquantitative errors if used without defect-specific augmentation.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use foundation potentials as starting point for high-throughput scanning; fine-tune with small defect-specific DFT sets (tens of structures) for quantitative phonon/PL predictions; include charged-state configurations if charged-defect accuracy is required.

extracted_data.name_short: Fine-tuning foundation models for defect phonons
extracted_data.name_full: Fine-tuning pretrained foundation MLFFs with small defect-specific datasets for phonon and PL predictions
extracted_data.brief_description: Take a general foundation MLFF and fine-tune it using a compact set (tens) of DFT structures sampled along defect relaxation pathways and finite-displacement configurations to recover near-hybrid-DFT accuracy for force constants, Huang–Rhys factors, and photoluminescence lineshapes.
extracted_data.material_systems: Various defect-host systems used to benchmark phonons and PL (examples in review include diverse point defects across multiple materials, specific perovskites and color-center-like defects).
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies and impurity centers, defects with localized vibrational modes relevant for PL and nonradiative capture.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Charge states included via defect-specific training data for each charge state; fine-tuning was performed per defect+charge-state in Turiansky's approach.
extracted_data.target_properties: Second-order force constants, phonon frequencies/eigenvectors, Huang–Rhys factors, photoluminescence (PL) lineshapes, and vibrational contributions to optical spectra.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation model fine-tuning (defect-specific augmentation)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Start from a pretrained equivariant GNN MLFF; add a small number (tens) of high-quality DFT configurations (relaxations and finite-displacement samples) for the defect and charge states of interest; fine-tune weights to improve local force-constant predictions.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Fine-tuning datasets are defect-centered (samples along relaxation coordinate and local displacements) though model operates on full supercell.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Equivariant message-passing descriptors with learned radial/angle-sensitive interactions; fine-tuning focuses on improving representation of defect-local environments; specific cutoff details not reported in review.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Foundation equivariant GNNs (various E(3)-equivariant force fields discussed), fine-tuned on defect data.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Yes — explicit fine-tuning of foundation potentials (same model weights adapted with small defect datasets).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Very small defect-specific fine-tuning sets (tens of DFT structures; optionally augmented with 10–30 finite-displacement structures) per defect/charge state.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Fine-tuning with tens of samples dramatically improved force-constant accuracy and PL spectral fidelity compared to foundation-only models; produced near-hybrid-DFT accuracy in examples reported.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Small amounts of defect-specific data (order 10s) sufficient to attain high accuracy for phonon/PL metrics, indicating high data efficiency when starting from foundation models.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Benchmarking against DFT-calculated force constants, Huang–Rhys factors, and PL spectra; comparisons included foundation-only, fine-tuned, and defect-specific-from-scratch baselines.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Turiansky compared foundation-only vs fine-tuned vs adding 10–30 finite-displacement samples; fine-tuning yielded large improvements indicating the benefit of small targeted datasets.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported near-hybrid-DFT accuracy for Huang–Rhys factors and spectral widths after fine-tuning (no single numeric MAE reported in review for all cases); qualitative figures show marked improvement in PL lineshape fidelity.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Fine-tuned MLFFs provide accurate force constants and phonon eigenvectors necessary to compute electron–phonon coupling, Huang–Rhys factors, PL lineshapes, and to feed phonon scattering calculations relevant to thermal-conductivity degradation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Fine-tuning corrects local PES and force-constant errors of foundation models, capturing localized vibrational modes critical for defect optical and nonradiative processes.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Fine-tuning must be defect- and charge-state-specific to reach high fidelity; foundation-only models may suffice for trends but not for quantitative localized phonon physics.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Start from a foundation MLFF and fine-tune with a compact, targeted DFT dataset (include finite-displacement samples); include charge-state samples if charged-defect phonons are needed.

extracted_data.name_full: One-defect-one-potential (defect-specific compact MLFFs)
extracted_data.brief_description: Train a compact equivariant ML potential from scratch for a single defect using a small, randomly displaced dataset centered on the defect to accurately reproduce local PES, enabling scalable phonon and nonradiative-capture computations in very large supercells.
extracted_data.material_systems: Individual defect-in-host systems studied case-by-case; approach applied to multiple defects to demonstrate scalability (PL and nonradiative capture benchmarks).
extracted_data.defect_types: Specific single defects (vacancies, interstitials, impurity centers) treated individually; tailored models for each defect/charge state; supports large supercells for phonon embeddings.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Models trained per defect and charge state when needed; explicit charge-state training provides charge-aware PES for that specific state.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect force constants, phonon dispersions in huge supercells (>10^4 atoms), Huang–Rhys factors, photoluminescence lineshapes, full-dimensional nonradiative multiphonon capture rates.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-specific local MLFF (one-defect-one-potential)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Construct a compact equivariant GNN MLFF trained from scratch using a small set of defect-centered displaced configurations; embed learned force constants into large supercells to compute full vibrational/optical/nonradiative properties.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Explicitly defect-centered: training data sampled in local region around defect; model designed to capture local PES and then embed into global supercell context for large-scale phonon calculations.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Equivariant local descriptors with neighbor cutoffs sufficient to capture defect local environment; trained species-aware embeddings; specific cutoff/basis not detailed in review.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Compact equivariant GNN trained from scratch for each defect (referenced as equivariant models with improved force-constant embedding scheme).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No — trained from scratch per defect, not relying on foundation pretraining.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Small defect-centered datasets of randomly displaced configurations; sufficient to reproduce DFT phonons and PL results; allows scaling to very large supercells due to local-focus force-constant embedding.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Designed to be highly accurate for the single target defect but not intended to transfer across defects or hosts; trade-off is high fidelity vs generality.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Small numbers of defect-centered samples suffice to achieve DFT-comparable phonon/PL predictions for the target defect; efficient for one-off high-accuracy calculations.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Benchmarks against full DFT-derived Huang–Rhys factors, PL lineshapes, and nonradiative capture rates; compared to foundation and fine-tuned models showing defect-specific models achieve highest fidelity.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared to foundation-only and fine-tuned approaches; defect-specific models outperform in accuracy but at cost of per-defect training.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported qualitatively (figures) that Huang–Rhys factors, PL lineshapes, and nonradiative capture coefficients from defect-specific MLFFs agree with DFT benchmarks; exact numeric MAEs not universally quoted in review.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Directly enables accurate phonon-mode-resolved calculations for defects, full PL spectra, and explicit multiphonon nonradiative capture rates; supports embedding into large supercells to capture long-range elastic effects relevant to scattering.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Local training focuses model capacity on capturing the true defect PES including localized modes and large relaxations, critical for accurate optical and nonradiative predictions.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: No cross-defect transferability; requires per-defect training effort (though small); not suited for high-throughput across many defects unless automated.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use one-defect-one-potential for quantitative defect phonon and nonradiative-capture studies where high accuracy is required; combine with foundation models or fine-tuning for screening workflows.

extracted_data.name_full: Charge-aware neural network potential with explicit system-charge input
extracted_data.brief_description: Behler–Parrinello neural-network potential augmented with an explicit global system-charge input node so a single ML potential can represent multiple defect charge states consistently and reproduce charge-dependent phonon spectra.
extracted_data.material_systems: Example: nitrogen vacancy (V_N) in GaN studied in cited work; technique applicable to charged-defect phonons in ionic/semiconducting materials.
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies in multiple charge states (V_N in GaN example with 0, +1, +2, +3 charge states); approach applicable to charged point defects generally.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicit: a global system-charge node included in neural network inputs to represent total charge state and allow one model to handle multiple charges coherently.
extracted_data.target_properties: Phonon spectra (force constants), energies, and forces across multiple defect charge states; used to reproduce DFT phonon spectra.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Global-charge-augmented atom-centered ML potential
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Standard atom-centered symmetry-function NNP augmented by an additional input representing the total system charge, enabling the network to modulate outputs (energies/forces) according to charge state.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Model trained on supercell configurations with defects; not necessarily defect-centered training but charge node encodes global electrostatic state.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Uses Behler–Parrinello symmetry functions (atom-centered radial/angular features) plus global charge scalar node; species encoded via atomic inputs as usual in NNP.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Behler–Parrinello neural network (atom-centered symmetry function NNP) modified with an extra input representing system charge.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No pretraining described; trained on DFT data including charged states.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained on DFT datasets that include pristine, defect-containing, and charged configurations for each charge state; review reports accuracy numbers from cited study.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Demonstrated accurate reproduction of DFT phonon spectra across multiple charge states in the GaN V_N example, indicating method generalizes across charges for that system; broader cross-material transfer not assessed.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Reported small energy and force errors (energies ~1.4 meV/atom, forces ~64 meV/Å) for the GaN example indicating practical data efficiency for multi-charge training in that system.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Benchmarking vs DFT phonon spectra for multiple charge states; errors in energies and forces reported.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared to conventional NNPs trained only on neutral/individual charge states; explicit charge node allowed a single model to reproduce multiple charge states.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported errors in cited study: energy error ~1.4 meV/atom and forces ~64 meV/Å; close agreement in phonon branches with minor high-frequency deviations.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Directly used to reproduce DFT phonon spectra across charge states and therefore supports phonon-scattering and thermal-transport related analyses for charged defects.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Global charge input lets the ML potential capture charge-dependent changes in local PES and vibrational properties without training independent models per charge.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Approach demonstrated for one system; may require including charged reference configurations and careful treatment of background charge and electrostatic corrections for supercells to be quantitatively accurate.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include explicit charged-state configurations in training and consider global charge descriptors when multi-charge-state predictions are required; validate phonon spectra across charges against DFT.

extracted_data.name_full: ML force fields trained to compute defect phonons and defect-limited thermal conductivity
extracted_data.brief_description: Machine-learned potentials (e.g., NNPs, equivariant GNNs, NEP) trained on pristine and defected charged/neutral configurations to compute second- and third-order force constants, defect scattering, and defect-limited lattice thermal conductivity at DFT-like accuracy.
extracted_data.material_systems: Examples include AlN (with defects) for defect-limited thermal conductivity, cBN with vacancies and isotopic disorder, MgO/LiF/CsSnBr3 for finite-temperature defect formation; applied to a range of semiconductors and ceramics.
extracted_data.defect_types: Vacancies, interstitials, isotopic disorder and mixed defect species; both neutral and charged defects included in training in some studies.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Mixed strategies: some models explicitly include charged configurations in training (Dou et al.), others train on neutral and charged mixed data without explicit charge features; charge-aware strategies (e.g., global charge node) are possible.
extracted_data.target_properties: Second- and third-order force constants, phonon dispersions and DOS in defected supercells, phonon scattering rates, and defect-limited lattice thermal conductivity (kappa) computed using MLFF-derived force constants.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: MLFF-derived force-constant prediction for phonon transport
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Train MLFFs on a dataset including pristine and defective configurations (possibly in multiple charge states) to accurately predict forces; compute finite-difference force constants or employ ML-derived dynamical matrices to obtain phonon spectra and scattering needed for BTE-based thermal conductivity calculations.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Training includes both pristine and defect-containing supercells; defect-centered sampling used when focusing on defect-localized vibrational features.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: NNP symmetry functions or equivariant GNN descriptors used; third-order force constants obtained from ML-predicted forces over finite displacements; angular/radial invariances respected in architectures used.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Behler–Parrinello NNPs, neuroevolution potentials (NEP), equivariant GNN MLFFs depending on study; architectures chosen to reproduce forces accurately for phonon extraction.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Some studies trained from scratch on targeted datasets including defects (Dou et al.); foundation models may be used/fine-tuned in other contexts.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Training datasets include pristine and defected configurations along relaxations and finite-displacement samples; diversity and inclusion of charge states determine fidelity for charged-defect phonons.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Dou et al. computed defect-limited thermal conductivity in AlN with DFT-level accuracy using MLFF trained on mixed charged/neutral defect data; foundation models show promise but require fine-tuning for localized modes.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Including defect configurations and finite-displacement samples in training yields accurate second- and third-order force constants with much lower computational cost than DFT; amount of data varies but mixed training sufficient in reported cases.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Compare ML-derived phonon dispersions and thermal-conductivity (via BTE or scattering approximations) to DFT-computed references; include finite-temperature MD sampling where relevant.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared ML-predicted force constants and kappa to DFT results; ablations include presence/absence of charged-defect data and inclusion of third-order interactions.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported reproduction of DFT phonon spectra with small deviations; Dou et al. reported ability to compute defect-limited thermal conductivity with DFT-level accuracy (no single universal numeric reported in review summary).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Direct: MLFFs used to compute force constants and phonon scattering by defects, allowing evaluation of defect-limited kappa and thermal-conductivity degradation via standard phonon transport frameworks (BTE/relaxation-time approximations).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Accurate local PES and force constants from MLFFs enable phonon scattering and thermal-transport calculations that are otherwise infeasible due to DFT cost; inclusion of charged configurations improves treatment of charge-dependent vibrational responses.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Strongly localized modes and large relaxations may be missed by off-the-shelf potentials; charged defect handling requires targeted training; accuracy for third-order interactions depends on training data quality.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Train MLFFs on combined pristine + defect + finite-displacement samples, include charged configurations if relevant, and validate ML force constants against DFT before computing thermal-transport properties.

extracted_data.name_full: Architectures explicitly biased to defects: defect-informed GNNs and coordinate-based transformer MLFFs
extracted_data.brief_description: New ML architectures adapted for defect physics: transformer-style models operating on coordinates to avoid graph over-smoothing and long-range issues (transformer coords-in-space), and defect-informed GNNs that explicitly encode defect-centric information for structure prediction.
extracted_data.material_systems: Proposed and demonstrated in recent 2025 studies on defect structure prediction and MLFF accuracy benchmarking; not limited to a single chemistry.
extracted_data.defect_types: Used for relaxed defect structure prediction (split vacancies, local reconstructions) and related tasks rather than bulk property prediction.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Architectural proposals; charge handling not intrinsic but could be incorporated; specific implementations vary by study.
extracted_data.target_properties: Relaxed defect structures, local geometry prediction; some models targeted energies/forces via MLFF variants.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-informed GNN and coordinate-based transformer representations
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Replace or augment standard graph representations with coordinate-space transformers to better capture long-range interactions and avoid over-smoothing; defect-informed GNNs include explicit cues about defect centers or perturbations to bias network to local defect physics.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Explicit defect-centering in defect-informed GNNs; coordinate transformers operate on full-structure coordinates but can be conditioned on defect site.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Coordinate-based representations avoid discrete neighbor graph construction; defect-informed GNNs retain atomic/species information plus defect-centric indicators.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Transformer coordinate models (non-graph) and defect-informed variants of message-passing GNNs; motivated to improve long-range and defect-specific expressivity.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Not necessarily; architectures can be trained from scratch or potentially pretrain on bulk data then specialize.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Developed to address limitations seen when applying bulk-trained MLFFs to sparse defect datasets; data requirements contingent on architecture and task.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Reported to improve accuracy on defect structure prediction and to reduce long-range/over-smoothing problems in comparisons cited in review; quantitative benchmarks not extensively enumerated in review.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Architectural inductive biases aim to improve sample efficiency for defect tasks, but explicit learning curves not reported in summary.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Benchmarked against standard GNN MLFFs and DFT-relaxed structures; active-learning or teacher-student distillation used in some works.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared transformer vs GNN MLFFs and defect-informed vs vanilla GNNs; improvements reported for defect-specific tasks.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Improvements in prediction accuracy reported qualitatively; specific numeric metrics not aggregated in the review summary.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Primarily targeted at structure and energy predictions; improved relaxed geometries and forces indirectly benefit phonon calculations and thermal-transport predictions when accurate PES is recovered.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Coordinate transformers avoid over-smoothing inherent to graph aggregation; defect-informed cues focus model capacity on important local distortions around defects, improving geometry prediction.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Still emerging; needs systematic benchmarking across chemistries and defect types; may require careful scaling for large supercells.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Consider architecture choices that encode defect-centric inductive biases (defect indicators, coordinate attention) when building MLFFs for defect structure prediction and downstream phonon tasks.

extracted_data.name_full: Gaussian Process surrogate models and active learning for defect PES exploration
extracted_data.brief_description: Use of Gaussian Process models with uncertainty quantification in an active-learning loop to evaluate candidate defect structures during global optimization/search and call DFT only for high-uncertainty configurations, improving data efficiency.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied in structure-searching for silicon self-interstitials and V_O in anatase-TiO2 examples; useful for amorphous and defect-rich systems.
extracted_data.defect_types: Self-interstitials, oxygen vacancies, and generally defect geometries in many host systems during global search.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: GP models used primarily for PES and structural search; charge states can be included if training data contain charged configurations, uncertainty estimates guide DFT sampling.
extracted_data.target_properties: Relative energies of candidate defect geometries, PES landscape exploration, identification of low-energy metastable configurations.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: GP surrogate with active learning (teacher-student and uncertainty-based sampling)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Train GP surrogate to predict energies with posterior uncertainty; in evolutionary/global search, accept low-uncertainty model predictions but query DFT for high-uncertainty configurations and iteratively update the GP with new labels.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Can target local defect-centered candidate structures sampled by structural perturbation toolkits (e.g., ShakeNBreak); representations are typically structure-to-energy mappings using local descriptors or global coordinate features.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: GP inputs often derived from local structural descriptors or compressed representations; details depend on implementation; uncertainty output used for acquisition.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Gaussian Process regression (non-deep); sometimes combined with student-teacher distillation to yield faster MLIPs.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: GP is trained on the fly; teacher-student distillation used to produce ultra-fast MLIPs for downstream large-scale simulation.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Designed for low-data regimes where DFT is expensive; active learning minimizes DFT queries by focusing on high-uncertainty samples.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Active-learning reduces total DFT sampling and has been shown to recover relevant metastable configurations in cited case studies; teacher-student distillation enabled million-atom models in follow-up work.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Uncertainty-guided sampling reduces DFT budget; GP uncertainty is effective for prioritizing DFT calculations in structure search.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Evolutionary or global search with GP surrogate in the loop; validation by DFT re-evaluation of selected candidates and checking if low-energy structures are found.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared to pure DFT-only searches; GP-accelerated workflows found similar minima at substantially lower DFT cost.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported qualitative speed-ups and successful identification of lower-energy defect reconstructions (examples include silicon self-interstitials and V_O in TiO2); specific wall-time or query-count savings vary across studies.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Indirect: improved exploration of defect minima yields better starting points for phonon calculations and MLFF training for vibrational properties.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: GP uncertainty estimates effectively guide expensive DFT calculations toward informative regions of PES, improving data efficiency in defect structure search.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: GPs scale poorly with very large datasets; limited accuracy compared to deep MLFFs but valuable for uncertainty-driven sampling in low-data regimes.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use GP surrogates with active learning during structure-search pipelines; combine with teacher-student distillation to produce fast student MLIPs for large-scale dynamics.

extracted_data.name_full: MACE high-body-order equivariant atom-centered features
extracted_data.brief_description: Atom-centered, equivariant high-body-order features produced by the MACE message-passing architecture (4-body messages, spherical expansion up to l_max=3) used as the primary featurization for predicting energies, forces and derived properties across crystals, molecules and defects; features are element-aware and constructed from local neighbour geometry within a radial cutoff.
extracted_data.citation_title: Mace: Higher order equivariant message passing neural networks for fast and accurate force fields
extracted_data.material_systems: Many hosts across the paper: inorganic crystals (Materials Project coverage), BCC metals (point and extended defects), Si (Si interstitials), metal oxides (CeO2), MOFs (Mg-MOF-74), water and aqueous interfaces, catalytic surfaces (Pt(111), Cu, In2O3), alloys and more — i.e. multiple hosts and chemistries.
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects and extended defects are reported in applications (Si interstitials, proton defects H3O+/OH- in water, point and extended defects in BCC metals, activation energies for point defect and dislocation motion); explicit mention of defect complexes is not given in detail in main text but extended/complex defects (dislocations) are considered in SI.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: No explicit charge-state encoding: the representation is structural (atomic positions and species) only. Charged species (e.g., hydronium, hydroxide, dissolved ions) appear in simulations implicitly via atomic identities and positions, but there is no explicit electron chemical potential, background-charge correction, nor explicit electrostatic/charge labels incorporated into the learned representation; model also lacks explicit long-range electrostatics beyond the ~12 Å receptive field.
extracted_data.target_properties: Total energies, forces and stresses (used to obtain: defect formation and migration activation energies and NEB profiles, reaction barriers, phonon dispersions), examples include activation energies for point-defect/dislocation motion, NEB energy profiles for catalytic pathways, phonon dispersions (in SI); direct prediction of phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal-conductivity degradation is not reported in the main text.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Atom-centered equivariant high-body-order descriptor (MACE features)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Each atom has an element embedding; local geometric information up to a radial cutoff is expanded in a spherical basis and combined into 4-body equivariant messages via tensor products; messages are passed through two MACE layers to produce per-atom energy contributions. Short-range ZBL repulsion and Agnesi distance transform are used to stabilize close approaches; a learnable density-normalisation scales the atomic basis.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Atom-centered (local) representation — not a defect-centered subgraph or explicit delta-to-pristine encoding; defect-related tasks are handled by feeding defective supercells through the same atom-centered MACE representation (the paper uses the internal features to compare local environments between training and defect NEB images).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Radial cutoff (effective receptive field) ≈ 6 Å (two-message-passes → ≈12 Å global receptive field), radial expansion: 10 Bessel functions × polynomial cutoff, spherical expansion up to l_max = 3; 4-body messages (correlation order 3) per layer; tensor-decomposed 128-channel representation; element identity encoded via learned element embeddings; equivariant (E(3)) features implemented with e3nn.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: MACE (equivariant message-passing graph tensor network) with two message-passing layers, high body-order (4-body) equivariant messages, mild nonlinearity (nonlinearities in radial basis and final readout), tensor-decomposition parameterisation; L=1 ('medium') model used in this paper.
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Yes — the MACE-MP-0 foundation model (pretrained on the MPtrj dataset) provides the internal atomic/environment embeddings used out-of-the-box and then fine-tuned for downstream tasks; internal high-dimensional MACE features are projected (UMAP) to assess similarity between training and out-of-domain environments (e.g., NEB images).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Pretrained on MPtrj (Materials Project trajectories) containing ≈1.5M configurations (approx. 150k unique MP structures, mostly small periodic unit cells, ~90% under 70 atoms), DFT (PBE) labels; defect-specific training data are not enumerated — downstream defect/catalysis tasks are handled by fine-tuning on small application-specific datasets (typical fine-tuning size ≈100 configurations; NEB fine-tuning examples used as few as 5 single-point DFT labels per profile).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Strong out-of-domain performance reported: MOF energy prediction on QMOF (13,912 structures) MAE = 0.040 eV/atom despite no QMOF training; catalysis NEB paths on In2O3 and Cu show qualitatively correct barriers out-of-the-box and excellent quantitative agreement after few-shot fine-tuning (5 DFT points); UMAP projections of MACE features show overlap between training atomic environments and NEB defect environments indicating shared representation; general stable MD for many chemistries including charged species in liquids reported. Reported baseline/model-level metrics: pretrained medium model energy MAE ≈ 18 meV/atom and force MAE ≈ 39 meV/Å; after fine-tuning energy MAE down to ≈13 meV/atom on some tasks.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Fine-tuning evidence: NEB/catalysis examples achieved near-DFT quantitative agreement after fine-tuning with as few as 5 single-point DFT calculations per energy profile; typical fine-tuning for applications used ≈100 configurations and multi-head replay to avoid catastrophic forgetting; comparisons in Fig.4 show fine-tuned foundation model substantially outperforms models trained from scratch on the same small datasets.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Fine-tuning protocol: multi-head replay fine-tuning (replays a subset of foundation training data during FT). For downstream tasks the paper reports small-sample fine-tuning (≈100 configs) and occasional 5-point NEB fine-tunes; explicit train/validation/test split strategies for defect-specific datasets are not detailed in the main text (many defect/phonon/NEB results and detailed protocols referred to SI/appendices).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Main comparisons: pretrained MACE-MP-0 vs the same model after fine-tuning (multi-head replay FT) vs a model trained from scratch only on the small fine-tuning dataset (the FT model consistently wins). The paper also compares to DFT references (PBE-D3) and custom ML potentials in application cases; ablation of long-range interactions and spin/electrostatics is discussed as limitations but not ablated experimentally in the main text.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Reported numbers relevant to defect/transfer tasks include: pretrained medium model energy MAE ≈ 18 meV/atom and force MAE ≈ 39 meV/Å; MOF (QMOF) PBE energy MAE = 0.040 eV/atom; ice-polymorph relative lattice energies MAE ≈ 5 meV; phonon and defect benchmarks reported in SI (numbers not all reproduced in main text). NEB/catalysis FT agreement described qualitatively as 'excellent' after 5-point fine-tunes, but full numeric tables are in SI.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Paper reports the model can predict phonon dispersions (benchmarked in SI) and therefore can supply the harmonic phonon spectrum needed for phonon transport calculations; however, no direct workflow or reported results for ML prediction of phonon scattering rates or explicit lattice thermal conductivity degradation due to point defects is presented in the main text — the paper does not report direct ML predictions of scattering rates or kappa degradation nor coupling to BTE/relaxation-time-approximation in the main body (phonon results are limited to dispersions and related benchmarks in SI).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue the high body-order equivariant features capture many-body local geometry and chemistry necessary for transferability, and that the foundation model's internal features enable identification of similar local environments across domains (UMAP example) explaining out-of-domain performance; fine-tuning with a handful of data points corrects local energetic offsets efficiently, supporting the foundation + few-shot paradigm.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Reported limitations relevant to defects: absence of explicit long-range electrostatics and spin degrees of freedom (limits accuracy for charged defects, dilute ionic screening, interfaces); inconsistencies in training data due to sporadic Hubbard U application in Materials Project (affects systems with certain transition metals and O/F, creating discontinuities); model inherits PBE functional limitations (no dispersion unless additive D3 applied), and short radial cutoff may hamper description of long-range fields produced by charged defects. Also, while MD stability is good, quantitative accuracy for intermolecular interactions and some catalytic states remains limited without FT.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use the foundation MACE-MP-0 model out-of-the-box for exploration and then fine-tune with a small, application-specific DFT dataset (≈5–100 configurations) using multi-head replay FT to avoid catastrophic forgetting; apply additive DFT-D3 corrections when dispersion matters; for charged-defect problems or long-range electrostatic effects, augment the model/representation to include explicit electrostatics or use larger receptive fields / targeted FT data; ensure consistent electronic-structure settings in training/FT to avoid Hubbard-U related inconsistencies.

extracted_data.name_full: Multi-head replay fine-tuning (foundation model adaptation protocol)
extracted_data.brief_description: A fine-tuning protocol used to adapt the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential to downstream tasks (including NEB/catalysis and defect-related calculations) by training on a small new dataset while replaying a subset of the foundation training data to avoid catastrophic forgetting.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied across multiple downstream examples in the paper: catalytic NEB paths (Cu and In2O3), MOF adsorption dynamics, and other application-specific examples including defect-related NEBs and point-defect activation energies in SI.
extracted_data.defect_types: Used to improve predictions on tasks that include reaction paths and defect migration barriers (NEB images, point-defect/dislocation motion), but the protocol itself is general-purpose (not defect-specific).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Protocol does not add explicit charge-state features; it fine-tunes the same structure-only MACE representation. Handling of charged defects remains governed by the underlying representation (i.e., no explicit charge labels added by FT unless user supplies charged configurations during FT).
extracted_data.target_properties: Used to lower force and energy errors for application-specific targets: NEB energy profiles (reaction and migration barriers), forces, and energies; thereby improving predicted activation energies and reaction energetics relevant to defects and catalysis.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Foundation-model fine-tuning with replay (multi-head replay FT)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: During FT the loss includes both the new small application dataset and a replayed subset of the original foundation training data; separate model head(s) may be used to preserve foundation capabilities while adapting to new tasks.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: No change to centering: fine-tuning still operates on full supercells/atom-centered inputs; practitioners can supply defective supercells during FT to adapt locally to defect environments.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Does not change descriptor hyperparameters (radial cutoff, spherical expansion, message order); it updates model weights starting from pretrained MACE parameters and uses a replay subset to stabilize representations.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Applied to the MACE graph-tensor-network architecture (two MACE layers, equivariant messages).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: Relies on pretrained MACE-MP-0 weights as initialization; FT modifies these weights while replaying foundation data.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Typical FT regimes shown: ≈100 configurations for many applications; for NEB reaction profiles FT with as few as 5 single-point DFT calculations per profile was sufficient to reach near-DFT agreement in examples presented.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: FT demonstrably improves out-of-domain predictions: NEB reaction profiles for CO oxidation on Cu and CO2→methanol step on In2O3 achieve excellent agreement with DFT after small-number FT (5 points) where pretrained model alone was only qualitatively correct; FT models retain foundation robustness due to replay.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Strong few-shot evidence: 5 single-point DFT labels per NEB profile produced excellent quantitative agreement with DFT for several reaction barriers; FT with ≈100 configs substantially reduces force errors across several applications compared to pretrained-only and to models trained from scratch on the small dataset.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Multi-head replay FT: the loss includes the small FT dataset and a subset of the original training data; specific training hyperparameters and replay subset sizes are given in SI/appendices but main-text examples report FT epochs ≈50 for some energy-weighted FT runs.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Comparison shown between pretrained model, fine-tuned model (multi-head replay) and a model trained from scratch only on the small FT dataset — fine-tuned model consistently outperforms 'from-scratch' baseline and improves over pretrained-only for quantitative accuracy.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Qualitative statements and selected numbers: fine-tuning reduces force RMS errors significantly across several tasks (Fig.4). Example: several NEB profiles reach 'excellent agreement' with DFT after FT with only a few points (numeric NEB errors are provided in SI but not all reproduced in main text).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: FT can be used to improve phonon predictions when FT data includes phonon-related configurations (the paper fine-tunes to r2SCAN for XC upgrade in SI); no explicit example of FT targeted to defect-induced phonon scattering or thermal conductivity was reported in main text.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue that starting from a foundation potential and fine-tuning with a handful of application-relevant configurations is an efficient workflow: the foundation captures broad chemical priors while FT corrects local energetic errors with very little data.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: FT does not solve representational deficiencies such as lack of long-range electrostatics or spin; if the foundation lacks required physics for a target (e.g., charged-defect long-range fields), FT with small local datasets may be insufficient without augmenting the representation or including explicit electrostatic features.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: When tackling defect/dopant tasks: generate a small, targeted DFT set sampling the defect configuration space (NEB images, migration endpoints), fine-tune using multi-head replay to avoid catastrophic forgetting, and include dispersion/electrostatic corrections or augment model physics when long-range interactions are important.

extracted_data.name_full: MPtrj dataset (Materials Project trajectories collection)
extracted_data.brief_description: The primary pretraining dataset used for MACE-MP-0: ≈1.5M DFT configurations derived from Materials Project static calculations and structural optimizations, covering a wide range of inorganic crystals and some molecular components; labeled with PBE energies/forces/stresses (with some entries using Hubbard U).
extracted_data.material_systems: Inorganic crystals across much of the periodic table (approx. 150k unique MP structures), small periodic unit cells (≈90% < 70 atoms), plus some molecular components; used to pretrain a foundation potential transferable to MOFs, catalysts and defects.
extracted_data.defect_types: MPtrj itself is largely composed of bulk/relaxed crystalline snapshots and MD/trajectory snapshots from Materials Project; it is not a targeted defect database. Defect-related examples in the paper come from fine-tuning/supplementary datasets rather than enumerated defect entries in MPtrj.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: DFT labels are PBE; in Materials Project some calculations include Hubbard U for specific transition-metal + O/F compositions, leading to energy inconsistencies; MPtrj configurations do not systematically include explicit electron chemical potential labels or charged-defect corrections.
extracted_data.target_properties: Energy, forces, stresses (used to train ML potential which is then used to compute defect formation energies, activation barriers, NEBs, phonons, etc.).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Dataset used to pretrain foundation MACE features (no special defect featurization inside dataset itself).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Large, heterogeneous collection of DFT-relaxation snapshots and static calculations; serves as broad coverage pretraining corpus so that atom-centered MACE features learn general chemical/geometric priors.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Dataset is not defect-centered; contains many periodic bulk/unit-cell snapshots but not an explicit strategy of pristine-vs-defect delta encodings.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: N/A (dataset description).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Used to train MACE models (see MACE entity).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: This dataset is the pretraining source for the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential; internal features/embeddings arise from training on MPtrj.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: ≈1.5M configurations (rough count given), derived from Materials Project static and structure-optimization tasks; DFT level PBE with occasional Hubbard U; mostly small periodic unit cells.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: The model pretrained on MPtrj generalizes to MOFs (QMOF) with MAE = 0.040 eV/atom and to many out-of-domain tasks after fine-tuning; UMAP analysis shows overlap in local environments between MPtrj training set and out-of-domain NEB defect images in specific tests.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Foundation trained on large MPtrj enables few-shot FT (5–100 points) to reach DFT-level accuracy for specific NEB/defect tasks, demonstrating efficiency of the foundation + FT workflow.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Training/validation splits for the foundation fit are described in SI; the paper reports overall trained-model errors (energy and force MAEs) on validation/test splits but detailed defect-specific split strategies are in appendices/SI.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Paper discusses systemic data issues in MPtrj (Hubbard U inconsistencies, magnetic order variability) as sources of error but does not present defect-specific ablations comparing defect-only vs bulk-only pretraining.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Size ≈1.5M configurations; foundation-model trained on MPtrj achieves energy MAE ≈18 meV/atom and force MAE ≈39 meV/Å (medium model).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: Foundation trained on MPtrj gives a model able to reproduce phonon dispersions (benchmarked in SI); however, MPtrj lacks explicit datasets targeted at phonon-scattering-by-defects or thermal-conductivity degradation, so direct training for defect-induced thermal transport is not demonstrated.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue breadth/diversity of MPtrj is sufficient to produce transferable atomic-environment priors captured by MACE, enabling out-of-domain simulations and efficient FT for defects and catalysis.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: MPtrj contains inconsistent application of Hubbard U for certain transition metals with O/F that introduces energetic discontinuities; magnetic-order variability across entries for the same material can contribute energy scatter (some materials vary by >100 meV/atom across magnetic orders), which may degrade defect-prediction accuracy in affected chemistries.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: When building/using foundation models for defect physics, curate/avoid inconsistent electronic-structure labels (Hubbard U), include representative charged/defect configurations or plan targeted fine-tuning, and consider adding explicit long-range electrostatics if charged defects or dilute screening are central to the target tasks.

Atomic cluster expansion for accurate and transferable interatomic potentials
