extracted_data.name_full: Base set of defect-site descriptors (period/group, defect-site index, neighbor counts)
extracted_data.brief_description: A small, defect-centered numeric encoding used for every impurity+site datapoint that records the impurity element period and group, a numeric defect-site index (encoding substitutional/interstitial site identity), and the number of Cd and X (Te/Se/S) nearest neighbors at that site.
extracted_data.material_systems: Cd-based chalcogenides: CdTe, CdSe, CdS, plus mixed-anion alloys CdTe0.5Se0.5 and CdSe0.5S0.5 (models trained on the first three and tested on mixed-anion compounds).
extracted_data.defect_types: Single-point defects only: substitutional dopants at Cd site (M_Cd) and X site (M_X), interstitials (M_i) at different interstitial positions (neutral/Cd-site/X-site variants), native vacancies and antisites (for intrinsic defect energetics). No defect complexes or Frenkel pairs were modeled.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Does not itself encode charge; used alongside other features (see oxidation-state entry). ML targets include charged-defect transition levels but the base vector only identifies site and coordination numerically.
extracted_data.target_properties: Used as part of feature sets to predict neutral-state formation enthalpy (ΔH) and charge transition levels ε(q1/q2); downstream E^f(E_F) vs Fermi level curves and screening (dominating impurities).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Defect-centered tabular/site-indexed feature vector (base)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: A compact tabular representation centered on the defect site: elemental identity encoded by period/group, discrete numeric defect-site index (0=M_Cd,1=M_X,0.5=neutral interstitial, 0.25/0.75 for interstitials biased to Cd/X site), and integer counts of Cd and X neighbors.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered: encodes only local site identity and coordination; used together with additional element/unit-cell-derived descriptors rather than encoding full supercell geometry.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Local environment captured coarsely via number of Cd and X neighbors (integer counts). No explicit radial/angular basis, no cutoff radius reported beyond implicit coordination shells from site identification; species information in base vector is categorical/ordinal (period/group indices and neighbor counts).
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none (tabular descriptors + classical regressors: Random Forest, Kernel Ridge, LASSO).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Used across the datasets in the paper (PBE and HSE data). Base descriptors included for all computed datapoints (PBE ΔH dataset: 989 points; PBE ε dataset: 2550 points; HSE ε dataset: 680 points).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Used as part of full feature sets when testing models trained on CdTe/CdSe/CdS and applied to out-of-sample mixed-anion compounds (CdTe0.5Se0.5 and CdSe0.5S0.5); contributed to the reported out-of-sample errors (see overall results).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Learning curves show error decreases with more training data when using the base vector plus other descriptors; base vector alone yields worse performance (see ablation comparisons), so base vector is necessary but not sufficient for data-efficiency.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Train/test splits done over the CdTe+CdSe+CdS pooled data with explicit out-of-sample evaluation on mixed-anion compounds; experiments included many random train draws (100 different models) to estimate mean and standard deviation; typical reported split used 90% training / 10% test for parity plots and RMSE estimates.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: This base set is the mandatory core in all ablations; comparisons were made by adding elemental or unit-cell defect properties on top of it (see separate entries).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Not predictive by itself; used within combined descriptor sets that achieved RMSEs reported elsewhere (e.g., ΔH combined descriptors test RMSE ~0.38 eV).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors treat a compact numeric encoding of the defect site as a necessary anchor to relate elemental/unit-cell features to a specific defect geometry and coordination; the site-index and neighbor counts capture the primary local coordination differences among substitutional/interstitial sites.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Very coarse — does not encode continuous geometry, strain, atomic distances, angular information, or long-range electrostatics; insufficient alone to reach best accuracies.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use as a minimal defect-centered scaffold but augment with unit-cell-derived energetic/electronic descriptors and elemental properties for accurate predictions; include explicit charge-related features when predicting transition levels.

extracted_data.name_full: Elemental property descriptor set (period, group, ionization energy, electronegativity, ionic radii, etc.)
extracted_data.brief_description: A featurization composed solely of tabulated elemental properties of the impurity atom (M) such as period, group, first ionization energy, electronegativity, ionic radius, and other scalar chemical descriptors.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to CdTe, CdSe, CdS and tested on mixed-anion variants; used as one of three main feature families.
extracted_data.defect_types: Same single-point defect types as in the study (substitutional M_Cd, M_X; interstitial M_i); elemental features only characterize the impurity species, not the site geometry.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: No explicit charge-state features included in elemental-only set; for transition-level models the oxidation-state features (O1,O2) were added to enable charge-aware modeling (see separate entry).
extracted_data.target_properties: ΔH (neutral formation enthalpy) and ε(q1/q2) (charge transition levels).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Elemental property fingerprint (tabular)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Encodes continuous chemical attributes of the impurity atom (ionization energy, electronegativity, ionic radii, period, group) to capture chemical trends in defect energetics.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Not defect-centered by itself — must be combined with base site encoding to refer to a particular defect instance.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: No local environment radial/ angular detail; species info is continuous scalar properties rather than one-hot encoding.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Used across the PBE and HSE datasets; fed into models trained on CdTe/CdSe/CdS data (sizes as in Table I).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Elemental-only models performed worse on out-of-sample mixed-anion compounds compared to models including unit-cell defect features (out-of-sample RMSEs larger: e.g., ΔH RFR out-of-sample RMSE ~0.84 eV with elemental-only vs ~0.52 eV combined).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Learning curves show elemental-only features give higher errors at all training sizes; combining with unit-cell features reduces needed data to reach a given RMSE.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Same training/test splits; comparisons were made by training identical regressors on each descriptor family to evaluate importance.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Served as a baseline; ablation shows substantially worse performance than unit-cell or combined descriptors (Tables II and III).
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Example: For PBE ΔH using RFR: test RMSE = 0.65 eV (elemental-only) vs 0.38 eV (elemental+unit-cell); out-of-sample RMSE for CdTe0.5Se0.5 = 0.84 eV (elemental-only) vs 0.52 eV (combined). For ε(q/q-1), elemental-only RFR test RMSE = 0.34 eV vs combined = 0.30 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Elemental properties carry useful chemical trend information but lack electronic/energetic context provided by explicit defect calculations, limiting predictive power.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Performs poorly for out-of-sample mixed compositions and lacks ability to capture host-dependent band-edge alignment effects.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Combine elemental descriptors with cheap (unit-cell) computed defect electronic/energetic features to improve transferability and accuracy.

extracted_data.name_full: Low-cost unit-cell defect calculation descriptors (energetic and electronic)
extracted_data.brief_description: Energetic and electronic quantities computed from a cheap 8-atom (Zinc Blende) unit-cell defect calculation for each impurity+site: formation enthalpy from unit cell (Cd-rich/intermediate/X-rich) and aligned valence/conduction band edges, used as features to improve ML predictions.
extracted_data.material_systems: CdTe, CdSe, CdS and mixed-anion tested; unit-cell defect calculations performed for the same impurity-site combinations as the supercell computations where available.
extracted_data.defect_types: Same single-point defect types (substitutional/interstitial) — unit-cell defect calculation performed for MCd, MX, or Mi in the 8-atom cell.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Unit cell calculations provide band-edge information; charged-defect correction and full-charge-state supercell corrections are handled in the DFT supercell calculations (Freysoldt) but the unit-cell features themselves are neutral-state energetic/electronic descriptors used by ML.
extracted_data.target_properties: ΔH and ε(q1/q2) prediction; unit-cell band edges show strong linear correlation with certain transition levels (+1/0, 0/-1).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Low-cost unit-cell defect feature embedding
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Uses properties from an inexpensive 8-atom defect calculation: unit-cell formation enthalpy (Cd-rich/intermediate/X-rich) and the valence/conduction band edges (universally aligned via deep Cd 5s core), providing host electronic context and energetic proxy for full supercell behavior.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered but computed in a small cell; acts as a compact surrogate for the larger supercell defect energetics.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Implicitly encodes local relaxation/energetics from the unit-cell DFT calculation; no explicit radial/angular basis disclosed; species present via actual DFT calculation.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Unit-cell features available for many points; highly correlated with supercell ΔH (|r| > 0.9 for ΔH) and with some transition levels (VB/CB edges |r| = 0.82/0.74 with +1/0 and 0/-1). Used across PBE and HSE modeling pipelines.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Inclusion of unit-cell features substantially improved out-of-sample performance on mixed-anion compounds compared to elemental-only features (Tables II–III); models with unit-cell features generalize better to CdTe0.5Se0.5 and CdSe0.5S0.5.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Adding unit-cell features reduced required training data to reach a target RMSE (learning curves show earlier saturation and lower asymptotic error when unit-cell features included). Example: ΔH test RMSE drops from ~0.65 eV (elemental-only) to ~0.45 eV (unit-cell-only) and to ~0.38 eV (combined).
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Compared in identical train/test/out-of-sample splits and over multiple random training draws; feature importance from Random Forest confirms unit-cell formation enthalpy is the top feature for ΔH prediction.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Ablation studies show unit-cell-only outperforms elemental-only; combined elemental+unit-cell gave best results. Feature importance analysis highlights unit-cell formation enthalpy and band-edge features.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Example metrics: For PBE ΔH using RFR: training RMSE = 0.20 eV (unit-cell features), test RMSE = 0.45 eV; combined features test RMSE = 0.38 eV. For ε(q/q-1) test RMSE using RFR: unit-cell-only = 0.33 eV, combined = 0.30 eV.
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors claim unit-cell defect properties capture key host-specific electronic structure (band edges) and energetic trends that are highly predictive for defect transition levels and formation enthalpies; they act as an inexpensive surrogate of supercell physics.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Unit-cell computations are cheaper but may not capture full supercell relaxation or long-range electrostatic/strain effects; some transition-levels differences between PBE and HSE remain and require additional handling.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Compute low-cost unit-cell defect properties (formation enthalpy, aligned VB/CB edges) to include as features; combine with elemental descriptors for best transferability and accuracy.

extracted_data.name_full: Explicit oxidation-state features (O1, O2) to encode charge transitions
extracted_data.brief_description: Two scalar features representing the impurity atom formal oxidation state (O1) and the host defect-site atom oxidation state (O2: +2 for Cd, -2 for Te/Se/S, 0 for interstitial), added so that O1-O2 equals the defect charge q and a single model can be trained for ε(q/q-1) across all q.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied for charge-transition modeling in CdTe, CdSe, CdS and tested on mixed-anion compounds.
extracted_data.defect_types: Single-point charged defects (substitutional/interstitial) across multiple integer charge states (+3..-3 in DFT supercells; ML targets ε(q/q-1) transitions).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicit charge-aware feature: O1 and O2 are added to descriptor sets to encode the expected charge q via O1-O2=q, enabling ML to learn ε(q/q-1) as one regression target rather than separate models per q; DFT computed charged-supercell energies used Freysoldt correction for physical charged-defect references.
extracted_data.target_properties: Charge transition levels ε(q1/q2) (all modeled transitions) and via these the Fermi-level-dependent formation energy E^f(q,E_F).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Charge-aware oxidation-state encoding
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Encodes nominal oxidation states of impurity and site as scalar features so charge differences map to q; this lets models learn patterns across different charge transitions.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered (applies to the impurity+site datapoint); ties directly to predicted charged-defect physics.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Oxidation states are scalars, not continuous electron-density features; no explicit long-range electrostatic descriptors included in ML input.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: none
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Used for ML of ε(q/q-1) across many PBE and HSE datapoints (see Table I for sizes); DFT charged calculations used for ground-truth with Freysoldt corrections.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Including oxidation-state features allowed training a single ε(q/q-1) model across multiple q and improved predictive generality; out-of-sample mixed-anion RMSE for ε with combined descriptors (including O1/O2) ~0.30–0.34 eV.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Encoding charge via oxidation states reduces number of distinct models to train and helps share information across charge states, improving sample efficiency relative to training separate models per transition.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Models for ε(q/q-1) used pooled transition data and included O1/O2 in all descriptor sets; model performance reported for random splits and out-of-sample tests.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Authors contrasted training separate models per transition vs single model with O1/O2 and found the latter convenient; feature importance shows O1 (impurity oxidation state) is highly important for ε predictions.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Using RFR with combined descriptors including O1/O2: test RMSE for ε(q/q-1) ~0.30 eV; out-of-sample RMSE ~0.33–0.34 eV (PBE-level).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Encoding oxidation states informs ML of the integer charge transfer context and allows learning of transition-level trends across different q values, improving generalization.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Formal oxidation states are approximate and may not capture partial charge localization or long-range electrostatic screening; ML still depends on DFT corrections for charged-supercell effects.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Include simple oxidation-state features when training unified models for charge transition levels; continue to apply proper charged-supercell corrections (Freysoldt) for DFT labels.

extracted_data.name_full: Using lower-fidelity (PBE) transition levels as features and delta-learning to predict higher-fidelity (HSE) levels
extracted_data.brief_description: For scarce high-fidelity HSE data, the authors include PBE-computed ε(q1/q2) as an additional descriptor and/or train models on the difference δ = HSE - PBE (delta-learning), yielding substantially improved HSE prediction accuracy.
extracted_data.material_systems: HSE ε(q/q-1) modeling for CdTe, CdSe, CdS and mixed-anion compounds where only limited HSE data exist (HSE dataset ~680 points vs PBE ~2550).
extracted_data.defect_types: Single-point charged defects and the same transition levels (+2/+1 to -1/-2 for HSE subset).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: PBE ε values include charged-defect information; delta-learning models the difference between HSE and PBE transition levels (which are charge-state aware), and predicted HSE = PBE + predicted δ.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE-level ε(q/q-1) transition levels (higher-fidelity electronic defect levels).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Cross-fidelity descriptor (PBE embedding) and delta-learning
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Adds the inexpensive/low-fidelity DFT prediction (PBE ε) as a numeric feature to ML models for HSE labels; alternatively, directly regress δ = HSE - PBE and combine with PBE to get HSE estimates.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered: PBE prediction corresponds to the same impurity+site instance (so used as a per-datapoint scalar embedding).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: PBE ε is a scalar per transition and implicitly summarizes local and host-dependent electronic structure within the lower-fidelity theory.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none (applied with Random Forest regression and compared to KRR and LASSO).
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: This is an example of leveraging a lower-fidelity computed embedding rather than ML pretraining; not a neural foundation model.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: HSE ε dataset small (~680 points); PBE ε available for many more (~2550). Including PBE as a descriptor reduced test and out-of-sample RMSE for HSE from ~0.60 eV (without PBE) down to ~0.23 eV (with PBE); delta-learning gave test RMSE ~0.20–0.22 eV (Table IV).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Including PBE boosts generalization to out-of-sample mixed-anion compounds: example out-of-sample RMSE for HSE with PBE descriptor ≈ 0.20–0.22 eV; PBE and HSE ε are highly correlated (>0.95) which underlies success.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Delta-learning and adding PBE drastically reduce required HSE training data to reach a given error; error curves saturate earlier and at lower RMSE when PBE included.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: HSE models trained on the available HSE subset from CdTe/CdSe/CdS and evaluated on held-out tests and out-of-sample mixed compositions; comparisons made between models with and without PBE as descriptor and δ-learn models.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Ablation shows including only PBE as sole descriptor yields comparable performance to richer descriptor sets with PBE; delta-learning of δ gave lowest test/out-of-sample RMSEs among methods tested.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Representative numbers: HSE ε RFR test RMSE without PBE ~0.61 eV, with PBE ~0.23 eV; δ-learn (RFR) test RMSE ~0.20 eV; out-of-sample RMSEs similarly reduced to ~0.20–0.26 eV (Table IV, Fig. 6).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Because PBE and HSE ε are strongly correlated, PBE provides a powerful, low-cost embedding that transfers information about defect level trends; delta-learning captures systematic shifts between fidelities.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Relies on availability of a correlated low-fidelity theory (here PBE); if PBE-HSE correlation is weaker for other materials or defect types, the approach may be less effective. Some HSE outliers (Cu and Sn interstitials) degrade RMSE until removed.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: When high-fidelity labels are scarce, include lower-fidelity predictions as features or apply delta-learning; validate correlation between fidelities and check for outlier defect chemistries where systematic offsets fail.

extracted_data.name_short: Overall ML pipeline (RFR/KRR/LASSO with combined descriptors)
extracted_data.name_full: Random Forest / Kernel Ridge / LASSO regressors trained on combined elemental + unit-cell + base descriptors (with charge features) for defect energetics and transition levels
extracted_data.brief_description: A supervised learning pipeline using tabular defect-centered descriptors (base + elemental + unit-cell; plus oxidation states and optionally PBE ε) fed into classical regressors (Random Forest Regression, Kernel Ridge Regression with Gaussian kernel, and LASSO), with Random Forest performing best for out-of-sample screening.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to CdTe, CdSe, CdS training set and tested on mixed-anion CdTe0.5Se0.5 and CdSe0.5S0.5; HSE models used smaller subsets.
extracted_data.defect_types: Single-point substitutional/interstitial/ vacancy/antisite defects; per-datapoint modeling of impurity+site (no complexes).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: DFT labels included explicit charged-supercell calculations (+3 to -3) with Freysoldt corrections; ML models predict charge transition levels ε and use oxidation-state features to capture q-dependence; final E^f(E_F) curves assembled from ML ΔH and ε predictions to classify dominating impurities.
extracted_data.target_properties: Neutral formation enthalpy ΔH, charge transition levels ε(q1/q2), and derived Fermi-level-dependent formation energy E^f(E_F); used for screening dominating impurities that can shift equilibrium Fermi level.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Tabular defect-centered descriptor + classical regressor pipeline
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Concatenate base site indices, elemental descriptors, unit-cell defect features, and charge/oxidation-state scalars into a single feature vector per defect instance; train Random Forest / KRR / LASSO to regress ΔH or ε.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Defect-centered (each feature vector corresponds to a specific impurity at a specific site); unit-cell computation gives a local reference rather than full-supercell geometry.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Local geometry represented only via site index and neighbor counts plus unit-cell DFT relaxation results; no explicit radial/angular basis or rotational equivariance used.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: none
extracted_data.pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings: No neural pretraining used; PBE predictions used as cross-fidelity embeddings for HSE modeling/delta-learning.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: PBE ΔH dataset: 989 computed points across 1827 possible combinations (~54% coverage); PBE ε dataset: 2550 points (~23% of 10962 possible transitions); HSE ε dataset: 680 points (~9.3% of 7308).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Explicit out-of-sample test on mixed-anion compounds (not present in training): ΔH combined-descriptor test RMSE ~0.38 eV (test) and out-of-sample ~0.52–0.57 eV; ε combined-descriptor RFR test RMSE ~0.30 eV and out-of-sample ~0.30–0.34 eV. Classification of whether impurity 'dominates' intrinsic defects: ML agrees with DFT in >95% of cases (false pos+neg <5%).
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Learning curves show RMSE improves with training size and begins to saturate; ~50% of PBE ΔH data gives ΔH test RMSE ~0.40 eV and out-of-sample ~0.55 eV. For HSE, adding PBE as descriptor reduces HSE RMSE substantially, supporting cross-fidelity data-efficiency.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Models trained on pooled CdTe+CdSe+CdS data (often 90% training /10% test), uncertainties estimated from 100 random train draws; explicit out-of-sample evaluation on intentionally unseen mixed-anion compounds; feature importance reported from Random Forest; no graph/neural cross-validation reported.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Systematic comparisons between three descriptor families (elemental-only, unit-cell-only, combined) and three regressors (RFR, KRR, LASSO) show: unit-cell features >> elemental-only; combined best; RFR best for out-of-sample screening though KRR sometimes slightly better on test set; LASSO worst generally. Including PBE as descriptor or delta-learning significantly improves HSE predictions.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Key reported RMSEs (eV): PBE ΔH (RFR, combined) test RMSE = 0.38 eV, out-of-sample ~0.52–0.57 eV; PBE ε(q/q-1) (RFR, combined) test RMSE = 0.30 eV, out-of-sample ~0.30–0.34 eV; HSE ε with PBE descriptor (RFR) test RMSE ≈ 0.23 eV, out-of-sample ≈ 0.20–0.26 eV; δ-learn (RFR) test RMSE ≈ 0.20 eV (Table II–IV). Classification (dominating impurity) agreement: >95% concordance with DFT (false pos+neg <5%).
extracted_data.phonon_or_thermal_transport_link: none — paper does not model phonon scattering, scattering rates, or lattice thermal conductivity degradation.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: The combination of elemental and unit-cell defect properties captures both chemical trends and host electronic/energetic context (e.g., band-edge alignment) that determine defect levels; Random Forest feature importances confirm the unit-cell formation enthalpy and impurity oxidation state as top predictors for ΔH and ε respectively.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Does not include explicit long-range electrostatic descriptors beyond unit-cell band-edges; limited HSE data constrains high-fidelity predictions; some HSE outliers (Cu, Sn interstitials) cause higher RMSE until excluded; no treatment of defect complexes or phonon-related transport properties; unit-cell surrogates may miss supercell relaxation effects.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Use combined elemental + unit-cell defect descriptors as a strong baseline; include oxidation-state features for charge transitions; apply Freysoldt corrections for DFT charged labels; use PBE predictions as auxiliary features or delta-learn to predict scarce high-fidelity labels; validate transferability with out-of-sample mixed-composition tests and report uncertainties via ensemble methods.

extracted_data.name_full: Modified Band Alignment correction (MBA)
extracted_data.brief_description: An empirical, band-gap-dependent correction to align defect charge-transition levels and formation energies from low-fidelity (LDA/GGA/PBE) calculations to hybrid (HSE) accuracy by applying an electrostatic-potential-derived shift plus a single fitted linear-in-gap term (β) and a constant formation-energy offset (γ).
extracted_data.material_systems: Primary: zincblende III-V dilute bismides (Ga-V:Bi: GaP/GaAs/GaSb; In-V:Bi; Al-V:Bi). Also tested on CdX (X = S, Se, Te) chalcogenides (from Ref. [46]). Multiple hosts used for training and testing.
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects (substitutional Bi on III and V sites, vacancies, antisites) and pair/complex defects (nearest- and second-nearest-neighbor pairs). Charges analyzed ranged -5 to +5 (stable states mainly ±2 or ±3); pair defect complexes included.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicit charge labels q are used in formation energy formulas; Fermi level E_F treated as variable; Freysoldt (FNV) electrostatic correction applied to charged-supercell energies; MBA projection includes q-dependent terms and an empirical constant γ to correct formation energies.
extracted_data.target_properties: Defect formation energies, charge-state transition (defect) levels referenced to VBM, binding energies of defect pairs.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Band-alignment-based numerical correction (MBA)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Start from LDA/GGA defect charge-transition energies E^d; add an average electrostatic-potential shift E_shift (from pristine LDA vs HSE), then apply a band-gap-scaled linear correction: E_corr^d = E^d + E_shift + β((1-δ)E_g - E^d) (δ set to 0), and project to formation energies with an additional constant γ; β and γ are fitted empirically on a training set.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Uses pristine (undefected) reference: alignment of average electrostatic potential of pure cell between low- and high-fidelity calculations; not a local structural descriptor, but references defect energies to a pristine host baseline.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not applicable — MBA is not a local atomic descriptor but a scalar correction applied to computed defect energies/levels; no neighbor cutoff or angular/radial basis reported.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Parameters (β = -0.14, γ = 0.839 eV, δ = 0) fitted on Ga-V:Bi dataset (188 stable defect levels for Ga-V:Bi training set). Validated on In-V:Bi (198 point-defect formation energies calculated with both LDA and HSE) and on an external CdX dataset of 656 PBE→HSE charge-transition levels from Ref. [46]. Full produced database: 2673 defect formation energies (mix of direct HSE and LDA+MBA).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Fitted on Ga-V:Bi and applied without refit to In-V:Bi: MBA defect-level MAE = 0.175 eV (ME ≈ -0.009 eV) vs HSE; formation-energy MAE = 0.384 eV. Applied to CdX (PBE→HSE) data: defect-level MAE = 0.194 eV (ME ≈ -0.006 eV). These show significant accuracy gains vs BA and direct LDA/PBE and demonstrate reasonable transfer across similar semiconductor chemistries and across semi-local functionals.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Authors report that re-optimizing MBA parameters with as few as ~10 points produces noticeable improvement; MBA has only one (β) (for levels) and one (γ) (for formation energies) major fitted parameters, indicating high data efficiency compared to ML that requires larger HSE+LDA training sets.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Parameters optimized by minimizing RMSE on Ga-V:Bi training data; validation performed on held-out In-V:Bi dataset (explicitly computed with both LDA and HSE) and on external CdX dataset. Parity plots, MAE/RMSE/ME and precision/recall/F1 for stability/classification used for assessment. No use of graph splits — evaluation is across material systems (train on Ga-V:Bi, test on In-V:Bi and CdX).
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Direct LDA/GGA baseline and standard Band Alignment (BA) correction (constant E_shift) used as baselines. MBA reduces MAE relative to BA (e.g., Ga-V:Bi defect levels MAE BA=0.226 eV -> MBA=0.182 eV). Ablations include setting δ = 0 (simpler 1-parameter correction) justified by information criteria; sensitivity to needing reoptimization for other crystal structures/supercell sizes tested.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Ga-V:Bi (defect levels): LDA MAE = 0.439 eV -> BA MAE = 0.226 eV -> MBA MAE = 0.182 eV; (formation energies at E_F = 0): LDA MAE = 1.612 eV -> BA MAE = 0.904 eV -> MBA MAE = 0.370 eV (with γ chosen to set ME=0). In-V:Bi (test): defect levels MBA MAE = 0.175 eV; formation energies MBA MAE = 0.384 eV. CdX test (656 levels): MBA MAE = 0.194 eV. RMSE and ME statistics given in Table I of paper.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Authors argue the dominant discrepancy between local/semi-local and hybrid defect levels is a band-alignment/band-gap effect (hence a constant + band-gap-dependent linear term suffices). MBA addresses systematic overestimation near bottom of gap after BA by adding a gap-scaled term. Remaining errors attributed to LDA/GGA inability to capture charge-density reorganization (especially q=0) and localization/Jahn-Teller effects.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: MBA cannot correct q = 0 formation energies through band-alignment projection (intrinsic limitation); it can mispredict stability/classification when LDA lacks certain charge-state transitions (outliers where LDA/BA/MBA predict different stable charge states than HSE); parameters may require reoptimization for different crystal structures, supercell sizes, or significantly different chemistries; somewhat less effective for very low band gap materials but still improved ME/MAE.
extracted_data.recommended_best_practices: Compute E_shift from average electrostatic potential of pristine cell with at least one HSE primitive calculation; apply FNV electrostatic corrections consistently; fit MBA β (and γ for formation energies) on a small representative set (authors show ~10 points already useful) when switching to different crystal structures/supercell sizes; include spin-orbit coupling and consistent supercell size to improve transferability; use MBA as a fast multifidelity route before expensive HSE calculations.

extracted_data.name_full: Band Alignment correction (BA) using average electrostatic potential
extracted_data.brief_description: A prior method aligning defect charge-transition levels between semi-local (LDA/GGA/PBE) and hybrid (HSE) functionals by adding a constant shift E_shift derived from the difference in averaged electrostatic potential of the pure host computed with both functionals; formation energies projected as q·E_shift.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to same III-V:Bi systems (Ga-, In-, Al-based) in this paper; BA previously used in other defect studies across semiconductors in literature.
extracted_data.defect_types: Same as MBA application: point defects and pair defects in zincblende III–V and test CdX systems.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Includes explicit q in projected formation-energy correction E^f_corr = E^f + q E_shift; relies on FNV electrostatic correction to charged-supercell energies.
extracted_data.target_properties: Charge-state transition levels, formation energies, binding energies (via projection).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Constant band-alignment shift (BA)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Compute E_shift = avg(electrostatic potential difference between HSE and LDA for pristine cell) and add to all LDA defect levels: E_corr^d = E^d + E_shift; project to formation energies as qE_shift.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Uses pristine-reference average electrostatic potential (global alignment), not a local defect-centered structural featurization.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not applicable.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Applied on same datasets as MBA; initial BA assessed on Ga-V:Bi (training set), compared to MBA and LDA.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: BA improves over raw LDA but shows systematic overestimation near the bottom of the gap and material-dependent bias (especially for larger band gap materials). BA MAE on Ga-V:Bi defect levels = 0.226 eV vs LDA 0.439 eV; BA performed less well than MBA on In-V:Bi and CdX tests.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Only requires a single primitive-cell HSE calculation for each host to compute E_shift, making it data-efficient and cheap.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Compared to HSE reference for defect levels and formation energies across Ga-V:Bi dataset and on In-V:Bi and CdX test sets.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Used as baseline for MBA and ML comparisons; BA partially corrects band-gap underestimation but cannot address position-dependent errors within the gap.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: See Table I: BA defect levels MAE (Ga-V:Bi) = 0.226 eV; formation energies MAE = 0.904 eV (Ga-V:Bi). CdX BA MAE = 0.230 eV (defect levels).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Captures major band-alignment contribution to the discrepancy between semi-local and hybrid functionals by aligning reference potentials; residuals attributed to localization and other physics not captured by constant shift.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Systematic over/underestimation across gap, cannot correct q = 0 formation energies, performs worse than MBA when position-in-gap dependence exists.

extracted_data.name_full: LDA/GGA-derived scalar feature set used for ML regression
extracted_data.brief_description: A compact feature vector assembled from quantities available at LDA/GGA cost: defect formation energy, charge state, host band gap, FNV electrostatic correction magnitude, total energy, and Bader charge analyses, used as inputs to regressors/NNs to predict HSE-level defect properties.
extracted_data.material_systems: Ga-V:Bi training/test splits, In-V:Bi test and internal experiments; features in principle general for other semiconductors.
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects (and could extend to pairs) for charge states across -5 to +5 (stable range used).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Charge state included as an explicit scalar feature; Fermi-level dependent quantities (formation energy at E_F) are included; FNV correction magnitude included as a scalar feature to capture electrostatic finite-size effects.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE defect formation energies and charge transition levels.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Scalar LDA/GGA defect features
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Concatenate scalar outputs of inexpensive DFT calculations (e.g., uncorrected formation energy, q, band gap of host, FNV correction, total energy, Bader charges) to form a fixed-length feature vector for conventional ML regressors (linear regression, NN, random forest).
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Features are global scalars derived from defective-supercell outputs and from pristine host properties (pristine band gap), so include both defect and host reference information but do not form an explicit defect-centered graph.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: No explicit local neighbor cutoff or atomic-environment basis used; atomic localization captured indirectly via Bader charge summary features.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Built from LDA/HSE paired calculations for Ga-V:Bi (used for training/validation) and In-V:Bi; number of examples for ML exploration not given explicitly but training used the computed datasets (hundreds of defects), cross-validated with leave-system-out CV.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Linear regression using these features showed similar performance to MBA on In-V:Bi; more complex NN trained on these features achieved comparable MAE to MBA and transferred reasonably when cross-validated by leaving systems out. However ML requires HSE training labels for supervised fitting.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Linear multivariable regression showed strong coefficients for charge state and formation energy indicating a low-dimensional dominant effect; NN required modest hyperparameter tuning but benefit from the inclusion of formation-energy and charge features. No explicit few-shot curves beyond MBA remarks.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Leave-system-out cross validation and random 5-fold CV reported. Leave-system-out CV MAE for defect levels ~0.195 eV (ME ≈ 0.04 eV); formation energy MAE ≈ 0.343 eV.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Authors compared linear regression importance (charge & formation energy dominant) vs neural networks (3-layer) and found NN not substantially better than MBA despite heavier training cost. Inclusion of Bader features and FNV improved model but band-alignment-like variables dominated.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Neural network (3-layer 128-64-32) leave-system-out CV: defect levels MAE ≈ 0.195 eV (ME = 0.04 eV); formation energies MAE ≈ 0.343 eV (ME = -0.115 eV). Random 5-fold CV showed only marginal improvement.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Feature importance analysis indicates that the band-alignment/band-gap shift (captured by formation energy and charge-state terms) is the primary factor explaining differences between low/high fidelity calculations; Bader charges capture localization effects but contribute less.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Requires HSE labels for supervised fitting (making training expensive); more computationally intensive than MBA; may be less transferable without retraining; cannot directly recover atomic-scale spatial features unless augmented with local descriptors.

extracted_data.name_full: Feedforward neural network (3-layer: 128-64-32 nodes)
extracted_data.brief_description: A fully connected neural network with three hidden layers (128, 64, 32 neurons) trained on LDA/GGA-derived scalar features to predict HSE defect formation energies and defect levels.
extracted_data.material_systems: Trained/validated on III-V:Bi LDA/HSE paired datasets (Ga-V:Bi training, In-V:Bi validation) in the paper's ML exploration.
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects (various substitutional, vacancies, antisites) across charge states.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Charge state included as an explicit input feature.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE defect formation energies and charge-transition levels.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Feedforward descriptor-to-target NN
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Dense feedforward architecture taking scalar LDA-derived features (formation energy, q, band gap, FNV correction, total energy, Bader metrics) as input; trained under leave-system-out CV and 5-fold CV.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Uses scalar defect-level outputs and host properties as input — not an explicit defect-centered graph.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: None beyond Bader charge scalars; no explicit neighbor cutoffs or atomic environment basis used.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Feedforward MLP (not an equivariant/graph model).
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Trained on Ga-V:Bi LDA/HSE paired data and validated by leave-system-out CV; dataset size corresponds to the computed defect examples in the paper (hundreds).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: NN performance similar to MBA on validation (MAE ~0.195 eV for defect levels), but ML requires retraining with HSE labels for new chemistries; no evidence of large-scale cross-chemistry generalization without retraining.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: No explicit few-shot learning curves for NN reported; authors note NN required modest hyperparameter searches and was more computationally intensive than MBA.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Leave-system-out cross validation; random 5-fold CV reported as marginally better.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared against linear regression (feature importance analysis) and MBA/BA baselines; NN led to similar MAE to MBA but at higher cost.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Leave-system-out CV: defect levels ME ≈ 0.04 eV, MAE ≈ 0.195 eV; formation energies ME ≈ -0.115 eV, MAE ≈ 0.343 eV.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: NN can nonlinearly combine LDA-derived scalars to capture residuals not explained by band alignment, but the dominant band-alignment effect makes simple corrections like MBA competitive.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Requires paired HSE labels for supervised training; heavier computational overhead; limited interpretability relative to MBA.

extracted_data.name_full: Freysoldt–Neugebauer–Van de Walle (FNV) electrostatic finite-size correction
extracted_data.brief_description: An established correction scheme for charged-defect supercell DFT calculations that removes spurious electrostatic interactions between periodic defect images by aligning local potentials and applying an analytic image-charge correction using dielectric screening.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied to all charged-defect DFT calculations in the paper across III-V:Bi and CdX validations.
extracted_data.defect_types: Charged point defects and charged defect complexes in supercell calculations.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicitly corrects charged-supercell total energies; experimental dielectric constants used for screening where available (authors note LDA-calculated dielectric constants are acceptable when experimental are unknown). FNV correction magnitude also used as an input feature in ML experiments.
extracted_data.target_properties: Corrected defect formation energies and charge-transition levels.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Electrostatic finite-size correction (FNV)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Align local electrostatic potentials between defected and pristine supercells and apply image-charge correction using dielectric constant to obtain formation energies corrected for periodic-image electrostatics.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Uses spatial average in potential region between periodic images of defect to compute alignment; not a featurization per se but produces a scalar correction.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Region chosen as 30% of the potential area between periodic images for averaging; dielectric constants taken from experiment or LDA when needed.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Applied for all DFT defect calculations in this study (64-atom supercells) and used as input feature in ML models.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Standard, widely used method; authors note FNV works with 64-atom cells giving errors ≲0.16 eV for defect formation energies when compared to much larger cells for typical charges.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Not applicable.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Applied consistently to all charged defect DFT outputs; alignment region and procedure kept consistent across dataset.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Not compared to other electrostatic corrections in this paper; authors used FNV by default.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Authors estimate errors due to supercell size after FNV correction up to ~0.16 eV (from convergence tests reported).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Necessary to remove spurious periodic electrostatic interactions so that band-alignment corrections and ML regressors can operate on physically meaningful formation energies.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Supercell-convergence residual errors remain (~0.16 eV for worst cases reported); relies on choice of dielectric constant (experimental preferred).

extracted_data.name_full: Machine-learned impurity level prediction for semiconductors: the example of Cd-based chalcogenides
extracted_data.brief_description: A prior work (Mannodi-Kanakkithodi et al.) that trained ML models (including Random Forest Regression) to predict hybrid-functional (HSE) defect levels from PBE defect levels and elemental/descriptive features for CdX (CdS, CdSe, CdTe) and alloys; used as an external benchmark comparison.
extracted_data.citation_title: Machine-learned impurity level prediction for semiconductors: the example of Cd-based chalcogenides
extracted_data.material_systems: Cd-based chalcogenides (CdS, CdSe, CdTe) and alloys.
extracted_data.defect_types: Impurities and defects (single-species point defects / impurities with various charge states) used in their published dataset.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Included PBE-calculated defect levels at different charge states; ML predicted levels referenced to HSE; specifics of charge-handling in their model not exhaustively reproduced here but PBE defect information was a key input.
extracted_data.target_properties: Charge-state transition levels (PBE→HSE mapping).
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Elemental properties + PBE defect levels used as ML features (RFR and other regressors)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: The ML uses elemental descriptors of impurities and the PBE-calculated defect level(s) as primary inputs to predict the corresponding HSE defect levels; best reported model was Random Forest Regression with RMSE ≈ 0.24 eV on 10% left-out test set.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Features include PBE defect outputs and elemental features — implicitly using defective-supercell results as input (not explicit defect-centered graph).
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not a local atomic-environment descriptor; features were elemental/chemical plus PBE-computed defect properties.
extracted_data.graph_model_architecture: Random Forest Regression (RFR) used as best average ML model in their study.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Dataset size: 656 PBE→HSE defect charge-state transition levels (used by Polak et al. for MBA validation); dataset publicly available and used as an external test in this paper.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Polak et al. compared MBA vs the ML model on the same CdX data: ML RFR RMSE = 0.24 eV on internal 10% left-out test; on out-of-sample alloy systems (CdTe0.5Se0.5 and CdSe0.5S0.5) ML RMSE = 0.235 eV while MBA RMSE = 0.267 eV, indicating ML had somewhat better out-of-sample performance in that test.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: The ML model requires PBE defect levels and HSE targets for training; reported cross-validation and out-of-sample performance demonstrates reasonable generalization for related chemistries but requires substantial labeled data.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: 10% left-out test set cross-validation and out-of-sample alloy tests reported in Ref. [46]; used by authors here for direct comparison.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: ML used elemental features with PBE defect levels; compared to BA/MBA approaches in the present paper; RFR was best single-model reported in Ref. [46].
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Ref. [46] reported best average ML model RMSE = 0.24 eV (10% left-out test); out-of-sample alloys RMSE = 0.235 eV. Polak et al. report MBA RMSE ~0.240±0.035 eV on same main dataset and MBA RMSE = 0.267 eV on the out-of-sample alloys.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Using PBE-computed defect levels as inputs allows ML to effectively learn the mapping to HSE, indicating much of the discrepancy can be learned from semi-local outputs plus elemental descriptors.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Requires curated PBE→HSE paired datasets for training; may need retraining for very different chemistries or cell sizes; performance advantage over MBA on out-of-sample tests is modest.

extracted_data.name_full: Ga-V:Bi first-principles defect dataset (this work)
extracted_data.brief_description: The paper's main high-fidelity dataset: comprehensive HSE and LDA calculations of point defects and nearest/second-nearest pair defects in GaP:Bi, GaAs:Bi, and GaSb:Bi across multiple charge states, used to fit and validate BA/MBA and ML models.
extracted_data.material_systems: GaP:Bi, GaAs:Bi, GaSb:Bi (zincblende III-V dilute bismides).
extracted_data.defect_types: 27 defect types per material: 6 point defects (Bi_III, Bi_V, v_III, v_V, III_V antisite, V_III antisite) and 21 pair defects (nearest- and second-nearest neighbor pairs). Charges -5..+5 analyzed (stable states mostly up to ±3).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Explicitly enumerated charges; Freysoldt (FNV) electrostatic correction applied; defect levels and formation energies evaluated as function of Fermi level.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE-calculated defect formation energies, charge transition levels, and binding energies; used as ground truth for fitting β and γ and training ML.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: DFT-computed scalar defect outputs (used for downstream corrections/ML)
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Provides both low-fidelity (LDA/PBE) and high-fidelity (HSE) defect-level and formation-energy pairs; features derived from these outputs were used for regression and band-alignment corrections.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Supercell-based defective calculations referenced to pristine host electrostatic potential; no specialized defect-centered graph representations used.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: DFT relaxations with spin-orbit coupling included; no explicit neighbor cutoff descriptors beyond atomic relaxations reported.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: 188 stable defect levels reported for Ga-V:Bi training set; total computed database across III-V:Bi families includes 2673 defect formation energies (mix of direct HSE and LDA+MBA-corrected values).
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: Used as the main training set for MBA parameter selection; successful transfer tested on In-V:Bi and CdX.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Large number of defects (hundreds) allowed robust empirical fitting of MBA parameters and ML leave-system-out CV.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Direct HSE calculations used as reference for parity plots and error statistics; LDA baseline compared and BA/MBA corrections applied to LDA results.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Used for ablation between LDA, BA, MBA and ML outcomes; helped reveal position-in-gap dependent biases of BA.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: See Table I entries for Ga-V:Bi (formation energy, defect levels, binding energy metrics for LDA, BA, MBA).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Large, chemically consistent dataset enables quantification of band-alignment errors and empirical correction across many defect types and charge states.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Supercell size (64-atom) imposes residual finite-size errors (~0.16 eV). Dataset is specific to zincblende III-V Bi-doped systems; generalization to other crystal structures may require refitting.

extracted_data.name_full: In-V:Bi LDA/HSE point-defect test dataset
extracted_data.brief_description: Independent set of point-defect calculations in InP:Bi, InAs:Bi, InSb:Bi computed with identical protocols (both LDA and HSE) to validate MBA transferability.
extracted_data.material_systems: InP:Bi, InAs:Bi, InSb:Bi (zincblende In-based dilute bismides).
extracted_data.defect_types: Single-species point defects analogous to Ga-V:Bi set (198 defect formation energies enumerated).
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Same charged-state enumeration and FNV corrections as Ga-V:Bi; used as an external test set for MBA and ML.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE defect formation energies and defect levels used for validation.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: DFT-computed paired LDA/HSE defect outputs
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Independent HSE and LDA calculations used to test transferability of MBA parameters and ML regressors.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Pristine-reference alignment used; no specialized featurization beyond DFT outputs.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: As per main calculations (HSE-relaxed structures with SOC); no explicit neighbor-basis descriptors.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: 198 formation energies (3 hosts × 6 point defects × 11 charge states enumerated), all computed with both LDA and HSE.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: MBA with parameters fitted on Ga-V:Bi produced defect-level MAE = 0.175 eV and formation-energy MAE = 0.384 eV on In-V:Bi, demonstrating transferability within III-V:Bi family.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Validation highlights MBA transferability without retraining; authors also tested refitting with small numbers (~10) of points for different datasets.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Used as an independent test dataset; parity plots and error-statistics reported.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared direct LDA, BA, and MBA predictions vs HSE for In-V:Bi.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: In-V:Bi MBA: defect levels MAE = 0.175 eV (ME ≈ -0.009 eV); formation energies MAE = 0.384 eV (ME ≈ 0.236 eV).
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Successful validation suggests MBA parameters fitted on Ga-V:Bi capture major systematic differences between LDA and HSE in similar III-V dilute-bismide chemistries.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Authors note In-V:Bi are chemically similar to Ga-V:Bi and therefore represent a favorable test; different crystal structures or very different chemistries may still require refitting.

extracted_data.name_full: Two-fidelity (LDA/GGA low fidelity + HSE high fidelity) multifidelity strategy
extracted_data.brief_description: A practical approach combining many inexpensive low-fidelity DFT defect calculations with a small number of high-fidelity HSE references (primitive cell or sample defects) to produce corrected defect energetics efficiently via BA/MBA or ML.
extracted_data.material_systems: Applied across III-V:Bi systems and validated on CdX; general multifidelity concept referenced in literature (Refs. [46,64,65]).
extracted_data.defect_types: Point defects and pair defects across charge states; multifidelity used to scale up coverage of defect space.
extracted_data.charge_state_handling: Low-fidelity explicit q retained; E_shift derived from high-fidelity pristine calculations; q-dependent projections used for formation energies.
extracted_data.target_properties: HSE-accurate defect formation energies and defect levels approximated from LDA/GGA data with limited HSE references.
extracted_data.representation_strategy_name: Multifidelity band-alignment correction
extracted_data.representation_strategy_description: Use LDA/GGA computed defect outputs en masse and correct them toward HSE using information from a small number of HSE pristine calculations (for E_shift) and/or a few HSE defect examples to fit MBA parameters; alternative is ML trained on matched low/high fidelity pairs.
extracted_data.defect_centering_or_reference: Pristine-reference via high-fidelity primitive-cell calculations combined with defective low-fidelity supercell outputs.
extracted_data.local_environment_descriptor_details: Not applicable beyond LDA outputs and any extra scalar features (Bader, FNV) used.
extracted_data.data_regime_and_dataset: Large-scale low-fidelity LDA/GGA computed defect sets (thousands of defects when corrected) combined with few high-fidelity HSE calculations that anchor the corrections; in this study about one HSE primitive cell per host used for E_shift plus HSE defect calculations for parts of dataset.
extracted_data.transferability_evidence: MBA is a practical embodiment of multifidelity approach and shows transfer across similar systems with small high-fidelity anchoring data; other multifidelity ML literature cited and supports approach.
extracted_data.data_efficiency_evidence: Authors emphasize computational savings (~20× faster than full HSE for systems studied) while achieving HSE-like accuracy via MBA; benefit increases with number of low-fidelity calculations.
extracted_data.evaluation_protocol: Fit on HSE-rich subset, applied to large LDA/GGA set; compared to direct full-HSE where available.
extracted_data.baselines_and_ablations: Compared to full HSE (gold standard) and pure LDA/PBE baselines; MBA reduces cost with modest accuracy loss.
extracted_data.performance_metrics: Computational cost reduction ~20× reported for systems studied; numerical error metrics as in MBA/BA comparisons.
extracted_data.interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims: Much of the discrepancy between LDA and HSE is systematic and can be corrected using small-number high-fidelity anchors — enabling high-throughput defect databases with near-hybrid accuracy.
extracted_data.failure_modes_and_limitations: Requires at least some HSE references for alignment/parameter fitting; extrapolation to very different chemistries/crystal structures may require additional HSE data.
