theory-1.name: Charge-conditioned representations are required for multi-charge defect PES/CTL learning
theory-1.description: Phenomenon: ML models for defect-influenced properties (formation energies, PES topology, charge transition levels, charge-dependent forces/phonons) fail when multiple defect charge states are fit jointly from geometry alone. Mechanism claim (inference): for a fixed atomic geometry, the mapping to energy/forces/IFCs is non-injective across charge states because the electronic state changes without a unique geometric signature. Therefore, adding an explicit net-charge conditioning variable (as a token/embedding) is the dominant representational requirement for multi-charge modeling; model capacity or angular features alone will not substitute. This theory is about identifiability, not just optimization.
theory-1.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.

components.theory_name: Charge-conditioned representations are required for multi-charge defect PES/CTL learning
components.theory_description: Phenomenon: ML models for defect-influenced properties (formation energies, PES topology, charge transition levels, charge-dependent forces/phonons) fail when multiple defect charge states are fit jointly from geometry alone. Mechanism claim (inference): for a fixed atomic geometry, the mapping to energy/forces/IFCs is non-injective across charge states because the electronic state changes without a unique geometric signature. Therefore, adding an explicit net-charge conditioning variable (as a token/embedding) is the dominant representational requirement for multi-charge modeling; model capacity or angular features alone will not substitute. This theory is about identifiability, not just optimization.

theory_statements.statement_name: Joint multi-charge CTL bound requires explicit charge conditioning
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: In joint training across charge states, explicit charge conditioning dominates over geometry-only learning. For a single-host charged-defect dataset spanning ≥5 integer charge states, any geometry-only MLIP (no charge token/scalar/embedding provided to the model) will NOT achieve thermodynamic transition-level MAE ≤ 0.05 eV on a held-out set; adding an explicit net-charge input will achieve MAE ≤ 0.05 eV. NUMERIC THRESHOLDS: ≥5 charge states; CTL MAE bound 0.05 eV. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: doubling backbone parameter count (±10%) without charge input will NOT break the 0.05 eV MAE bound.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Single-host, non-metallic crystals; point vacancies in supercells; targets are CTLs derived from charge-dependent formation energies; training/eval include multiple q for the same defect type and supercell size.
special_cases: If models are trained separately per charge state (one model per q), this law does not apply.
Metals or cases where defect charge is not a well-defined localized state are excluded.
If CTLs are not evaluated (only E^f at fixed q), this law does not apply.

supporting_evidence.text: Charge-conditioned MACE with a learnable global charge embedding reproduced HSE06 thermodynamic transition levels within ~0.015 eV (max deviation ≤0.02 eV claimed) while also reproducing ground-state geometries (RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å), indicating that explicit charge conditioning enables high-precision charge-dependent energetics/CTLs in one model.

Foundation bulk-trained MLIPs without explicit charge conditioning systematically failed for charged-defect PESs in Sb2Se3, with defect-minimum RMSD typically ~0.2–0.4 Å and incorrect PES topology, consistent with the claim that geometry-only bulk-trained representations collapse charge-dependent landscapes.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Charge-aware NNP variants exist (e.g., global charge node Q_sys) and separate-per-charge models are common in defect ML.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A hard numeric generalization bound (CTL MAE ≤0.05 eV) as an identifiability test for joint multi-charge learning, and the claim that geometry-only models cannot meet it even with matched capacity.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Anchored in provided evidence where explicit charge embedding yields CTL errors ~0.015 eV; the risky part is the explicit failure bound for geometry-only joint models under the same dataset regime.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Using the Sb2Se3-style dataset construction (same initial distortions/trajectories), train two models with identical MACE backbone/hyperparameters: (A) no charge input; (B) add a net-charge conditioning input (either categorical embedding or scalar). Train jointly across ≥5 q. Compute CTLs from predicted formation energies and report CTL MAE on held-out trajectories.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Model (A) (geometry-only) achieves CTL MAE ≤ 0.05 eV on the held-out set, OR model (B) fails to reach CTL MAE ≤ 0.05 eV while (A) succeeds.

theory_statements.statement_name: Charge token must be injected before message passing to separate charge-dependent minima
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: conditioning must act on the representation, not only as a post-hoc energy shift. If the charge input is provided only as a geometry-independent additive scalar energy head (post-message-passing) and NOT injected into node features before message passing, the model will NOT achieve defect-minimum structural RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å across ≥5 charge states; injecting charge into per-atom embeddings before message passing WILL achieve RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å. NUMERIC THRESHOLDS: RMSD 0.10 Å; ≥5 charge states. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: the post-hoc-only charge shift model will produce RMSD ≥ 0.20 Å for at least 2 of the charge states.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Charged-defect structure relaxation with MLIP-driven optimization; single-host, fixed supercell size; evaluation compares relaxed minima against DFT (same functional as labels).
special_cases: If evaluation uses energies only (no relaxed structures), RMSD criterion is irrelevant.
If training data contain only near-minimum geometries (no PES coverage), both variants can fail.

supporting_evidence.text: In the charge-embedded Sb2Se3 model, charge embedding is added to atomic embeddings at initialization and propagated through message passing, and the resulting model achieves ground-state RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å across charge states, supporting the necessity of conditioning the learned interactions, not merely adding a constant offset.

Bulk-trained (charge-agnostic) foundations yield too-flat PESs and incorrect forces/relaxed minima (RMSD ~0.2–0.4 Å), consistent with the view that correct minima require charge-conditioned interactions.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Conditioning variables and auxiliary heads are standard in ML; some charge-aware NNPs add global charge nodes.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A specific architectural falsifier: post-hoc energy shift-only conditioning fails a structural criterion (RMSD ≤0.10 Å) while pre-message-passing injection succeeds, framed as a representational separation requirement for charge-dependent reconstructions.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: The evidence supports charge injection working; the risky commitment is that post-hoc-only will systematically fail across multiple charge states with RMSD ≥0.20 Å for ≥2 charges.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Train three variants on identical charged-defect trajectories: (1) no charge input, (2) charge only as additive global energy head after pooling, (3) charge injected into per-atom embeddings before message passing. Relax the same set of initial distortions for each q and compare relaxed minima RMSD vs DFT.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Variant (2) achieves RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å across all ≥5 charge states, OR variant (3) fails to achieve RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å while (2) succeeds.

new_predictions_likely: On Sb2Se3-like charged vacancy datasets, replacing separate-per-charge models with one joint model that includes a charge conditioning input will reduce average CTL MAE by ≥0.10 eV relative to a geometry-only joint model at matched parameter count.

If charge conditioning is injected pre-message-passing, the number of distinct relaxed minima found across charge states will increase by ≥2 (counted by SOAP clustering at r=5 Å) compared to a geometry-only model, because charge-dependent basins become separable.
new_predictions_unknown: A single scalar charge density input (Q_sys-style) will fail the CTL MAE ≤0.05 eV criterion on the same dataset where a categorical embedding passes; if it passes, the theory’s claim about representational separation (scalar vs embedding) is weakened.
A very-long-range coordinate transformer (no explicit charge input) will still fail CTL MAE ≤0.05 eV across ≥5 charges; if it succeeds, the identifiability premise is falsified.
negative_experiments: Fork test (decisive): train geometry-only joint-charge model vs charge-conditioned joint-charge model on the same dataset; if geometry-only achieves CTL MAE ≤0.05 eV, this theory is refuted.
Fork test (architectural): charge-only-posthoc head vs charge-injected-pre-message-passing; if posthoc-only reaches RMSD ≤0.10 Å across all charges, this theory is refuted.

unaccounted_for.text: A charge-aware Behler–Parrinello NNP using only a global scalar Q_sys achieved DFT-like κ and phonon properties for charged vacancies in AlN, suggesting that in some single-host regimes a scalar may suffice, contrary to the implied need for richer embeddings in all cases.

special_cases: Single-host, single-defect-type, narrow configuration space can allow weaker charge conditioning (e.g., a scalar) to be sufficient for forces/phonons.

If training data include separate charge-specific geometries only (no shared-geometry collisions), geometry-only models may partially succeed by memorizing geometry-charge correlations, reducing the identifiability barrier.

existing_theory.what_already_exists: Charge-state conditioning/global charge nodes for NNPs; separate-per-charge models; charged-defect phonon MLFFs with charge scalars.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: Numeric identifiability thresholds on CTL error for joint multi-charge learning and an architectural necessity claim about where charge must enter the network to recover charge-dependent minima.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Moves from 'charge helps' to a falsifiable bound and a specific architectural fork.

theory-2.name: Foundation-energy transfer works only through defect–pristine differencing; defect-only local MLIPs break under supercell scaling
theory-2.description: Phenomenon: MLIPs and energy models show strong systematic errors when used outside the training regime (larger supercells, different hosts), especially when trained only on defect-containing cells. Mechanism claim (inference): the dominant transfer error is a host-baseline energy misattribution (and corresponding force/curvature softening) that does not cancel unless the representation or evaluation explicitly subtracts a matched pristine reference or includes host data. Therefore, for data-scarce defect sets, the best representation strategy is not 'learn E_f directly from defective cell', but 'learn total energy robustly and compute formation energies by matched defect–pristine differences', or explicitly train on both pristine and defect configurations to avoid host bias.
theory-2.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.

components.theory_name: Foundation-energy transfer works only through defect–pristine differencing; defect-only local MLIPs break under supercell scaling
components.theory_description: Phenomenon: MLIPs and energy models show strong systematic errors when used outside the training regime (larger supercells, different hosts), especially when trained only on defect-containing cells. Mechanism claim (inference): the dominant transfer error is a host-baseline energy misattribution (and corresponding force/curvature softening) that does not cancel unless the representation or evaluation explicitly subtracts a matched pristine reference or includes host data. Therefore, for data-scarce defect sets, the best representation strategy is not 'learn E_f directly from defective cell', but 'learn total energy robustly and compute formation energies by matched defect–pristine differences', or explicitly train on both pristine and defect configurations to avoid host bias.

theory_statements.statement_name: Supercell scaling failure of defect-only local energy decomposition
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: defect-only local MLIPs break under supercell scaling while reference-difference energy models do not. If a local per-atom-decomposed MLIP is trained on ≤600 defect-containing configurations from a fixed small supercell and WITHOUT any pristine/host-only training structures, then when evaluated on pristine host supercells with ≥2× atom count, it will NOT achieve mean absolute host energy error ≤ 100 meV/atom; it will exceed 500 meV/atom. Conversely, an energy model used only via ΔE = E(defect) − E(pristine) will achieve host error ≤ 100 meV/atom under the same 2× scaling. NUMERIC THRESHOLDS: training size ≤600; scaling ≥2× atoms; host error bounds 100 and 500 meV/atom. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: adding angle features or equivariance to the defect-only MLIP will NOT reduce host error below 100 meV/atom without adding pristine data.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Neutral defects or charge-neutralized training sets; same chemistry; transfer to larger supercells than training; evaluated on pristine host total energies (not just formation energies).
special_cases: If the MLIP training set includes explicit pristine/bulk structures spanning volumes/temperatures, this law does not apply.
If only formation energies are evaluated and error cancellation is allowed, host error criterion is not directly tested.

supporting_evidence.text: Allegro-style local MLIP trained on a small defect-only dataset exhibited severe systematic host-energy bias when applied to host supercells (reported ≈1180 meV/atom host error), demonstrating the defect-only decomposition failure mode.

MLH (Hamiltonian-based) trained on 600 defect-related structures transferred to larger supercells and achieved defect formation-energy MAE 16–45 meV up to 383 atoms, consistent with the idea that representations that preserve a consistent host baseline (via electronic structure prediction) avoid catastrophic host bias under scaling.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: It is known that MLIPs need diverse training and that formation energies are computed by differences; host-bias issues have been observed qualitatively.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A numeric scaling law with explicit thresholds (≤600 training, ≥2× scaling, >500 meV/atom failure) tied to the presence/absence of pristine data and framed as a representation/label-construction requirement.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Directly grounded in the reported ≈1180 meV/atom host bias for defect-only MLIP; extends it into a falsifiable threshold statement for scaling.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Pick one chemistry (e.g., SiO2) and generate a defect-only training set of ≤600 structures from a fixed supercell size. Train (A) local MLIP (per-atom energy sum) and (B) a total-energy model evaluated only via ΔE between defect and pristine. Test both on pristine host supercells of 2× and 4× size. Measure mean absolute host energy error per atom vs DFT.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Model (A) achieves host error ≤ 100 meV/atom at ≥2× size without pristine training data, OR model (B) exhibits host error ≥ 500 meV/atom at ≥2× size.

theory_statements.statement_name: Pretrained bulk energy models transfer to defects only via differencing, not direct defect regression
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: with bulk-pretrained weights, formation-energy transfer is driven by energy differencing, not direct defect featurization. For vacancy formation energies in diverse chemistries using a bulk-pretrained energy-per-atom model applied to unrelaxed defective cells, computing E_f via E(defect) − E(perfect) + μ will NOT achieve MAE ≤ 0.7 eV unless a global bias correction is applied; with a single global shift (one scalar) the MAE WILL be ≤ 1.0 eV but will NOT be ≤ 0.7 eV. NUMERIC THRESHOLDS: 0.7 eV and 1.0 eV MAE. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: fine-tuning on ≤50 defect labels will NOT push MAE below 0.7 eV if defect structures remain unrelaxed at inference.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Neutral single-atom vacancies; unrelaxed defective supercells at inference; bulk-pretrained energy model used without (or with minimal) defect fine-tuning; broad chemistry mix (elements, oxides, 2D).
special_cases: If defective structures are relaxed (DFT/MLIP), MAE thresholds can improve and this statement may fail.
If training includes defect structures, this is outside the 'bulk-pretrained only' scope.

supporting_evidence.text: Pretrained ALIGNN energy-per-atom model transferred from perfect bulk training to vacancy formation energies with overall MAE 1.51 eV, improved to 1.00 eV with a global scissor-shift, indicating a persistent systematic bias and that even with correction performance remains ~1 eV scale rather than sub-0.7 eV.

The same study used unrelaxed defective structures for ALIGNN inference while DFT vacancy energies were relaxed, providing a concrete failure mode (geometry mismatch) that supports the negative prediction that small fine-tuning will not cross a tight MAE threshold if inference geometries remain unrelaxed.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Using energy differences and global shifts is common; pretrained-to-defect transfer has been explored.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A falsifiable numeric ceiling (cannot reach ≤0.7 eV MAE under unrelaxed inference) and a claim that small defect fine-tuning cannot overcome inference-geometry mismatch.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Uses the provided MAE numbers (1.51 eV; 1.00 eV after shift) to set an explicit bound and a concrete failure regime.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Take the 508-vacancy benchmark. (i) Evaluate bulk-pretrained ALIGNN via differencing on unrelaxed defective cells with and without one global shift; (ii) fine-tune weights on 50 randomly selected defect labels but still using unrelaxed defect geometries at inference. Compare MAE to DFT relaxed vacancy energies.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: After fine-tuning on ≤50 defects, MAE ≤ 0.7 eV is achieved while still using unrelaxed defective geometries at inference.

new_predictions_likely: In defect-only local-MLIP training with ≤600 structures, adding just 50 pristine/bulk configurations to the training set will reduce pristine-host energy bias by ≥400 meV/atom on ≥2× larger supercells (measured on the same test set).

For bulk-pretrained vacancy models, relaxing the defective structure with any force-accurate potential before inference will reduce MAE by ≥0.3 eV relative to unrelaxed inference, even without changing the energy model.
new_predictions_unknown: If a modern equivariant local MLIP (same training regime: ≤600 defect-only) achieves host error ≤100 meV/atom on ≥2× supercells without pristine data, then the 'host-baseline misattribution' mechanism is incomplete.
If a bulk-pretrained energy model plus a single global shift reaches MAE ≤0.7 eV on unrelaxed defects, then the claimed ceiling is false.
negative_experiments: Fork test: defect-only MLIP vs defect–pristine differencing energy model under ≥2× supercell scaling; if defect-only MLIP host error ≤100 meV/atom, theory is refuted.
Fork test: bulk-pretrained ALIGNN differencing with one global shift; if MAE ≤0.7 eV on the 508 vacancy benchmark using unrelaxed geometries, theory is refuted.

unaccounted_for.text: MLH achieves extremely small formation-energy MAE (16–45 meV) with only 600 structures, but it is not a simple energy-differencing approach; it uses Hamiltonian prediction and electronic structure, which may represent a different mechanism than pristine-reference subtraction alone.

special_cases: If formation energies (not absolute host energies) are the only metric, error cancellation can mask host bias; this theory is specifically about host baseline transfer and scaling.
Strongly localized defects where the rest of the cell is near-identical to pristine may show better cancellation even for defect-only MLIPs.

existing_theory.what_already_exists: Formation energies by differencing; known need for diverse training; pretrained-to-defect transfer with global bias correction.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: Hard numeric supercell-scaling failure thresholds for defect-only local MLIPs and a numeric MAE ceiling for unrelaxed vacancy inference even after small fine-tuning.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Uses provided quantitative failures/successes to make risky generalization bounds.

theory-3.name: Δ-to-pristine defect encoding is the transfer bottleneck for cross-host energetics
theory-3.description: Phenomenon: ML models for defect/dopant energetics show poor out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer across host chemistries when they ingest the full defective supercell as an absolute object. Theory: the dominant source of OOD failure is that the model must implicitly learn and subtract a host-dependent baseline energy manifold (host size/chemistry/strain) before learning the comparatively small defect perturbation. Therefore, representations that explicitly encode the defect as a Δ (defect minus pristine, or defect-local subgraph paired with pristine-local subgraph) will outperform full-supercell absolute encodings on cross-host transfer and few-shot adaptation. Conversely, models trained on full defective supercells without explicit pristine reference will NOT transfer unless the new defect class/chemistry is substantially represented in training (as observed for impurities/alloys/complexes).
theory-3.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.

components.theory_description: Phenomenon: ML models for defect/dopant energetics show poor out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer across host chemistries when they ingest the full defective supercell as an absolute object. Theory: the dominant source of OOD failure is that the model must implicitly learn and subtract a host-dependent baseline energy manifold (host size/chemistry/strain) before learning the comparatively small defect perturbation. Therefore, representations that explicitly encode the defect as a Δ (defect minus pristine, or defect-local subgraph paired with pristine-local subgraph) will outperform full-supercell absolute encodings on cross-host transfer and few-shot adaptation. Conversely, models trained on full defective supercells without explicit pristine reference will NOT transfer unless the new defect class/chemistry is substantially represented in training (as observed for impurities/alloys/complexes).

theory_statements.statement_name: Δ-reference encoding flips OOD transfer from multi-eV failure to sub-eV at ≤100 labels
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: Explicit defect Δ-to-pristine encoding (paired pristine+defect graphs with a subtraction readout) dominates over absolute defective-supercell encoding for cross-host transfer. NUMERIC THRESHOLD: when fine-tuning on ≤100 labeled examples from a new defect category (impurities OR alloys OR complexes), Δ-encoding will achieve test RMSE ≤ 0.70 eV, while absolute full-supercell encoding will NOT go below 1.50 eV. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: absolute encoding will not reach RMSE ≤ 0.70 eV under the ≤100-label regime even with identical architecture depth and cutoffs.
theory_statements.domain_scope: DFT-labeled defect formation energies in semiconductors/insulators using periodic supercells; tasks include transfer from native defects to impurities/alloys/complexes across multiple hosts (e.g., ZB binaries and CdX-like families). Applies to models that ingest atomistic structures (GNNs) and are trained to predict formation energies directly.
special_cases: If the new task is still within the same defect distribution as training (e.g., native defects only across same host family), the advantage may shrink (outside the transfer claim).

If labels are defined as energy differences using a pretrained total-energy model for both pristine and defect (energy-difference pipeline), the representation already contains an implicit Δ and falls under the Δ-encoding side of the fork.

supporting_evidence.text: ALIGNN trained only on native defects transfers poorly: tested on impurities/alloys/complexes RMSEs 2.17/2.68/2.98 eV, indicating absolute defective-supercell encoding without explicit pristine reference does not generalize across defect categories/chemistries.

Adding 50% of the new dataset to training reduces those RMSEs to 0.36/0.70/0.18 eV, showing that representation+model can succeed once the baseline shifts are learned with substantial in-domain examples—consistent with missing explicit Δ baseline subtraction being the bottleneck.

Vacancy formation via energy-difference using a pretrained bulk energy-per-atom ALIGNN model (defect and pristine predicted separately) demonstrates transfer from pristine to vacancies without defect-specific training (MAE 1.51 eV, 1.00 eV after global shift), consistent with the benefit of explicitly computing a Δ energy rather than learning absolute defect energies from scratch.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Energy-difference (Δ) ideas exist in defect formation-energy definitions and in some ML pipelines that compute E_defect − E_host. Transfer learning from bulk to defects also exists.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A sharp, falsifiable quantitative claim tying Δ-encoding to a specific low-label (≤100) OOD transfer regime and a hard failure bound (>1.50 eV) for absolute encodings on impurity/alloy/complex transfer, motivated by the observed multi-eV OOD collapse of full-supercell models.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: This reframes the evidence (multi-eV OOD failures and big gains only after adding many new-category examples) as a baseline-subtraction identifiability problem and predicts a concrete sample-efficiency crossover under Δ-encoding.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Construct paired inputs for each defect: (i) absolute defective supercell graph; (ii) paired pristine supercell graph + defect supercell graph with a constrained subtraction readout (E_defect_pred − E_pristine_pred + μ). Train both with identical GNN backbones. Train on Dataset1 (native ZB defects) and fine-tune on exactly N=100 labeled examples from Dataset2 (impurities) or Dataset4 (complexes). Compare RMSE on held-out from that dataset.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: With N=100 fine-tune labels, the absolute-encoding model achieves RMSE ≤ 0.70 eV OR the Δ-encoding model fails to reach RMSE ≤ 0.70 eV (on the same test split and architecture capacity).

theory_statements.statement_name: Angle-rich encodings improve in-domain RMSE but do NOT fix category transfer
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: Adding explicit 3-body angle features (line-graph) primarily reduces in-domain error but does not rescue cross-category OOD transfer. NUMERIC THRESHOLD: on Dataset1 (native ZB defects), an angle-rich model (ALIGNN-like) will achieve RMSE ≤ 0.20 eV while a distance-only model (CGCNN-like) will NOT beat 0.30 eV; however, for transfer from native→impurities with zero impurity labels, angle-rich encoding will NOT achieve RMSE ≤ 1.50 eV (it will exceed 1.50 eV). NEGATIVE PREDICTION: angle-rich models will not reduce the native→impurity zero-shot error below 1.50 eV despite large in-domain gains.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Graph models trained from scratch on defect formation energies in multi-host zincblende semiconductors; evaluation includes (a) random split in-domain native defects and (b) zero-shot transfer to impurity dataset without impurity labels.
special_cases: If pretraining on a very large chemically diverse defect dataset is used, this statement does not apply (it assumes training from scratch on Dataset1-like data).
If the transfer task is within the same defect type distribution (native→native across similar hosts), OOD may be smaller.

supporting_evidence.text: In-domain Dataset1 q=0: ALIGNN RMSE 0.15 eV vs CGCNN 0.35 eV vs MEGNET 0.40 eV, consistent with angles improving in-domain accuracy strongly.
Zero-shot transfer of ALIGNN trained on Dataset1 to impurities yields RMSE 2.17 eV (>1.50 eV), showing angle-rich encoding does not solve defect-category transfer by itself.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Angle features can improve atomistic prediction accuracy; OOD transfer can fail without representative data.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A combined two-regime quantitative fork: large benefit in-domain (≤0.20 eV) but a hard negative bound on category transfer (>1.50 eV) even with angle-rich encodings, explicitly separating 'geometry expressivity' from 'baseline subtraction / chemistry coverage' as the transfer limiter.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Directly abstracts the ALIGNN vs CGCNN in-domain gap and the ALIGNN transfer collapse into a discriminative claim that angles are not the missing ingredient for category transfer.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Train (1) ALIGNN and (2) a CGCNN variant augmented with explicit angle features removed/added (or an ALIGNN ablation removing the line-graph) on Dataset1 only. Evaluate zero-shot on Dataset2 impurities. Compare to in-domain Dataset1 test RMSE.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Angle-rich model achieves impurity zero-shot RMSE ≤ 1.50 eV OR distance-only model reaches in-domain RMSE ≤ 0.20 eV under the same data and training protocol.

new_predictions_likely: With N=50 impurity labels (fine-tune) and Δ-encoding, impurity RMSE will be ≤1.0 eV; absolute encoding will remain ≥1.7 eV.
For alloy transfer (CdSe_xTe_1-x-like) with N=100 labels, Δ-encoding will reduce RMSE by ≥1.0 eV relative to absolute encoding (e.g., 1.8→0.8 eV).
new_predictions_unknown: Δ-encoding will reduce the need for intermediate-structure augmentation: removing intermediate structures will increase RMSE by ≤0.05 eV for Δ-encoding but by ≥0.15 eV for absolute encoding (in-domain Dataset1).
negative_experiments: Fork test: keep architecture fixed, switch only representation to paired pristine+defect Δ readout. If absolute encoding matches or beats Δ-encoding at N=100 (RMSE difference ≤0.1 eV), the theory is refuted.

unaccounted_for.text: Pretrained bulk-to-defect vacancy transfer still has large MAE (~1.0 eV after shift), indicating Δ alone is insufficient without relaxation/charge/chemistry-specific corrections; the theory does not fully explain residual bias magnitude.

conflicting_evidence.text: No direct evidence item reports a Δ-to-pristine graph encoding experiment on the ALIGNN datasets; the quantitative ≤100-label bound is an inference requiring new experiments.

special_cases: Metals and systems with delocalized electrons where local message passing is known to struggle may violate the claimed sample-efficiency even with Δ-encoding (outside scope of provided semiconductor-heavy evidence).

existing_theory.what_already_exists: Energy-difference formation-energy computation and transfer from bulk models to defect energies.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: A hard, low-label OOD transfer prediction for Δ-encoding versus absolute encoding, motivated by explicit multi-eV transfer collapse in full-supercell models.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Connects observed OOD failures to an identifiability/baseline-subtraction representation defect and commits to quantitative improvements under strict few-shot conditions.

theory-4.name: Charge-state generalization requires explicit charge conditioning; separate-per-q models will fail under geometric domain shift
theory-4.description: Phenomenon: charged defects create multiple PESs for identical nuclear coordinates; models that do not condition on charge conflate these PESs. Theory: for multi-charge-state tasks (including charged-defect phonon/IFC workflows), representing charge as an explicit conditioning variable (global charge scalar/embedding) is necessary and sufficient to avoid charge-PES collapse; training separate models per charge state is brittle when inputs are not fully relaxed or when charge-state datasets are imbalanced. The mechanism is that charge introduces a geometry-independent energy offset plus a geometry-dependent interaction modulation; a charge embedding should include both (as seen in the Sb2Se3 MACE scheme).
theory-4.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.

components.theory_name: Charge-state generalization requires explicit charge conditioning; separate-per-q models will fail under geometric domain shift
components.theory_description: Phenomenon: charged defects create multiple PESs for identical nuclear coordinates; models that do not condition on charge conflate these PESs. Theory: for multi-charge-state tasks (including charged-defect phonon/IFC workflows), representing charge as an explicit conditioning variable (global charge scalar/embedding) is necessary and sufficient to avoid charge-PES collapse; training separate models per charge state is brittle when inputs are not fully relaxed or when charge-state datasets are imbalanced. The mechanism is that charge introduces a geometry-independent energy offset plus a geometry-dependent interaction modulation; a charge embedding should include both (as seen in the Sb2Se3 MACE scheme).

theory_statements.statement_name: Without charge conditioning, a joint-charge MLFF will NOT separate charge-specific minima below 0.10 Å RMSD
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: A single joint MLFF conditioned on global defect charge (categorical embedding) dominates over a charge-agnostic joint MLFF trained on pooled multi-charge data. NUMERIC THRESHOLD: for a fixed defect and five charge states, charge-conditioned MLFF will yield ground-state RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å for each charge state, while charge-agnostic pooled MLFF will NOT achieve RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å for at least 3 of 5 charge states. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: the charge-agnostic pooled model will fail the ≤0.10 Å criterion (i.e., produce RMSD >0.10 Å) on most charge states even with the same backbone and training set size.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Charged vacancy (or charged point defect) PES learning in semiconductors/ionic semiconductors using equivariant MLFFs trained on DFT relaxations/trajectories spanning multiple integer charge states; evaluation is on relaxed minima geometries per charge state.
special_cases: If the defect has negligible charge-dependent reconstruction (all charge states share the same minimum), then charge-agnostic pooling may pass RMSD thresholds (outside intended charged-reconstruction regime).
If separate per-charge models are trained and tested only on near-optimized geometries of that same charge, this statement does not apply (it concerns pooled joint training without charge input).

supporting_evidence.text: In Sb2Se3, adding a global charge embedding to MACE yields ground-state RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å across charge states and predicts transition levels within 0.015 eV; an ablation without charge embedding fails to separate charge-state latent clusters and fails to identify correct ground states.

Foundation bulk-trained MLIPs lacking charge conditioning fail on charged-defect PESs with RMSD typically 0.2–0.4 Å, supporting that charge-agnostic representations collapse charge-dependent landscapes.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Training separate models per charge state and including charge as a feature have been discussed; charge-aware NNPs with global charge nodes exist.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A concrete falsifiable geometric success criterion (RMSD thresholds) and the claim that pooled multi-charge training without charge input fails for most charge states, tied to a numeric count (≥3 of 5 charge states) and grounded in the Sb2Se3 ablation evidence.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Uses direct evidence where charge embedding is necessary for correct minima; converts it into a general, high-information prediction with explicit failure counts and thresholds.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Using the same Sb2Se3-style dataset (or an analogous multi-charge dataset in a second material), train two MACE models: (A) pooled multi-charge without charge input; (B) pooled multi-charge with categorical charge embedding + geometry-independent embedding readout. Relax the same set of distorted initial configurations per charge and compare RMSD to DFT minima per charge.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Charge-agnostic pooled model achieves RMSD ≤ 0.10 Å for all 5 charge states OR charge-conditioned model fails to achieve RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å for at least 4 of 5 charge states.

theory_statements.statement_name: Separate-per-q formation-energy GNNs will NOT be robust on unoptimized inputs unless ≥30% intermediate structures are included
theory_statements.theory_statement: FORK: Intermediate-structure (IS) augmentation dominates over training only on optimized structures for robustness to unoptimized defect geometries. NUMERIC THRESHOLD: for charge-specific supercell-graph models trained separately per q, if IS constitute < 30% of training structures, the model will NOT reduce CTL RMSE below 0.25 eV when evaluated on pristine/unoptimized defect inputs; with IS ≥ 30%, CTL RMSE will be ≤ 0.20 eV after surrogate optimization. NEGATIVE PREDICTION: without sufficient IS fraction (<30%), the CTL RMSE floor stays ≥0.25 eV even if the model attains formation-energy RMSE ≤0.30 eV on optimized geometries.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Defect formation-energy GNNs (ALIGNN-like) predicting charge-specific formation energies used to construct CTLs; evaluation includes starting from unoptimized defect structures and (optionally) applying model-driven iterative optimization; zincblende semiconductor-like datasets with intermediate relaxation snapshots available.
special_cases: If evaluation is only on DFT-optimized structures (no unoptimized/pristine inputs), IS augmentation fraction is irrelevant (outside this statement).
If an MLFF providing forces is used to relax structures (not energy-only iterative distortions), results may differ.

supporting_evidence.text: ALIGNN study reports that including intermediate (partially optimized) structures improves robustness and that charged models trained mostly on optimized geometries are less reliable on pristine/unoptimized charged structures.

ALIGNN-based iterative optimization reduced CTL RMSE from 0.37 eV (unoptimized) to 0.17 eV (optimized), indicating that robustness to unoptimized inputs is a key limiting factor and can be improved by learning relaxation pathways (which IS augmentation targets).

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Training on intermediate structures and using ML surrogates for relaxation have been demonstrated; per-charge models are common.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A quantitative IS fraction threshold (30%) tied to CTL RMSE limits on unoptimized inputs, providing a crisp falsifier for when IS augmentation becomes necessary rather than just helpful.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Converts qualitative claims about IS usefulness and quantified CTL improvements after optimization into a risky, testable bound on dataset composition.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Rebuild Dataset1 with controlled IS fractions f∈{0%,10%,30%,50%} while keeping total sample count fixed (subsample). Train per-charge ALIGNN models and evaluate CTLs from pristine/unoptimized inputs after fixed-budget ALIGNN-optimization. Plot CTL RMSE vs f.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: With IS fraction <30%, CTL RMSE falls below 0.25 eV OR with IS fraction ≥30%, CTL RMSE remains above 0.20 eV under the same optimization budget.

new_predictions_likely: In a multi-charge MLFF, adding a geometry-independent charge-embedding readout term will reduce energy RMSE by ≥20% relative to charge-conditioning only in node initialization (same dataset), because it captures pure charge offsets.
For charge-conditioned MLFFs trained on five charge states, removing the charge embedding will increase minimum-geometry RMSD by ≥0.15 Å on average (e.g., 0.05→0.20 Å).
new_predictions_unknown: A continuous charge descriptor (q/V as scalar) will outperform categorical charge embedding when extrapolating to unseen supercell sizes by ≥0.05 Å RMSD, despite categorical embeddings winning in fixed-size training.
negative_experiments: Fork test: pooled training with and without charge embedding. If charge-agnostic pooling reaches RMSD ≤0.10 Å for all charge states, the theory is refuted.

unaccounted_for.text: Charge-aware Behler–Parrinello NNP uses a global charge scalar Q_sys but notes it does not explicitly contribute to forces; yet it reproduces many vibrational/thermal metrics in AlN. This theory does not explain when a charge input that does not affect forces is still sufficient.

conflicting_evidence.text: No evidence item provides a quantitative IS fraction sweep; the 30% threshold is an inference that must be experimentally validated.

special_cases: For defects whose charge dependence is weak (same geometry across q), explicit charge conditioning may not improve geometric predictions (outside scope).
For metals where the concept of discrete localized charged defects is ill-posed, charge conditioning may not correspond to physically meaningful PES separation (outside scope).

existing_theory.what_already_exists: Charge nodes/conditioning for NNPs and charge-aware potentials.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: The explicit geometric failure criterion for pooled training without charge conditioning and the claim that most charge states fail simultaneously; plus a dataset-composition threshold for IS augmentation tied to CTL accuracy on unoptimized inputs.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Grounds the need for charge conditioning in an explicit charged-defect PES ablation result and extends it with falsifiable numeric bounds.

theory-5.name: Defect-reference subtraction is the main lever for cross-host transfer (not bigger models)
theory-5.description: Cross-host transfer fails primarily because full-supercell pooling forces the network to learn absolute host energy baselines and band-alignment offsets that vary strongly with chemistry; this drowns the defect signal. Representations that explicitly reference the pristine host (E_defect − E_pristine or explicit Δ-features) compress the learning problem to a localized perturbation, yielding large gains in transfer and data efficiency. The fork is that (A) transfer is limited by missing physics/long-range interactions versus (B) transfer is limited by an avoidable target/representation mismatch (absolute-vs-delta). This theory commits to (B): defect-reference subtraction dominates.
theory-5.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.

components.theory_name: Defect-reference subtraction is the main lever for cross-host transfer (not bigger models)
components.theory_description: Cross-host transfer fails primarily because full-supercell pooling forces the network to learn absolute host energy baselines and band-alignment offsets that vary strongly with chemistry; this drowns the defect signal. Representations that explicitly reference the pristine host (E_defect − E_pristine or explicit Δ-features) compress the learning problem to a localized perturbation, yielding large gains in transfer and data efficiency. The fork is that (A) transfer is limited by missing physics/long-range interactions versus (B) transfer is limited by an avoidable target/representation mismatch (absolute-vs-delta). This theory commits to (B): defect-reference subtraction dominates.

theory_statements.statement_name: Delta-energy representation crosses the 1.0 eV OOD barrier with ≤10% target-host labels
theory_statements.theory_statement: Fork: (delta-to-pristine energy target + shared weights across defect and pristine) beats (absolute defective-supercell formation energy regression) for OOD host transfer. If a model is trained on Dataset 1 (native defects) and adapted to Dataset 2 (impurities) with only 10% of Dataset 2 labeled points, then a delta-to-pristine training target (predict E_defect and E_pristine and subtract, or predict ΔE directly) will achieve impurity formation-energy RMSE ≤ 0.60 eV, while an otherwise-matched absolute-E^f model will NOT reach RMSE < 1.00 eV. Negative prediction: the absolute-E^f model will not cross 1.00 eV RMSE at 10% labels.
theory_statements.domain_scope: PBE-level defect formation energies across zincblende semiconductors in the ALIGNN dataset setting; OOD transfer from native defects (Dataset 1) to impurities (Dataset 2) with small labeled adaptation set; fixed relaxed-geometry protocol consistent with original datasets.
special_cases: If the adaptation set contains ≥50% of Dataset 2 (as in the reported experiment), both approaches may reach <0.6 eV and the gap can shrink.
If labels are computed on unrelaxed defective geometries while training uses relaxed geometries (or vice versa), both approaches can fail due to label/structure mismatch.

supporting_evidence.text: ALIGNN trained on native defects (Dataset 1) fails catastrophically on impurities (Dataset 2) with RMSE 2.17 eV, implying that naive absolute-supercell regression does not transfer across defect chemistry without in-domain labels.

A pretrained bulk-energy ALIGNN can be applied to both pristine and vacancy supercells and then differenced to obtain vacancy formation energies (E_defect − E_perfect + μ), demonstrating the feasibility and partial transferability of an explicit pristine reference subtraction pipeline.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Energy-difference constructions for formation energies and the general idea of learning deltas exist; pretrained bulk energy models have been differenced for vacancies.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A specific, risky cross-host few-shot bound tying transfer success to delta-to-pristine targets with explicit numeric thresholds (10% labels, ≤0.60 eV vs not <1.00 eV).
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Anchored to observed OOD failure without in-domain data (2.17 eV) and to demonstrated viability of pristine/defect energy differencing; makes a discriminating few-shot transfer prediction not present in evidence.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Train two models with identical architecture capacity: (A) absolute model regressing E^f from defective supercell; (B) delta model regressing ΔE = E_defect(supercell) − E_pristine(supercell) (or predicting both energies with shared trunk and subtracting). Pretrain on Dataset 1. Fine-tune each on a stratified 10% subset of Dataset 2. Evaluate RMSE on remaining 90% of Dataset 2.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: The absolute-E^f model achieves RMSE < 1.00 eV on Dataset 2 after 10% fine-tuning, OR the delta model fails to achieve RMSE ≤ 0.60 eV under the same protocol.

theory_statements.statement_name: Defect-only local MLIPs exhibit supercell-size energy drift above 50 meV/atom unless trained with explicit host references
theory_statements.theory_statement: Fork: (training includes pristine/host configurations or explicit host-reference subtraction) prevents supercell-size drift, versus (defect-only training) causes systematic host-energy bias. For atom-centered local MLIPs trained only on defect supercells of size ≤100 atoms, the mean absolute host energy error on pristine host supercells of size ≥200 atoms will NOT fall below 50 meV/atom; adding ≥100 pristine-host configurations to training will reduce that host energy error to ≤5 meV/atom. Negative prediction: defect-only training cannot reach <50 meV/atom host error at larger size.
theory_statements.domain_scope: Atom-centered local MLIPs (equivariant or symmetry-function based) trained on small defect supercells and evaluated on pristine host supercells of larger size; relevant to workflows that compute formation energies via total-energy differences.
special_cases: If the potential is a Hamiltonian-learning model (MLH) rather than a local energy decomposition MLIP, the statement may not apply because the error structure differs.
If long-range electrostatics dominates (highly ionic materials) and the MLIP includes explicit LR Coulomb terms, the drift threshold may change.

supporting_evidence.text: Allegro-style local MLIP trained on defect-only small-supercell data shows large systematic host-energy bias when applied to host supercells and larger supercells (reported ≈1180 meV/atom host error), consistent with strong size-transfer failure without host reference coverage.

MACE defect free-energy study explicitly warns that defect-only training can yield systematic errors when applied to larger supercells than those used for training, recommending inclusion of bulk/host data for reliable absolute energies.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: It is known that MLIPs can fail OOD and that including bulk/host data improves stability; some papers caution against defect-only training for size transfer.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A numeric bound (50 meV/atom failure threshold; ≤5 meV/atom after adding ≥100 host structures) posed as a falsifiable law-like prediction for defect-only training regimes.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Directly grounded in observed huge host bias and in documented methodological warning; the specific numeric thresholds are a risky commitment intended to be easily refuted by counterexamples.

theory_statements.discriminating_experiment: Train an atom-centered MLIP on (i) defect-only dataset (≤100-atom defect supercells), and (ii) the same dataset plus 100 pristine-host configurations spanning volumes/temperatures. Evaluate energy-per-atom MAE on pristine host supercells of size 200–600 atoms excluded from training; report mean absolute host error.
theory_statements.falsifies_if: Defect-only training yields pristine-host energy error <50 meV/atom for ≥200-atom supercells, OR adding 100 host structures fails to reduce error to ≤5 meV/atom.

new_predictions_likely: Delta-to-pristine fine-tuning with 10% impurity labels reaches ≤0.60 eV RMSE on Dataset 2, while absolute-E^f remains ≥1.00 eV under identical budgets.
Defect-only local MLIP training will show a clear size-dependent drift; at 200+ atoms, host error will exceed 50 meV/atom unless pristine host frames are added.
new_predictions_unknown: If delta-to-pristine features are added but the model is still trained to output absolute E^f (not ΔE), the improvement will vanish and RMSE will stay >1.0 eV even after 10% fine-tuning—distinguishing whether the gain is target-design vs input-featurization.

A foundation MLIP with replay fine-tuning (multi-head replay) may beat delta-to-pristine direct regression in the same 10% regime; if so, the bottleneck is not representation mismatch but pretrained PES priors.
negative_experiments: Fork test: with 10% impurity labels, if absolute-E^f matches or beats delta-to-pristine (absolute RMSE < 1.0 eV and delta RMSE > 0.6 eV), the theory fails.
Fork test: if a defect-only MLIP shows <50 meV/atom host error on large pristine supercells, the claimed necessity of explicit host referencing is refuted.

unaccounted_for.text: ALIGNN’s in-distribution superiority over CGCNN/MEGNET on Dataset 1 could be due to angle features rather than any host-referencing issue; this theory does not explain that gap, only transfer behavior.

conflicting_evidence.text: Pretrained bulk-energy ALIGNN differencing for vacancies still has large MAE (1.51 eV → 1.00 eV with shift), suggesting that pristine-reference subtraction alone does not guarantee high accuracy without defect-specific information, which could contradict strong claims of delta dominance if generalized too broadly.

special_cases: Charged defects: pristine-reference subtraction must be paired with consistent electrostatic corrections/alignment (e.g., FNV) or charge-conditioning; otherwise ΔE may be ill-defined across supercells.
Defects with migration/split reconstructions: delta-to-pristine on an unrelaxed geometry may misrepresent the final state unless relaxation/trajectory sampling is included.

existing_theory.what_already_exists: Energy difference formulas for formation energies; inclusion of bulk/host data to stabilize MLIPs; defect transfer failures with naive training.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: Explicit quantitative few-shot transfer thresholds that attribute the dominant transfer bottleneck to missing pristine-referenced targets, not model expressivity.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Builds from evidence of OOD failure and host-energy bias; turns these into sharp, refutable numeric commitments about delta-targeting.

theory-6.name: Charge-state physics is best represented by explicit charge conditioning; separate-per-q models will fail for phonon/κ tasks above a data threshold
theory-6.description: For charged defects, the PES and especially force constants change with charge state even at identical coordinates; this non-uniqueness cannot be resolved by structure-only descriptors. The high-information fork is: (A) training separate models per charge state is sufficient, versus (B) explicit charge conditioning (global charge embedding or global charge scalar) is necessary to share data across q and to get accurate phonon/thermal transport quantities. This theory commits to (B) and further claims that the benefit appears at a concrete data threshold because phonon/IFC targets require consistent cross-q derivatives.
theory-6.theory_query: Build theories about which representation and featurization strategies for point defects and dopants in crystalline materials (e.g., defect-centered graph encodings, local-environment descriptors, sparse defect representations, charge-aware embeddings, learned embeddings from foundation interatomic potentials) most improve machine learning prediction of defect-influenced material properties, and why. For additional context: we are especially interested in transferability across host materials and chemistries, data efficiency given scarce defect datasets, handling of charged defects and defect complexes, and downstream prediction of phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity degradation caused by defects, motivated by thermal management applications, based on the following results.
