metadata.title: Machine learning Hamiltonian enables scalable and accurate defect calculations: the case of oxygen vacancies in amorphous SiO2

tldr.text: The proposed MLH model enables efficient structural relaxations for host (defect-free) and defect systems in larger supercells, avoiding the systematic energy errors observed in MLIPs and holds significant potential for defect simulations in complex materials.

metadata.abstract: Point defects critically influence the properties of materials and devices, yet density functional theory (DFT) remains computationally demanding for defect supercell calculations. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer high efficiency but require extensive datasets. MLIPs trained only on defect configurations in small supercells exhibit systematic energy errors in larger supercells, demonstrating limited transferability. Here, we present a machine learning Hamiltonian (MLH) model-based method for calculating total energies and atomic forces in defect supercells with linear-scaling computational cost, enabling efficient structural relaxation and accurate formation energy predictions. We take oxygen vacancies in amorphous SiO$_2$ as an example and train the MLH model on defect configurations in 95-atom supercells, with the training data derived from 120 self-consistent field calculations and 12 structural relaxations. The MLH model enables efficient structural relaxations for host (defect-free) and defect systems in larger supercells, avoiding the systematic energy errors observed in MLIPs. The cancellation of energy errors between host and defect systems yields accurate formation energy predictions, with deviations from DFT below 50 meV. The proposed method holds significant potential for defect simulations in complex materials.

content.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonian (MLH) model for total energies and forces

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | MLH (this work) |
| name_full | Machine Learning Hamiltonian (MLH) model for total energies and forces |
| brief_description | An MLH-based workflow that predicts real-space Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian matrix elements with an equivariant GNN (HamGNN) and then derives wavefunctions, charge density, total energy and atomic forces, enabling linear-scaling defect relaxations and accurate formation energies from a small DFT dataset. |
| citation_title | here |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Amorphous SiO2 (a-SiO2) only in this study (multiple amorphous host cells were generated); single host chemistry tested (Si,O). |
| defect_types | Neutral oxygen vacancy (V_O) point defects only; no substitutional dopants, interstitials, antisites, Frenkel pairs or defect complexes considered. |
| charge_state_handling | Neutral-only; paper explicitly focuses on neutral defects and neutral defect formation energies (no explicit charged-defect labels, Fermi-level or background-charge corrections included). |
| target_properties | Predicted: Hamiltonian matrix elements, band structure, real-space wavefunctions and charge density, total energies, atomic forces, structural relaxation trajectories, and neutral defect formation energies. |
| representation_strategy_name | Real-space Hamiltonian prediction via an equivariant graph neural network (MLH/HamGNN) |
| representation_strategy_description | An E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (HamGNN) maps atomic positions and species to real-space Hamiltonian matrix blocks (decomposed into on-site and off-site parts). The network uses node (atomic/orbital) and edge (pair) features, with distance expanded in Bessel basis and relative directions embedded via spherical harmonics to produce orbital-resolved Hamiltonian matrix elements for the full supercell (periodicity handled through real-space to k-space Fourier transforms). |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full-supercell Hamiltonian prediction (not a small defect-centered delta representation). The model is trained on defect-containing 95-atom supercells and applied to larger supercells without relying on an explicit pristine reference subtraction; formation energies benefit from cancellation of host/defect total-energy errors. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Interatomic distances expanded with Bessel basis (N_b = 64); cutoff radius r_c = 26 Bohr (~13.8 Å); relative directions embedded with spherical harmonics up to l_max = 4; equivariant feature channels specified across parity and angular orders (detailed channel counts reported); species (Si, O) are included via node features in the graph (no explicit one-hot specification given, but species are encoded in node features). |
| graph_model_architecture | HamGNN: a transferable E(3)-equivariant graph neural network with 3 orbital-convolution layers, equivariant message-passing, and a pair-interaction layer; node features updated via orbital convolution; edge features formed by integrating atom-pair features. Detailed irreducible-representation channel counts and parity (even/odd) are reported. |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | No pretraining used for the MLH in this work; HamGNN is trained from scratch on the reported small DFT dataset (no transfer from foundation potentials or pretrained interatomic potentials). |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Training dataset: 120 SCF calculations (unrelaxed V_O structures) + 480 configurations sampled along 12 relaxation trajectories = 600 structures total (all from DFT on 95-atom supercells). Dataset split random 8:1:1 (train/val/test) for MLH. Relatively small/low-shot dataset compared with typical MLIPs. |
| transferability_evidence | Strong in-domain and out-of-training-size transfer demonstrated: MLH trained only on 95-atom defect supercells successfully predicts Hamiltonians, charge densities, energies and forces for hosts and V_O defects in larger supercells (tested 95, 215, 383 and host supercells up to 576 atoms). Quantitative results: Hamiltonian MAE on held-out test set 0.26 meV (matrix elements); for unseen 95-atom defect MAE 0.72 meV; charge-density MAE 3e-4 e/Å^3. Energy per-atom errors remain low (majority < ~1.2 meV/atom) and formation energy MAEs: 16 meV (95-atom), 26 meV (215-atom), 45 meV (383-atom), showing error cancellation and transfer to larger supercells. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Explicit claim and demonstration of small-data efficiency: model trained on only 120 SCF + 12 relaxations (600 structures) yet achieves DFT-comparable formation energies (<50 meV) and accurate forces; contrasted with other MLIP studies requiring thousands of DFT points (cited examples). No formal learning curves are provided, but the numerical outcomes show high sample efficiency. |
| evaluation_protocol | Dataset randomly split 8:1:1 for MLH (train/val/test). In relaxation-transfer tests, configurations encountered during a given relaxation trajectory were excluded from the training set to avoid leakage. For MLIP baseline, a 9:1 train/validation split was used. Additional out-of-training-size tests used unseen larger supercells. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Main baseline: an Allegro-style MLIP trained on the same dataset; direct comparison to DFT. Ablation-style evidence: comparison emphasizes that MLIP trained only on defect supercells shows systematic host energy errors and potential-energy-surface softening, while MLH avoids these systematic errors. No explicit internal ablation (e.g., varying HamGNN cutoffs or equivariance) is reported. |
| performance_metrics | Hamiltonian MAE (matrix elements): test 0.26 meV; unseen 95-atom defect: 0.72 meV. Charge-density MAE: 3×10^-4 e/Å^3. Total-energy errors: example MLH total energy 94 meV higher than DFT (≈1 meV/atom for a 95-atom cell); MLH per-atom energy errors reported ≈0.85 meV/atom (95-atom case), 0.41 meV/atom (215-atom), 1.1 meV/atom (383-atom). Atomic-force MAE: ~27 meV/Å for an example defect; typical force MAEs ≈25 meV/Å across many cases. MLIP baseline errors (for same tests): much larger — total energy error 990 meV and forces 115 meV/Å in one example; systematic host error ~1180 meV/atom in some host tests. Formation-energy MAEs (defect formation energy): 16 meV (95-atom), 26 meV (215-atom), 45 meV (383-atom). Band energies deviations ~0.01 eV. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | None in this work: the paper does not predict phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity degradation. It only notes in related-work citations that MLIPs have been used elsewhere to compute phonon spectra, Grüneisen parameters and related vibrational properties (e.g., Shimizu et al.). No coupling of MLH outputs to phonon/BTE calculations is presented. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Authors attribute MLH success to directly learning the electronic Hamiltonian (thus enabling charge density and wavefunction recovery) and to the equivariant graph representation that captures orbital and spatial symmetries; these features allow accurate host and defect energies even when trained on a small defect-only dataset. They also point to error cancellation between host and defect total-energy errors as the reason formation energies are much more accurate than absolute total-energy errors. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Reported limitations: MLH total energies are slightly elevated relative to DFT due to residual Hamiltonian errors and structural differences; the study focuses only on neutral defects (no charged defects or defect complexes); the MLH still exhibits increasing per-atom energy error at the largest supercell sizes (formation-energy errors grow with supercell size though remain <50 meV up to 383 atoms). No handling of long-range electrostatics for charged systems is presented. |
| recommended_best_practices | Train models that describe both host and defect systems (or use representations that recover electronic structure) to avoid systematic host-energy bias seen in MLIPs; use Hamiltonian-predicting equivariant models (MLH/HamGNN) to recover wavefunctions/charge density and derive energies/forces; exclude relaxation-trajectory configurations from training when evaluating transferability; small but carefully sampled DFT sets (including SCF samples and relaxation trajectories) can suffice for MLH training. |

content.title: HamGNN (Transferable E(3) equivariant graph neural network for Hamiltonian prediction)

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | HamGNN |
| name_full | HamGNN (Transferable E(3) equivariant graph neural network for Hamiltonian prediction) |
| brief_description | An E(3)-equivariant graph neural network architecture used here to predict real-space Hamiltonian matrix elements by decomposing them into on-site and off-site parts and performing orbital-aware equivariant message passing. |
| citation_title | Transferable equivariant graph neural networks for the Hamiltonian of molecules and solids |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Used here on amorphous SiO2; HamGNN was developed for molecules and solids generally (ref. paper). |
| defect_types | Applied to neutral oxygen vacancies in a-SiO2 in this work; HamGNN itself targets general Hamiltonian prediction (molecules/solids). |
| charge_state_handling | No explicit scheme for charged defects in this implementation; used for neutral systems here. |
| target_properties | Hamiltonian matrix elements, band structures, wavefunctions, charge densities, derived total energies and forces. |
| representation_strategy_name | Equivariant graph representation with orbital-resolved node features and pairwise edge features |
| representation_strategy_description | Nodes represent atoms/orbitals; edges encode pair interactions within cutoff; distances expanded in Bessel basis (N_b=64) and orientations in spherical harmonics (l_max=4) producing equivariant message passing that outputs on-site and off-site Hamiltonian blocks. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full-supercell graph (not defect-centered delta features); uses periodic image information when reconstructing k-space Hamiltonian. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Cutoff r_c = 26 Bohr; Bessel radial basis (N_b=64); spherical harmonics to l_max=4; equivariant irreducible representation channels with explicit parity and angular-order channel counts (detailed in Methods). |
| graph_model_architecture | Equivariant orbital-convolution layers (3 layers reported), pair interaction layer, equivariant message passing; orbitally resolved outputs (on-site/off-site decomposition). |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | No pretraining; trained from scratch on DFT Hamiltonian data in this work. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Trained on 600 DFT configurations derived from 95-atom supercells (120 SCF + 480 relaxation-sampled). |
| transferability_evidence | HamGNN (as used here) transfers to larger supercells and unseen amorphous configurations; Hamiltonian MAE on test 0.26 meV and unseen defect 0.72 meV; charge-density and energy/force predictions validate transfer. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | High efficiency shown: accurate Hamiltonian and derived properties from ~600 training structures. |
| evaluation_protocol | Random 8:1:1 split; held-out larger-supercell tests excluded training-relaxation configurations. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Compared directly to a local MLIP (Allegro) baseline trained on same data; HamGNN + MLH outperforms MLIP notably for host-energy bias and force accuracy. |
| performance_metrics | Hamiltonian MAE 0.26 meV (test), 0.72 meV (unseen 95-atom); charge-density MAE 3e-4 e/Å^3; energy/force errors reported in MLH entry. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | None in this implementation; HamGNN enables wavefunction/charge density outputs that in principle could be used for further vibrational/phonon coupling but not demonstrated. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Equivariance + orbital-aware features allow direct learning of electronic Hamiltonian, enabling recovery of electronic structure and better generalization to different supercell sizes. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | No charged-defect handling demonstrated; residual Hamiltonian errors can lead to slight systematic elevation of total energies; needs DFT Hamiltonian/SCF data for training. |
| recommended_best_practices | Use orbital-resolved equivariant GNNs with sufficiently large radial cutoff and angular resolution for Hamiltonian prediction; include relaxation-trajectory samples to cover configuration space. |

content.title: Allegro-style equivariant local interatomic potential (MLIP) baseline

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | Allegro MLIP (baseline) |
| name_full | Allegro-style equivariant local interatomic potential (MLIP) baseline |
| brief_description | A local equivariant interatomic potential (Allegro implementation) trained on the same small dataset as MLH and used as a baseline; it uses local atomic environment descriptors and predicts per-atom energies and forces. |
| citation_title |  |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Applied on amorphous SiO2 hosts and V_O defect supercells in this study as a baseline. |
| defect_types | Neutral oxygen vacancies (same as MLH tests); local potential learns defect configurations within cutoff. |
| charge_state_handling | None (neutral systems only). |
| target_properties | Per-atom energies and atomic forces (used for structural relaxations and energy comparisons). |
| representation_strategy_name | Local atom-centered equivariant descriptors with finite cutoff (Allegro-style) |
| representation_strategy_description | Local environment representation with cutoff 6 Å, equivariant tensor product layers (3 layers), l_max = 2; per-atom energy decomposition and force derivation via gradients. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Atom-centered local descriptor (full supercell energy obtained by summing local contributions); relies on local environments within 6 Å (no explicit pristine-reference subtraction). |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Cutoff radius = 6 Å; 3 tensor product layers; maximum angular quantum number l_max = 2; species included implicitly via node features as standard in Allegro-style models. |
| graph_model_architecture | Allegro-style equivariant local model with 3 tensor product layers; trained to predict per-atom energies and forces (details in Methods). |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | Trained from scratch on the small dataset in this work; no foundation-model pretraining used for this baseline. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Same small dataset as MLH (600 structures from 95-atom defect supercells); train/validation split 9:1 for Allegro baseline. |
| transferability_evidence | Poor transferability observed: Allegro trained on defect-only small-supercell data exhibits large systematic host-energy bias when applied to host supercells and to larger supercells (examples: systematic overestimation ≈1180 meV/atom in host tests; large total-energy and force errors for defect relaxations). |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Despite being trained on same small dataset, Allegro/MLIP shows poor performance; highlights that local MLIPs can require much larger datasets for reliable host/defect transfer. |
| evaluation_protocol | Random 9:1 train/validation split; tested on unseen relaxations and larger supercells where training relax configs were excluded. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Used as the principal baseline versus MLH; shows systematic energy errors and potential-energy-surface softening not present in MLH predictions. |
| performance_metrics | Example errors: total-energy error 990 meV and force MAE 115 meV/Å for an example defect; systematic host error ~1180 meV/atom in host relaxations; ΔQ structural deviations up to ~18 amu^{1/2}Å for MLIP-relaxed structures vs <2 amu^{1/2}Å for MLH in many cases. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | None in this work; Allegro baseline was not used to compute phonon-related properties here. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Local decomposition and training only on defect supercells caused inaccurate estimation of host-atom contributions and PES softening, leading to systematic errors; suggests MLIPs need host data or much larger datasets to avoid bias. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Large systematic host-energy bias when trained only on defect-containing small supercells; potential-energy-surface softening and poor structural-relaxation fidelity; not suitable here for accurate formation energies unless training sets expanded to include host configurations or much larger amounts of data. |
| recommended_best_practices | Include both host and defect supercells in MLIP training or greatly expand dataset diversity; validate MLIP host-energy bias before using summed-per-atom energies for formation energies. |

metadata.title: Multi-fidelity Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Charged Point Defects

tldr.text: This work finds that the current generation of foundation MLIPs do not describe the defect physics of the semiconductor Sb2Se3, and introduces global defect charge embeddings that distinguish the bonding characteristics of different charge states.

metadata.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can now reproduce the energy, forces and stresses of bulk materials with high accuracy compared to first-principles calculations. The description of imperfections, where coordination environments and electron counts deviate from those found in pristine reference structures, remains a challenge. We find that the current generation of foundation MLIPs do not describe the defect physics of the semiconductor Sb2Se3. We introduce global defect charge embeddings that distinguish the bonding characteristics of different charge states. We further employ a multi-fidelity approach that combines low-cost (semi-local exchange-correlation functional) reference data with high-quality (non-local hybrid functional) energies and forces that describe well the subtleties of the defect energy landscape. The resulting defect-capable force fields can find stable structural configurations and predict defect thermodynamics in quantitative agreement with direct quantum mechanical calculations, at a fraction of the computational cost.

content.title: Global defect charge embedding (charge-conditioned atom embeddings)

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | global_charge_embedding |
| name_full | Global defect charge embedding (charge-conditioned atom embeddings) |
| brief_description | A learnable embedding of the supercell total defect charge that is added to atomic species embeddings and read out as a geometry-independent energy term, enabling a single MLIP to distinguish multiple charge states of the same defect while propagating charge information through message-passing layers. |
| citation_title | here |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Single-host study: Sb2Se3 only (vacancies in Sb2Se3). |
| defect_types | Point vacancies (V_Sb(1), V_Se(1)); no dopants, defect complexes not modelled in experiments reported. |
| charge_state_handling | Explicit: total supercell charge treated as a categorical variable (five discrete classes) mapped to a 64-dimensional learnable embedding added to each atomic species embedding; also a geometry-independent embedding readout term (E_emb). Atomic forces computed from geometry-dependent interaction energy only (E_inter); electrostatic finite-size corrections applied separately when computing formation energies. |
| target_properties | Ground-state defect geometries (RMSD), total energies and forces, defect formation energies, thermodynamic transition levels (charge transition levels), configuration coordinate diagrams (CCDs) for carrier capture; reproduces PES topology across charge states. |
| representation_strategy_name | Charge-conditioned atom embeddings (global charge embedding added to per-atom embeddings) |
| representation_strategy_description | Total charge q_tot → learnable vector (64-D) added to atomic species embeddings at initialization and propagated through equivariant message-passing; embedding also read out directly to provide geometry-independent energy shift E_emb. This conditions both local interaction energies and global charge-dependent offsets. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full supercell representation (MLIP operates on entire supercell); latent-space differences to pristine reference were used for visualization (PCA of per-structure MACE feature vector differences vs pristine). Pristine bulk structures are included in training to provide host energy baseline. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Implemented within MACE: cutoff radius 5.5 Å; correlation order 3; spherical harmonics up to L=3; explicit species embeddings (one-hot → learned embeddings) augmented by charge embedding; ZBL pair repulsion included for short-range behavior. Charge embedding is categorical with 5 classes mapped to 64-D vectors. |
| graph_model_architecture | Integrated into MACE (equivariant many-body message-passing neural network, MACE v0.3.15); message-passing layers propagate charge-conditioned node features; architecture used 2 message-passing layers, 128 feature channels, hidden irreps as reported (128×0e ⊕ 128×1o ⊕ 128×2e ⊕ 128×3o). |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | No pretrained/foundation embeddings used to initialize the charge-embedded model; foundation MLIPs (bulk-trained) were benchmarked as baselines but not used to initialize the bespoke model. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Targeted defect dataset for V_Se(1) across five charge states with full relaxation trajectories (HSE06 reference). Training counts (per Table S1) total ~2.3k training structures across five charge states and ~570 test structures; pristine bulk relaxation trajectories (97 bulk structures) included. Data generated by DFT: hybrid HSE06 for joint model; PBE + HSE06 single-points for MF experiments. |
| transferability_evidence | Within-material transfer: strong — model reproduces HSE06 ground-states across five charge states for Sb2Se3 with RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å and transition levels within 0.015 eV; cross-material/generalization not tested. Foundation (bulk-trained) models trained on other data failed across charge states, showing domain gap — demonstrates the need for defect-specific training for transfer to defects. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Not quantified as learning curves for the charge-embedded model alone, but multi-fidelity experiments show that learning HSE corrections from ~10% high-fidelity single-points suffices to recover hybrid-level minima (MF approach described separately). The charge-embedded model achieved low RMSEs with the datasets reported (see performance metrics). |
| evaluation_protocol | Datasets filtered by trajectory-level and structure-level criteria; structures with short but physical bonds (1.5–2.0 Å) included only in training; remaining configs split 80/20 train/test with fixed random seed (100); trajectory outliers and force outliers removed; pristine bulk instances included in training. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Direct ablation: representation without global charge embedding showed overlapping latent clusters for different charge states (PCA), poor PES separation and incorrect ground-state identification. Comparison to explicit electrostatic/charge-equilibration models (QET, MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES) showed worse PES reproduction (Section S5). Inclusion of pristine bulk in training improves formation energy baseline. |
| performance_metrics | Test RMSE_E (energy per atom) average = 0.48 meV/atom; RMSE_F (forces) average = 20.15 meV/Å (Table S1 averages). Ground-state structural RMSD relative to HSE06 DFT ≤ 0.05 Å (well below 0.1 Å threshold). Thermodynamic transition levels predicted within 0.015 eV (max deviation ≤ 0.02 eV claimed). |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | No direct prediction of phonon scattering rates or lattice thermal conductivity in this work; authors state the MF surrogate could enable dense sampling needed for properties requiring many evaluations (e.g., finite-temperature free energies, luminescence lineshapes, defect dynamics), but no explicit BTE/phonon scattering or kappa degradation calculations are reported. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Authors argue global charge embeddings separate charge-specific PESs that local geometry descriptors alone cannot disambiguate, allowing similar local geometries to have different energy labels; embedding provides geometry-independent energy shifts plus propagated charge conditioning for interaction energies, enabling accurate modeling of charge-dependent reconstructions. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Limited to single supercell size used (3×1×1, 59-atom defects); no tests on defect complexes or dopants; generalization across materials not demonstrated; embedding treats total charge categorically (discrete classes used here) — continuous variation or mixed-charge systems not explored; electrostatic finite-size corrections were applied post hoc (not learned). |
| recommended_best_practices | Include defect configurations across relevant charge states in training; add global learnable charge conditioning to atom embeddings and a geometry-independent embedding readout; include pristine bulk trajectories for baseline energies; filter datasets conservatively (shortest bond-based filtering) and include high-distortion configurations in training only; combine multi-fidelity sampling (dense low-fidelity + sparse high-fidelity Δ-learning) to reduce high-cost data needs. |

| name_full | MACE equivariant many-body message-passing neural network (MACE v0.3.15) with defect extensions |
| brief_description | An equivariant many-body message-passing architecture used as the backbone MLIP; here augmented with global charge embeddings and multihead multi-fidelity readouts to model charged-defect PESs with high-order geometric features. |
| citation_title |  |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Sb2Se3 only in experiments reported. |
| defect_types | Point vacancies (V_Sb(1), V_Se(1)). |
| charge_state_handling | Handled via addition of global charge embedding into the MACE per-atom initialization and a separate embedding readout; forces derived from geometry-dependent part of MACE outputs. |
| target_properties | Total energies, atomic forces, defect structures, formation energies, thermodynamic transition levels, configuration coordinate diagrams. |
| representation_strategy_name | Equivariant message-passing with high-order geometric features (MACE) |
| representation_strategy_description | Many-body equivariant MPNN that forms node features and edge interactions using spherical harmonic expansions and higher-order correlations; here atomic embeddings are augmented with global charge embedding prior to message passing and a direct embedding readout contributes geometry-independent energy. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full-supercell representation; inclusion of pristine bulk structures in training provides host reference energy. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Cutoff 5.5 Å, correlation order 3, spherical harmonics up to L=3, hidden irreps given (128×0e ⊕ 128×1o ⊕ 128×2e ⊕ 128×3o), 2 message-passing layers, 128 feature channels; ZBL pair repulsion included. |

| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | Model trained from scratch on HSE06 defect + bulk data for bespoke model; foundation models (bulk-trained MACE variants) were benchmarked as baselines but not used to initialize the bespoke MACE. |

| transferability_evidence | Backbone MACE without charge embedding failed to identify defects; MACE with charge embedding succeeded on Sb2Se3; no cross-material transfer tests of MACE-based defect model reported. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Described hyperparameters and training strategy (loss weighting changes, SWA). No explicit learning curves reported for varying dataset size for MACE backbone alone. |
| evaluation_protocol | Training details: batch size 4 for joint charge model, 2 message-passing layers, SWA activated late in training; data splits and filtering described (80/20 train/test, seed 100). |
| baselines_and_ablations | Ablation of charge embedding (MACE without charge conditioning) shows overlapping latent descriptors and fails to separate charge states; comparisons to charge-equilibration variants (MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES) reported worse PES reproduction. |
| performance_metrics | See charge-embedding entry: RMSE_E ~0.48 meV/atom, RMSE_F ~20.15 meV/Å; ground-state RMSD ≤ 0.05 Å when MACE has charge embedding. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | No direct phonon/thermal transport outputs; MACE surrogate noted as enabling dense PES sampling which could indirectly be used for properties requiring many energy/force evaluations. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Equivariant, many-body features in MACE capture subtle geometry-dependent forces; coupling them with global charge conditioning enables the network to learn charge-dependent interaction energies and geometry-independent charge shifts. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Without charge conditioning and defect-data coverage, MACE reproduces flatter PES and misidentifies minima; performance depends on dataset quality and inclusion of defect trajectories. |
| recommended_best_practices | Use equivariant many-body MPNNs (e.g., MACE) with sufficient angular resolution and include ZBL short-range repulsion; augment atom embeddings with global charge conditioning for charged-defect problems; include bulk trajectories for baseline energies. |

content.title: Multi-fidelity delta-learning with shared latent representation and separate fidelity heads (PBE → HSE06 Δ-learning)

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | multi_fidelity_delta_learning |
| name_full | Multi-fidelity delta-learning with shared latent representation and separate fidelity heads (PBE → HSE06 Δ-learning) |
| brief_description | A joint training approach where the model learns a shared latent representation from dense low-fidelity (PBE) data and a sparse set (~10%) of high-fidelity (HSE06) single-point corrections via separate readout heads, enabling recovery of hybrid-level PES behaviour at much lower computational cost. |
| citation_title | here |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Sb2Se3 only (neutral and charged vacancy PESs explored with MF model). |
| defect_types | Point vacancies (neutral and charged V_Se(1) example used to demonstrate MF benefits). |
| charge_state_handling | Global charge embedding as in joint model; MF uses same charge-conditioned shared latent features with separate PBE and HSE06 output heads. |
| target_properties | High-fidelity PES surrogate (HSE06-level energies/forces), identification of global minima, configuration coordinate diagrams, defect formation energies after corrections. |
| representation_strategy_name | Multi-fidelity shared-latent Δ-learning (multihead readouts) |
| representation_strategy_description | Single shared MACE latent representation trained on dense PBE relaxations; a sparse subset (~10%) of HSE06 single-point labels is used to train a high-fidelity readout head to learn Δ(HSE06 − PBE) corrections; separate loss heads for each fidelity. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full-supercell representation; HSE06 single-points sampled from PBE-relaxed geometries (stratified sampling), initial and final configs always included. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Shared latent uses same MACE descriptor settings (cutoff 5.5 Å, correlation order 3, spherical harmonics up to L=3). |
| graph_model_architecture | Shared MACE backbone with two separate output heads (PBE and HSE06). |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | No external pretraining; the MF scheme leverages dense PBE data (low-fidelity) as de-facto pretraining with sparse HSE labels to correct to hybrid level. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Dense PBE relaxation trajectories for many initial distortions; ~10% of PBE-relaxed structures sampled uniformly for HSE06 single-point calculations (initial + final configs always included; effective HF fraction slightly <10% after deduplication). |
| transferability_evidence | MF model discovered an HSE06 global minimum (0.02 eV lower) missed by coarse HSE Γ-point sampling; subsequent converged HSE06 DFT confirmed ML-predicted minimum within 8 meV. This demonstrates MF can correct functional-dependent PES differences in the same material; cross-material transfer not assessed. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | High-fidelity labels reduced to ~10% of structures while recovering HSE06-level minima and CCDs; authors claim ~3 orders of magnitude reduction in computational cost for comprehensive PES exploration (Section S6.3). |
| evaluation_protocol | PBE relaxations with converged k-point sampling used for LF dataset; HF dataset comprised stratified HSE06 single-points on sampled PBE structures; training uses multihead loss with separate optimizations for low and high fidelity outputs. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Compared to standard coarse HF search (HSE06 Γ-point sampling) which missed the true HF global minimum; MF approach found the lower minimum and reproduced HSE CCDs at negligible inference cost. |
| performance_metrics | MF-predicted HSE global minimum reproduced by fully converged HSE06 DFT within 8 meV. MF recovered a global minimum 0.02 eV lower than coarse HSE Γ sampling which had found only a metastable minimum. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | No direct phonon/thermal transport predictions; MF surrogate enables dense sampling needed for properties that require many PES evaluations (authors suggest extensions), but no explicit phonon scattering/kappa calculations presented. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Learning Δ(HF−LF) on a shared latent allows the model to capture functional-dependent stabilization of PES basins that LF sampling alone misses, enabling accurate HF-level PES reconstruction from mostly LF data. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | MF relies on representative PBE sampling that overlaps HF basins; if LF PES misses an HF basin entirely, MF corrections may not find it unless sampling covers it; stratified sampling choices and supercell/fidelity mismatches can limit effectiveness. |
| recommended_best_practices | Use dense LF (PBE) exploration plus stratified sampling of HF (HSE06) single-points (~10% of structures including trajectory endpoints) to learn Δ corrections; include initial/final configs from trajectories; validate MF minima with converged HF calculations when possible. |

| brief_description | Large-scale foundation MLIPs trained mainly on pristine/closed-shell bulk data used as baselines; shown here to systematically fail at predicting charged-defect PESs and ground-state reconstructions due to domain gap and absence of explicit charge-state descriptors. |
| citation_title |  |

| material_systems | Benchmarked on Sb2Se3 defects in this work; foundation potentials themselves were trained on broad bulk/materials datasets (external). |
| defect_types | Benchmarked here on point vacancies in Sb2Se3 across multiple charge states; original foundation models primarily trained on pristine bulk structures (no explicit defects). |
| charge_state_handling | Typically charge-agnostic (no explicit total-charge conditioning) — some charge-aware foundation variants exist (see separate entity) but the ones benchmarked here are charge-agnostic. |
| target_properties | Designed for bulk energies/forces; here evaluated for defect ground-state geometries and PESs and found to predict flatter PESs and yield RMSD typically 0.2–0.4 Å vs DFT for defect minima. |
| representation_strategy_name | Bulk-trained atom-centered local descriptors within foundation MLIPs (varied architectures) |
| representation_strategy_description | Local atom-centered descriptors learned from large bulk datasets, locality assumed with truncated cutoffs; do not include explicit total-charge conditioning or defect-specific training data. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Operate on full supercell but trained predominantly on pristine/bulk local environments; therefore treat defects effectively as steric voids absent of defect-electronic effects. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Varies by model (MACE/GN-type architectures, OMAT descriptors for some); not augmented with defect charge features in baseline tests. |
| graph_model_architecture | Various foundation architectures benchmarked: MACE-MH-1, MACE-MPA-0, GRACE-2L-OMAT, MatterSim v1 5M — models include equivariant architectures and other graph neural-network variants trained on bulk data. |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | These are foundation pre-trained potentials (trained on large bulk datasets); in this paper they are used as baselines (benchmarked) rather than as featurization sources for the bespoke defect model. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Foundation models trained on large-scale bulk datasets (references cited); in this work, these models were applied out-of-distribution to Sb2Se3 defect configurations generated by SHAKENBREAK and DFT relaxations. |
| transferability_evidence | Tested on Sb2Se3 charged vacancy PESs — none consistently identified DFT ground states across all charge states; RMSD generally 0.2–0.4 Å. Coincidental success in single charge states attributed to error cancellation and not transferable. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Not designed for defect data; no few-shot defect adaptation reported here. Authors note severe data-domain gap making foundation models unreliable for defects without targeted defect data or charge conditioning. |
| evaluation_protocol | Same set of initial bond-distorted configurations (SHAKENBREAK) and DFT references used for fair comparison; models relaxed same initial configurations and resulting RMSDs compared to DFT-PBE references. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Baseline comparisons demonstrate that adding charge-conditioned or defect-training data is necessary; foundation models without these fail. Charge-aware foundation variants were also tested and failed if lacking defect training data. |
| performance_metrics | Typical structural RMSD of foundation models vs DFT for V_Sb(1) across charge states: ~0.2–0.4 Å (exceeding 0.1 Å success threshold). PESs predicted too flat; incorrect forces indicated. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | None reported; foundation models not applied to phonon or thermal transport for defects in this study. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Failures attributed to (i) domain gap: training data lacking electronically active, symmetry-broken defect environments; (ii) lack of explicit charge descriptors, causing collapse of charge-dependent PESs into one landscape. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Do not generalize to charged defects or neutral defects that undergo charge-driven reconstructions; accidental agreement in one charge state is non-transferable; cannot distinguish charge-induced energy shifts. |
| recommended_best_practices | Do not use bulk-trained foundation MLIPs for charged-defect structure searches without retraining/finetuning on defect data and/or adding explicit charge conditioning. |

| target_properties | Intended for energies/forces including electrostatics-sensitive configurations; here discussed for possible modeling of charged defects but noted challenges. |
| representation_strategy_name | Charge-equilibration / polarizable electrostatics / learned long-range descriptors |
| representation_strategy_description | Predict environment-dependent atomic electronegativities/hardnesses or atomic charges and include long-range electrostatic interactions or polarizability; alternatively learn explicit long-range descriptors to capture non-local interactions. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Generally full-supercell; these schemes distribute total charge among atoms and so inherently use global constraints. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Varies by implementation (QET predicts electronegativities and hardnesses; polarizable models include induced dipoles; learned long-range descriptors augment local descriptors with long-range terms). |
| graph_model_architecture | Implemented in various architectures (QET-TensorNet, MACE-POLAR, MACE-LES referenced); some are equivariant GNNs augmented with charge equilibration layers. |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | Some foundation charge-aware models (e.g., MACE-POLAR-1-L, QET-PES-MatQ) were pre-trained on existing datasets (OMol25, MatQ) and benchmarked here. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Typically trained on molecular and periodic datasets with charges; mentioned literature contexts include liquids, molecular crystals, and interfaces (not specifically defect-rich datasets). |
| transferability_evidence | Authors report that applying such approaches to charged defects in periodic supercells can suffer from ill-defined atomic charge partitioning, unphysical delocalization into the bulk, or computational scaling issues; in benchmarks here, MACE-POLAR-1-L and QET-PES-MatQ satisfied global charge but still failed to reproduce DFT defect ground states when training data lacked defect configurations. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Not quantified here; authors report that charge-equilibration methods have known difficulties for charged periodic defects and do not substitute for defect-specific training data. |
| evaluation_protocol | Charge-aware foundation models (MACE-POLAR-1-L, QET-PES-MatQ) were bench-marked on same Sb vacancy PESs; atomic charges summed to imposed total charge but structural predictions remained inaccurate. |
| baselines_and_ablations | Comparison showed that explicit atomic-charge modelling (MACE-POLAR, QET) did not by itself fix defect prediction failures — lack of defect training data remained limiting factor. |
| performance_metrics | Reported RMSD for neutral V_Sb(1): MACE-POLAR-1-L RMSD = 0.29 Å; QET-PES-MatQ RMSD = 0.33 Å. For q = -3: 0.32 Å and 0.22 Å respectively (all >0.1 Å). |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | No link reported; these electrostatic-aware representations are discussed only for energies/forces and charge distribution modeling. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | While these methods explicitly model charge redistribution and long-range electrostatics, authors caution about ill-defined atomic charge partitioning in periodic charged systems and possible unphysical delocalization, making global charge conditioning a simpler and effective alternative for defect charge-state discrimination. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Ill-defined atomic charge partitioning in periodic systems; potential for unphysical charge delocalization into bulk; non-linear scaling (e.g., Ewald) and computational overhead; when trained on datasets lacking defect-specific environments, these methods still fail to reproduce defect PESs accurately. |
| recommended_best_practices | If using charge-equilibration/polarizable schemes for charged defects, ensure training data includes charged defect configurations and verify against hybrid/HF references; consider global charge conditioning as simpler alternative combined with defect data. |

metadata.title: Machine-learning structural reconstructions for accelerated point defect calculations

tldr.text: A machine-learning surrogate model is harnessed to qualitatively explore the structural landscape of neutral point defects and predicts favourable reconstructions for unseen defects in unseen compositions for 90% of cases, thereby reducing the number of first-principles calculations by 73%.

metadata.abstract: Defects dictate the properties of many functional materials. To understand the behaviour of defects and their impact on physical properties, it is necessary to identify the most stable defect geometries. However, global structure searching is computationally challenging for high-throughput defect studies or materials with complex defect landscapes, like alloys or disordered solids. Here, we tackle this limitation by harnessing a machine-learning surrogate model to qualitatively explore the structural landscape of neutral point defects. By learning defect motifs in a family of related metal chalcogenide and mixed anion crystals, the model successfully predicts favourable reconstructions for unseen defects in unseen compositions for 90% of cases, thereby reducing the number of first-principles calculations by 73%. Using CdSe_ x Te_1− x alloys as an exemplar, we train a model on the end member compositions and apply it to find the stable geometries of all inequivalent vacancies for a range of mixing concentrations, thus enabling more accurate and faster defect studies for configurationally complex systems.

content.title: M3GNet universal graph machine-learning force field (fine-tuned on defect configurations)

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | M3GNet-MLFF (fine-tuned) |
| name_full | M3GNet universal graph machine-learning force field (fine-tuned on defect configurations) |
| brief_description | A universal graph-based machine-learning interatomic potential (M3GNet) pre-trained on bulk crystal data and fine-tuned here on a curated defect dataset to serve as a surrogate PES for rapid defect geometry exploration and structure searching. |
| citation_title | A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Applied to neutral cation vacancies in a diverse set of metal chalcogenides/ mixed chalcogen/halide hosts (50 hosts total) and to CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} pseudo-binary alloys; multiple hosts and alloys evaluated. |
| defect_types | Neutral point defects — specifically neutral cation vacancies (V_cation^0). No charged defects, interstitials, substitutional dopants, antisites, Frenkel pairs or explicit complexes were modeled in experiments (defect complexes not included). |
| charge_state_handling | Neutral-only in experiments (authors explicitly state universal MLFFs limited in describing charge); charge states not modeled. Paper discusses possible encodings: net charge as graph global attribute and use of 4th-generation MLFFs with explicit atomic charges, but these were not used here. |
| target_properties | Qualitative potential energy surface (PES) mapping: predicted relaxed geometries (local minima), relative energies of defect configurations (energy ordering), used to select candidates for DFT relaxation; indirectly accelerates calculations of formation energies once ground-state geometries are found. The work did not compute charge transition levels, migration barriers, or phonon thermal conductivity directly with the MLFF as final predictions (but discusses possible future applications). |
| representation_strategy_name | Defect-fine-tuned universal graph MLFF (M3GNet) with weighted-atom readout |
| representation_strategy_description | Graph constructed from the full supercell (periodic) using M3GNet graph featurisation: nodes = atoms with elemental embeddings from pretraining, edges encode radial (pair) and explicit 3-body information within cutoffs; model uses radial and 3-body cutoffs of 5 Å and 4 Å respectively and a weighted atom readout function. Model outputs energies, forces and stresses and is trained with a combined loss on energy/force/stress (weights 1/1/0.1). |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Full supercell graph representation (universal MLFF) fine-tuned on defect-containing supercells — not a reduced defect-only subgraph; however SOAP descriptors (see another entity) were computed only for the defect site to identify distinct minima. |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Graph cutoffs: radial cutoff 5 Å; 3-body cutoff 4 Å. Species encoded implicitly in node features initialized from the pre-trained bulk model (atomic/effective embeddings from M3GNet pretraining). Readout: weighted atom readout. Training loss: MSE on energies and forces (weights 1,1) and stresses (weight 0.1). |
| graph_model_architecture | M3GNet (universal graph deep learning interatomic potential). The paper also benchmarks architectures (CHGNet, MACE) during model selection but selects M3GNet. Key settings used: radial cutoff = 5 Å, 3-body cutoff = 4 Å, weighted atom readout, batch size 4, exponential LR scheduler (initial 5e-4). |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | Yes — model initialized from pre-trained M3GNet bulk model weights (trained on Materials Project bulk/formation-energy data); transfer learning/fine-tuning strategy used (bulk -> defect). The Materials Project/bulk pretraining provided embeddings and chemistry knowledge (e.g., Se–Te bonds) that improved generalisation to mixed alloys. |
| data_regime_and_dataset | First-principles (DFT HSE06) dataset created by authors: 132 neutral cation vacancies across 50 host compositions (25 elements, 6 space groups). After cleaning and frame selection: training = 11,955 configurations (63%), validation = 2,100 (11%), test = 4,830 (26%). For the alloy application a custom training set: ~1,420 frames (trained on CdTe and CdSe end-members) and validation ~140 frames; test on mixed CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} compositions. |
| transferability_evidence | Quantified: on a robust test set (13 unseen compositions, 32 defects) the fine-tuned M3GNet surrogate + DFT workflow correctly identified the DFT ground state in 88% of test defects and reduced required DFT calculations by 73% (acceleration factor ≈13). For the chalcohalide family (more chemically similar systems) the model identified the correct ground state for all test cases (100%). For CdSe_x_Te_{1-x} alloys: training on end-members and testing on mixed alloys resulted in correct ground-state identification for all defects and found more favourable ground states for 70% of defects (mean energy lowering −0.4 eV). |
| data_efficiency_evidence | Model trained with ~12k configurations (fine-tuned from pre-trained bulk weights) — authors show fine-tuning is effective and that including bulk structures with defects improves performance vs defect-only training. They compared sampling strategies (MS: 10 evenly spaced frames per relaxation vs DIRECT) and found MS performed better at similar dataset sizes; DIRECT only wins when its dataset is larger. Model training time: 30 epochs (~5.3 hours) for full dataset; alloy model trained for 80 epochs. The surrogate approach reduced the number of expensive DFT relaxations by 73% in structure searching. |
| evaluation_protocol | Composition-wise split: dataset split by composition into training (68% of defects/compositions), validation (5%) and test (27%) to evaluate out-of-distribution generalisation to unseen compositions; validation augmented with 5% of configurations from training systems. For alloys they trained on end-members and tested on mixed (out-of-sample) compositions; also a family-specific split for chalcohalides was tested. Spearman correlations computed per-defect and averaged. SOAP-based clustering / t-SNE used for manifold visualisation (M3GNet embeddings). |
| baselines_and_ablations | Benchmarks: compared model architectures (M3GNet, CHGNet, MACE), training on defect-only vs defect+bulk (defect+bulk improved performance), and sampling strategies (MS vs DIRECT). Ablation outcomes: defect+bulk training improved errors; MS sampling (evenly spaced frames) outperformed DIRECT for similar dataset sizes; pretraining (bulk -> defect) yielded transfer benefits (enabled detection of Te–Se bonds not present in defect training but present in bulk pretraining). Details in SI. |
| performance_metrics | Energy prediction metrics: MAE_absolute_energy (test) = 31.2 meV/atom; MAE_relative_energy (test, energies relative to defect ground state) = 11.3 meV/atom; for configurations <≈5 eV above minimum: MAE = 3.6 meV/atom (≈0.29 eV for an 80-atom supercell). Spearman rank correlation (ρ) on test set averaged across defects = 0.72. Structure-search success: MLFF+DFT identified correct DFT ground state in 88% of test defects; accelerated structure searching by factor ≈13; reduced DFT relaxations by 73%. For alloy application: found better ground states in 70% of defects with mean lowering −0.4 eV. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | Paper does not compute phonon scattering or lattice thermal conductivity degradation directly. It cites related work showing MLFFs can be used for phonon properties and defect phonon studies (e.g., Shimizu et al.) and suggests the surrogate approach could enable calculation of defect formation entropies and accelerate migration/phonon studies, but provides no direct ML prediction of scattering rates or kappa degradation. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | Authors argue that learning plausible defect reconstruction motifs (e.g., anion–anion dimerisation) across related chemistries is sufficient to qualitatively capture low-energy regions of defect PESs; pretraining on bulk databases encodes general chemical motifs (e.g., Se–Te bonding) that aid transfer to unseen local environments; graph-based universal MLFFs capture local bonding and many-body interactions needed to predict structural reconstructions; SOAP defect-site fingerprints effectively distinguish distinct local minima. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | Model limited to neutral cation vacancies in metal chalcogenides (no charged defects). Performance drops for out-of-distribution chemistries (ρ lower than bulk-only MLFFs) and for hosts with very complex PESs (e.g., V_Sn in Li4SnS4) — ~12% of test defects where MLFF ground state differed from DFT; errors for absolute energies sizeable though relative energy errors are smaller. MLFF cannot describe net charge transfer/charged states in current setup; sensitivity to sampling strategy (DIRECT biased to high-distortion frames) and to training data composition; SOAP/MLFF based identification may miss basins if training biased. |
| recommended_best_practices | Use a pretrained universal MLFF (bulk-trained) and fine-tune on defect configurations (include bulk frames to improve stability); sample ionic relaxation trajectories with evenly spaced frames (MS) for small training budgets; use SOAP fingerprints of the defect site (r=5 Å, n_max=10, l_max=10, σ=1.0 Å used here) to cluster/identify unique minima; split dataset by composition to assess cross-chemistry transfer; for alloys train on end members if possible and apply to mixed compositions; when addressing charge states either train separate MLFFs per charge state, encode net charge as a global graph attribute, or use 4th-generation MLFFs with explicit atomic charges; after MLFF-driven search refine chosen candidates with higher-accuracy DFT (tighter thresholds, SOC where needed). |

content.title: Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) descriptor computed for the defect site

content.text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| name_short | SOAP (defect-site) |
| name_full | Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) descriptor computed for the defect site |
| brief_description | A local rotationally- and translationally-invariant density-based descriptor computed on the defect neighbourhood used to fingerprint/cluster MLFF-relaxed structures and to identify distinct local minima of the defect PES. |
| citation_title | On representing chemical environments |
| mention_or_use | use |
| material_systems | Applied to the same set of defect-containing supercells (metal chalcogenides and alloys) to characterise local defect motifs. |
| defect_types | Used for neutral point defect configurations (cation vacancies) to fingerprint local minima; not used for charged defects or complexes here. |
| charge_state_handling | SOAP itself is geometry-based and charge-agnostic; no explicit charge features were included in SOAP fingerprints in this study. |
| target_properties | Used to identify and cluster distinct local minima of defect relaxation trajectories (helps select unique candidate structures for DFT refinement) — not used to directly predict scalar properties like energy or transition levels (although used in combination with MLFF energies to find minima). |
| representation_strategy_name | Defect-site SOAP fingerprint |
| representation_strategy_description | SOAP computed on the local neighbourhood centred on the defect site (local cutoff r = 5 Å), expanded in radial basis and spherical harmonics (n_max = 10, l_max = 10) with Gaussian smearing σ = 1.0 Å; cosine distance between SOAP vectors used to group minima. |
| defect_centering_or_reference | Defect-centered: SOAP computed for the defect site/local neighbourhood only (not full-cell SOAP). |
| local_environment_descriptor_details | Parameters reported: local cutoff r = 5 Å; n_max = 10 radial basis functions; l_max = 10 spherical harmonics; σ = 1.0 Å Gaussian smearing. Species included implicitly via atomic densities in SOAP expansion (standard SOAP, species-aware). Descriptor is invariant to rotations/translations and permutation of expansion coefficients handled by SOAP kernel/cosine distance. |
| graph_model_architecture | None |
| pretraining_or_foundation_embeddings | None |
| data_regime_and_dataset | Applied to the MLFF-relaxed structures from the DFT-generated dataset (tens of thousands of configurations), used to identify unique minima for each defect trajectory. |
| transferability_evidence | SOAP successfully discriminated minima across diverse hosts and was robust enough to identify different motifs (e.g., dimers vs non-dimer states) across compositions; used to select unique MLFF minima for DFT relaxation in the test set. |
| data_efficiency_evidence | SOAP-based clustering helped reduce the number of DFT relaxations by selecting unique candidates, contributing to the reported 73% reduction in DFT calculations when using MLFF+SOAP selection vs a full DFT-only search. |
| evaluation_protocol | Cosine distance between SOAP vectors of the defect site used to identify distinct minima; thresholding/clustering details in SI (SOAP parameters as above). |
| baselines_and_ablations | Authors report SOAP of defect site was more robust than energy- or RMSD-based grouping: energy-based grouping can miss minima with similar energies; RMSD sensitive to changes far from defect. SOAP chosen as the preferred fingerprint for motif identification. |
| performance_metrics | Not reported as a predictive metric; used qualitatively to identify distinct minima. Its use contributed to success rates (88% correct ground-state identification) by enabling selection of representative distinct MLFF minima for DFT refinement. |
| phonon_or_thermal_transport_link | SOAP is geometric and not by itself predictive of phonon scattering; authors do not use SOAP outputs for phonon/thermal transport tasks here. |
| interpretation_or_mechanistic_claims | SOAP of defect site captures local bonding rearrangements (e.g., anion–anion dimer formation) and is therefore effective to distinguish reconstruction motifs which are the key structural feature controlling defect energetics. |
| failure_modes_and_limitations | SOAP depends on chosen cutoff and expansion parameters; may not capture long-range strain/electrostatic differences; can fail if two minima have very similar local atomic densities but different long-range relaxations. |
| recommended_best_practices | Compute SOAP centred on defect site with r ≈ 5 Å for typical point-defect supercells; use relatively high n_max and l_max (authors used 10/10) and σ ≈ 1.0 Å; use SOAP cosine-distance clustering to select a small set of distinct candidate minima for high-accuracy DFT refinement rather than energy/RMSD thresholds. |
